issue.title: [Bugfix][Mamba] Honor --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype for the shared KDA layers

labels.name: repo-5faa5e07
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: repo-5faa5e07
labels.description: ONLY add when PR is ready to merge/full CI is needed

issue.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype` never reaches the KDA recurrent state of the models built on the shared KDA layers under `vllm/model_executor`, and on Kimi-Linear asking for `bfloat16` crashes the engine at startup. The affected code is platform-independent; only the Kimi-K3 specialized decode guard is ROCm-specific. This passes the flag at the five call sites that still drop it. Follow-up to #55364, which added the argument and plumbed it through `vllm/models/{kimi_k3,glm5next}` only.

## Claims

- Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct starts with `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16` instead of failing on `assert self.page_size_padded >= page_size`, and allocates a BF16 recurrent state: KV cache capacity +88% (dummy weights, `max_model_len=2048`) / +48% (real weights, `max_model_len=8192`).
- GSM8K is unchanged: 0.899 on `main` (`auto`), 0.898 with this PR (`auto`), 0.899 with this PR (`bfloat16`).
- The default (`auto`, FP32 recurrent state) is unchanged: identical state dtypes, page size and KV cache size.
- `BailingMoeV3ForCausalLM` / `AliceAIForCausalLM` and the Kimi-K3 AMD specialized decode guard now see the configured dtype too.

## Validation

1x MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 10.0, torch 2.13.0+rocm10.0.0, AITER 0.1.28.post1. The nightly wheel `0.33.0rc1.dev1104+g166c03874` (`main` @ 166c03874) with this branch's `vllm/` and `tests/` over it. The touched files and the code they depend on are unchanged between that commit and this PR's base; the unit test was rerun on the rebased branch with the same result.

**Unit test.** `pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_state_dtype.py`: 12 passed. On the base (every changed `vllm/` file from `main`, new test kept): 4 failed, 8 passed, i.e. every `bfloat16` case.

**Startup reproducer.** `LLM(Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct, load_format="dummy", max_model_len=2048, gpu_memory_utilization=0.85, mamba_ssm_cache_dtype=...)`, report the allocated `MambaSpec`s, then `generate`. 20 KDA layers in 3 groups (7 + 7 + 6).

| Arm | `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype` | Runs | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | `auto` | 1 | OK, `(bf16, fp32)`, page 2,211,840 B, 2,642,176 KV tokens |
| This PR | `auto` | 1 | identical to `main` |
| `main` | `bfloat16` | 2 | **startup crash**: `kv_cache_interface.py:1164 assert self.page_size_padded >= page_size` |
| This PR | `bfloat16` | 2 | OK, `(bf16, bf16)`, page 1,179,648 B, 4,970,240 KV tokens, `generate` OK |

**Accuracy.** Real weights, `vllm serve ... --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85`, `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5` (greedy):

| Arm | `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype` | KV cache (tokens) | GSM8K |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | `auto` | 7,380,992 | 0.899 |
| This PR | `auto` | 7,380,992 | 0.898 |
| This PR | `bfloat16` | 10,923,446 | 0.899 |

**Kernel.** The Kimi layer writes the FP32 final state through `scatter_states()`. `tests/kernels/mamba/test_gather_scatter_states.py` skips on non-CUDA platforms, so its scatter cases (including BF16 pool / FP32 source) were rerun on MI355X with the Kimi-Linear state row shape (32×128×128), batch 1/3/64/256: all bit-exact against `pool[idx] = src.to(pool.dtype)`.

`ruff check` / `ruff format --check`: clean.

CI: the new test is CPU-only (no GPU work, builds layers with `__new__`) and runs in the Kimi K3 jobs (B200 and MI355), which collect `tests/models/kimi_k3/`.

Not validated:
- **BailingMoeV3 / Ling and Alice AI end to end:** no checkpoint was available. Covered by the unit test only. The Bailing write-back cast is a no-op when the dtypes match.
- **Kimi-K3 specialized decode with a BF16 state:** only the guard's input changed. It now reports the BF16 layout as unsupported instead of claiming the supported `(bf16, fp32)` one.

## Details

**Root cause.** `MambaStateDtypeCalculator.kda_state_dtype()` takes `mamba_ssm_cache_dtype` since #55364, but these call sites still use the two-argument form, so they always return an FP32 recurrent state:

- `KimiGatedDeltaNetAttention.get_state_dtype()`
- `AliceAIForCausalLM.get_mamba_state_dtype_from_config()`
- `BailingMoeV3KimiDeltaAttention.get_state_dtype()` and `BailingMoeV3ForCausalLM.get_mamba_state_dtype_from_config()`
- the Kimi-K3 AMD specialized decode support guard

Kimi-Linear resolves to `kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py::KimiLinearForCausalLM` on CUDA and to `kimi_k3/amd/linear.py::KimiLinearForCausalLM` on ROCm and XPU. Both model-level classmethods pass the flag, while both build their KDA layers from the shared `KimiGatedDeltaNetAttention`, which does not. `Platform._align_hybrid_block_size()` (base class, all platforms) sizes the padded mamba page from the model-level dtype (BF16), the layers allocate with the layer-level dtype (FP32), and the page overflows.

**Write-back.** The KDA kernels return an FP32 final state. `BailingMoeV3KimiDeltaAttention` stores it with index assignment, which requires matching dtypes, so it is cast to the cache dtype. `KimiGatedDeltaNetAttention` stores it with `scatter_states()`, whose Triton store already converts (verified above), so it needs no change there.

The new test mirrors `tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_state_dtype.py`, which covers the same bug fixed for GLM-5.3-Flash.

Both model-level classmethods pass the flag, while both build their KDA layers from the shared `KimiGatedDeltaNetAttention`, which does not. `Platform._align_hybrid_block_size()` (base class, all platforms) sizes the padded mamba page from the model-level dtype (BF16), the layers allocate with the layer-level dtype (FP32), and the page overflows.

**Write-back.** The KDA kernels return an FP32 final state. `BailingMoeV3KimiDeltaAttention` stores it with index assignment, which requires matching dtypes, so it is cast to the cache dtype. `KimiGatedDeltaNetAttention` stores it with `scatter_states()`, whose Triton store already converts (verified above), so it needs no change there.

The new test mirrors `tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_state_dtype.py`, which covers the same bug fixed for GLM-5.3-Flash.

issue.title: feat(forge-loop): keep lane candidates the tree moved past as planning evidence
issue.body:
## What this is for

A queued lane candidate whose diff no longer applies after a sibling's KEEP is dropped, and nothing is kept: not its diff, not its plan's link to it, and not the lesson its session had already recorded, which is written only when a candidate is measured. Later rounds can neither read what that session found nor take its change up again. This change files each such candidate where later planners already look, and keeps it out of everything that treats candidates as measured.

## Evidence: the four sessions of the #2281 A/B

- 8 of about 55 lane candidates were dropped this way. Every one of the 8 had a lesson recorded, and every lesson was discarded.
- 7 of the 8 lessons report a correctness-passing change faster in the lane's own runs: 46.7 → 28.6 µs on the 13-case mean (a new LDS-staged kernel for M ≥ 512), 46.2 → 42.8 µs (small-M split-K), about 12% on m_512, about 7% on m_2048, 3.4%, 1.5–5% on large-M cases, and 1.5–2%. These are the lanes' own numbers, never measured canonically.
- The first of those, `always-r2` round 1 lane 2, was the direction three rounds later re-planned at the critic's insistence and kept at iteration 4 for +14.4%, the session's largest step.
- Planners already read archived candidates by path: 24 of the 139 plan and critic documents in these sessions cite `candidates/iter_NNN`, for example to port a GEMV route from an earlier candidate. A dropped candidate never appears there.
- Why they were dropped: in every case whose edits could be replayed from the transcript, the conflicting hunks fall in code all lanes route through, the per-M config tables and the launcher builders. Four replays reproduced the loop's `git apply --3way` failure.

## Description

- `campaign/unmeasured_lanes.py` (new): `UnmeasuredLaneArchive.record` files one candidate under `unmeasured_lanes/round_NNN_lane_K/` with `change.diff`, `plan.md`, `lesson.md` (when the session recorded one) and `meta.json`, and appends a row to `unmeasured_lanes/index.jsonl`. `meta.json` names the base commit, the iteration that dropped the candidate, the canonical commit it no longer applied to, the plan's summary line, and `lesson_reason` when there is no lesson. The directory is staged and renamed into place, a candidate already filed is not filed again (a resumed process drops it a second time), and a store that cannot be written logs a warning and costs only the record.
- `campaign/experiments_layout.py`: the `unmeasured_lanes` paths.
- `iteration/fanout.py`: `LaneResult` carries `round_iteration` and `base_commit` through the lane queue; a queue written before this change restores with neither.
- `iteration/lane_runtime.py`: `_fill_lane_queue` stamps both. `_take_lane_candidate(iteration)` files a candidate that no longer applies and logs `lane_candidate_unmeasured`. A candidate rejected for changing the measurement surface or the driver is logged as `lane_candidate_rejected` and not filed, since it is no evidence for a later round. `locked_run.py` passes the iteration.
- `roles/analysis_evidence.py`: every planning context cites `unmeasured_lanes/index.jsonl` as `unmeasured_lane_candidates` once it exists. The citation says the numbers in a record are the lane's own, not canonical measurements. The kind is superseded like the other run-level refs when a context is carried forward.
- `roles/prompt_view.py`: the Implementer's retrieval map names `unmeasured_lanes/round_NNN_lane_K/` once the index exists, so a plan that says to port one can be carried out. The optional entries of the map are passed as `OptionalRecords(handoffs=..., unmeasured_lanes=...)`, which replaces the `include_handoffs` flag.
- The candidate archive, merge stacking, the history digest, export and the knowledge base are unchanged and never see these candidates.
- `docs/kernelforge/forge_long_horizon_state.md`: the store, its events, and where it is cited.

- Linked issue(s): none.
- Tests:
  - New `campaign/test_unmeasured_lanes.py`: a filed candidate keeps its diff, plan, lesson and `meta.json`, with one index row and no staging left behind; a candidate without a lesson records why; filing the same candidate twice keeps the first; a store that cannot be written returns nothing.
  - `iteration/test_lane_rounds.py`: a candidate the tree moved past is filed with its round, base commit, dropping iteration and canonical commit, and logged; a candidate that edits the driver is logged as rejected and not filed; a fan-out round stamps its iteration and base commit on every queued candidate. Call sites pass the iteration to `_take_lane_candidate`.
  - `iteration/test_fanout.py`: the round and base commit round-trip through the queue, and an older queue entry restores without them.
  - `iteration/test_planning_context.py`: the planning context cites the store only once it has an entry, with a summary saying its numbers are not canonical.
  - `campaign/test_long_horizon_state.py`: the retrieval map names the store only once it has an entry; the handoff test uses `OptionalRecords`.
  - Run: `pytest -n 8 src/kernelforge/tests`: 6400 passed, 8 skipped, 4 failed. Three fail the same way on `main` in this environment (`config/test_rocpc_profile_discovery.py` ×2 and `test_assembly_aiter_moe_gpu.py::test_aiter_w4a16_roundtrip_rejects_wrong_silu_and_rebinds_arguments`). `rewrite_controller/test_opportunity_agent.py::test_hookless_resume_republication_clears_a_corrected_refusal` is flaky on `main` as well. `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean, `check_broad_suppress.py` clean, `lint-imports` 14 contracts kept, code-metrics gate run locally against `main`: PASSED.
- Size/complexity triggers crossed: none.
- If this simplifies or refactors: no mechanism removed. `render_long_horizon_header`'s `include_handoffs` flag became `OptionalRecords.handoffs`; its only caller and its test moved with it.
- Observable effect: a dropped lane candidate prints `candidate no longer applies; dropped unmeasured; filed under <dir>`. It leaves `forge_experiments/unmeasured_lanes/round_NNN_lane_K/` and a `lane_candidate_unmeasured` event, and later planning contexts list `unmeasured_lane_candidates` among their evidence. A rejected lane candidate now also leaves a `lane_candidate_rejected` event.
- Breaking changes: no. A lane queue written before this change resumes, and its candidates are filed without a round or base commit.
- PR addresses single concern: yes.
- Root cause is upstream (Magpie/TraceLens/GEAK/IntelliKit/AgentKernelArena), ticket filed: no.

issue.title: fix(forge-loop): plan each round under the search mode its iteration decided
issue.body:
## What this is for

Each iteration resolves its Analysis context before the Supervisor runs and decides the search policy after it, because the policy reads what the Supervisor resolved. Planning took the context Analysis built, so the dispatch (DIVERSIFY asks for every specialist role), the planners' search guidance and the plan-critic rule all saw the previous iteration's search mode. This change has planning read the mode its own iteration decided.

## Evidence: the four sessions of the #2281 A/B

- 7 of 40 plannings ran under a stale mode: 3 planned as EXPLOIT in the iteration the policy switched to DIVERSIFY, and 4 planned as DIVERSIFY after the policy had switched back to EXPLOIT.
- None of the 6 switches to DIVERSIFY in these sessions reached the planners in the iteration that made it. In `abr-r1`, iteration 12 decided DIVERSIFY (`NO_IMPROVEMENT_STALL`) and planned as EXPLOIT. Iteration 13 decided EXPLOIT (`DIVERSIFY_PLAN_CREATED`), crediting a DIVERSIFY plan that was never made, and planned as DIVERSIFY. When the switching iteration measured a queued lane candidate instead of planning, the DIVERSIFY guidance landed on the next planning, by which time the policy had already returned to EXPLOIT.
- Under the #2281 rule, 3 rounds were sent to review citing `search_mode_diversify` after the policy had decided EXPLOIT.
- Source: each `orchestration/iter_NNN/context.json` `search_policy.mode` compared with that iteration's `search_policy_decision` event.

## Description

- `iteration/round_admission.py`: `_with_search_policy(context)` returns the context with `search_mode`, `search_reason_codes`, `search_objective` and `search_mode_residence_remaining` taken from `run_state`, which `_update_search_policy` has just set.
- `iteration/iteration_phases.py`: `_run_orchestration` applies it to the planning context before the plan-review decision and the orchestration service read it.
- The Supervisor's evidence view still reads the mode in force before the iteration decides its policy, which is the mode it reviews; the Implementer's evidence map does not read the mode.

- Linked issue(s): none.
- Tests:
  - New `test_planning_context.py::test_planning_is_handed_the_search_policy_this_iteration_decided`: the Analysis context carries EXPLOIT and the iteration decided DIVERSIFY. The context handed to the orchestration service carries all four decided fields, and a round after a kept one is sent to review for `search_mode_diversify`. On `main` it fails with `'EXPLOIT' == 'DIVERSIFY'`.
  - Run: `pytest -n 8 src/kernelforge/tests`: 6384 passed, 8 skipped, 13 failed. The 13 fail the same way on `main` in this environment: GPU assembly tests, `test_deepseek_backend.py::test_the_retired_deepseek_variables_are_not_consulted`, and two `test_agent_relay_gateways.py` Claude probe tests. `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean, `check_broad_suppress.py` clean, `lint-imports` 14 contracts kept, code-metrics gate run locally against `main`: PASSED.
- Size/complexity triggers crossed: none.
- If this simplifies or refactors: no mechanism removed.
- Observable effect: an iteration that switches search mode now plans under the new mode. Its `orchestration/iter_NNN/context.json` `search_policy` matches the iteration's `search_policy_decision` event, the dispatch and the planners' search guidance follow the decided mode, and `plan_review` events cite the decided mode.
- Breaking changes: no.
- PR addresses single concern: yes.
- Root cause is upstream (Magpie/TraceLens/GEAK/IntelliKit/AgentKernelArena), ticket filed: no.

issue.title: [Fix] [AMD] aiter: Fix garbage decode output with unified attention at page size 1 under CUDA graph

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: CI: run the baseline test suite on this PR

issue.body:
## Motivation

With `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1` on a dense (non-sliding-window) model at the default page size 1, decode produces garbage output when CUDA graph is on. The first token (from prefill) is correct and every decoded token after it is wrong: with greedy sampling, `"The capital of France is"` continues as `" a ( ( ( ( ( ..."` instead of `" a city of romance, art, fashion, and cuisine. Paris is a must"`. GSM8K drops to 0.00. Nothing rejects this configuration, so it fails silently.

In `_apply_cuda_graph_metadata`, the unified-attention page table is copied into the captured `cuda_graph_page_table` only for sliding-window pools or `page_size > 1`. At page size 1 nothing is copied, so `unified_attention` reads an all-zero page table. Sliding-window models and Qwen3-VL (which gets page size 16 from its model override) are not affected. The non-CUDA-graph path builds the page table directly and is not affected either. The SHUFFLE 5D KV layout, the other decode path that reads this page table, requires a page size divisible by 8 (BF16 KV) or 16 (FP8 KV), so it never runs at page size 1. The AMD CI tests and cookbook recipes that enable unified attention all set `--page-size 16` or `64`, so page size 1 had no coverage.

## Modifications

- `aiter_backend.py`: copy the page table for every non-sliding-window configuration. `_transform_table_1_to_real` is the identity at page size 1, so the `page_size > 1` condition only skipped the copy.
- New AMD CI test `test/registered/attention/test_aiter_unified_attention_page_size_1.py`: GSM8K on `DEFAULT_MODEL_NAME_FOR_TEST` with unified attention at page size 1 (threshold 0.65).

## Accuracy Tests

MI355X (gfx950), single GPU, with and without this patch, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1 --attention-backend aiter`, CUDA graph on. GSM8K uses the same settings as the new CI test (200 questions, 5-shot, completion API, `max_tokens=512`), 3 runs each.

| Configuration | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| unified attention, page size 1 | 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.00 | 0.755 / 0.755 / 0.765 |
| unified attention, page size 16 (reference) | — | 0.765 |

A second dense model gives the same picture: Qwen3-8B scores 0.00 before and 0.95 after, the same as page size 16 (0.95).

The new CI test fails on `main` (`np.float64(0.0) not greater than or equal to 0.65`) and passes with this patch: 0.765 on MI355X, and 0.765 on MI300X (gfx942) in this PR's CI.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No change for configurations other than unified attention at page size 1, which was producing wrong output before. With the patch, page size 1 output throughput is within 2% of page size 16.

MI355X, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, `sglang.bench_serving`, random input 2048 / output 256, CUDA graph on, unified attention, patched build:

| Page size | Concurrency | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 58.79 | 4.24 | 224.5 |
| 16 | 1 | 61.89 | 4.25 | 223.4 |
| 1 | 32 | 572.97 | 7.48 | 3294.8 |
| 16 | 32 | 621.54 | 7.15 | 3342.5 |

## Reproduce

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1 python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct --attention-backend aiter --page-size 1 --port 30000

python -m sglang.test.run_eval --port 30000 --eval-name gsm8k --api completion \
  --num-examples 200 --num-threads 128 --max-tokens 512 --num-shots 5

python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 1 \
  --max-concurrency 32 --num-prompts 128 --seed 1
```

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — bug fix, nothing user-facing to document.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

issue.title: feat(kernelforge): hold planning and KB-summary answers to a JSON Schema

labels.name: repo-214761c4
labels.description: Waives the PR diff budget; added by a maintainer with a reason in the PR description

issue.body:
## Description

KernelForge asked several agent roles to write JSON (or a `VERDICT:` line) somewhere inside a free-form answer, then found, guessed at and repaired it in code. This PR lets a session be held to an answer shape instead and moves the four sessions whose answer code acts on onto it.

**Mechanism**

- `AgentRunSpec.output_schema` names a pydantic model (`AgentAnswer` subclasses: every field required, no extra keys, so the schema is one a provider's strict mode accepts).
- Claude Code is given it as `output_format` and returns the answer as `ResultMessage.structured_output`, now carried on `AgentRunResult.structured_output`. Codex gets it as the turn's `output_schema` (present since `openai-codex` 0.144). DeepSeek Harness cannot constrain its answer, so the schema is appended to the prompt of the turn and of a resume.
- `structured_answer(result, Model)` reads it back: the provider's structured value when there is one, else the text -- whole, then each fenced block, then the first `{` to the last `}` -- and raises `StructuredOutputError` naming the model otherwise. `validated_agent_answer` adds the existing API-failure and incomplete-session checks on top.

**Call sites moved onto it**

| Session | Answer | Removed |
|---|---|---|
| Plan critic | `PlanCriticAnswer`: `verdict` (ACCEPT/REVISE/REPLACE), `review` (Markdown), `lane_narrowing` | `VERDICT:` regex and the "missing means REVISE" inference, the width-block reader (`rfind` + extractor + absent/malformed/answered/repaired/not_asked), the width repair session and its turn/time/effort constants, ~50 lines of format instructions in the prompt |
| Dispatch | built per round: `role_id` and `target_case_ids` are enums of the registered roles and scored cases | the repair call, `_parse_dispatch_intents` (string-or-list, lower-casing, dropping), the unknown-role and unknown-case branches, `DispatchIntent` |
| Partition | `PartitionAnswer`: lanes with a boolean `joint`, and the cross-cutting move as an object | `_as_bool`, the string/list/float tolerance in the move reader and its `unreadable` status, `PARTITION_OUTPUT_SCHEMA` |
| KB experience summary | `RunSummary` with `category` as an enum | `_extract_json` and the LLM-path normalisation; the call now lives in `kb_store/run_summary.py` |

`roles/structured_output.py` (`extract_json_object`, `build_repair_prompt`) has no caller left and is deleted. The forge-fuse author prompt no longer asks for an `AUTHORING_RESULT:` line nothing reads.

**Deliberately not converted**, after reading each:

- *forge-fuse discovery*: sessions explore with tools and are routinely cut short by their turn or time budget; `_salvage_objects` recovers the proposals already written ("three quarters of responses arriving truncated"). A schema-held final answer would lose every one of those rounds.
- *rewrite-opportunity `task.json`*: written with file tools, not a final answer, and validated deliberately leniently with the refusal fed back to the agent.
- *roofline ceiling*: the analyst writes its files mid-session, so a session capped after writing still yields a ceiling today; the published file's `mean_ideal_ms` is documented in `docs/kernelforge/reference/cli.md`.
- *analysis artifacts* (`bottleneck.json`, `normalized_metrics.json`): files the prompt tells the agent not to spend turns repairing.

## Linked issue(s)

None.

## Tests

- New `tests/agent_backends/test_structured_output.py`: native and text answers (whole, fenced, embedded -- the assertions of the deleted `roles/test_structured_output.py`), every unusable shape naming its model, the schema instruction, extra keys refused, Claude's `output_format` and result hand-over, and a contract that every answer model in this PR produces a strict-mode schema (all properties required, no extra keys, no `$ref` siblings).
- Codex: a turn is given the schema only when its spec names one. DeepSeek: the schema rides the first prompt and the resume prompt.
- Plan critic, round review, lane partition, dispatch, planning fallbacks, plan revision and KB writer tests now answer in the structured shape. Tests that pinned the removed tolerance (string booleans, a move given as a string or list, the repair passes) are replaced by tests that such an answer is no answer: the critic fails open to `NOT_REVIEWED`, dispatch falls back to framework coverage without a second call, the partition collapses to one lane, the KB writes nothing.
- CI is green at this head: the full suite on Python 3.10 and 3.11, `pyproject declarations`, `ruff`, `import-linter` and `code-metrics`.
- Commands run locally: `pytest src/kernelforge/tests/agent_backends src/kernelforge/tests/workflows/forge_loop src/kernelforge/tests/knowledge/kb_store src/kernelforge/tests/workflows/forge_fusion` (3132 passed; the 49 failures fail identically on `main` in this environment), `pytest src/hyperloom/inference_optimizer/tests/test_packaging_lint.py` on bare pytest + PyYAML without pydantic (9 passed), `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .`, `lint-imports --no-cache` (14 kept).

## Size/complexity triggers crossed

None new. `orchestration.py` goes from 1604 to 1471 lines.

## If this simplifies or refactors

Removed: four format-recovery mechanisms (critic verdict inference, critic width-block reading plus its repair session, dispatch repair plus normalisation, partition lenient readers) and the two shared JSON extractors. Preserved: the critic's fail-open contract, lane-narrowing rules (single-lane floor, refused-empty-round, challenger refusal, joint-lane accounting), dispatch's framework completion (default roles, missing cases, duplicate merge), the partition's single-lane fallback, the KB rule that a summary the LLM did not give is not filed, and the MCP servers' import boundary (they still start without `kernelforge.agent_backends`).

## Observable effect

- The plan critic answers in one structured object. A review given only in prose, or with a verdict outside the three, is now `NOT_REVIEWED` (fail open to the draft) instead of being read as `REVISE`; `critic_review.md` opens with `VERDICT: <verdict>`.
- No width-repair session and no dispatch repair call are ever spent; an unusable dispatch answer falls back to framework coverage in one call.
- `structured_output.json` diagnostics: `plan_critic` loses `verdict_source`, `narrowing_status` and `narrowing_notes`; `lane_narrowing` loses `block`; `dispatch.raw_responses` becomes `dispatch.answer`; the partition's cross-cutting move no longer has an `unreadable` status.
- A KB experience summary in no usable shape now files nothing, as a failed summary call already did, instead of an empty `others` record.
- `pydantic>=2.0` is a declared dependency of the `forge` extra (it was already installed transitively through the provider SDKs). Importing `kernelforge.agent_backends` does not load it -- the answer types are imported from `kernelforge.agent_backends.structured_output` -- so code that reaches the package without the `forge` extra, such as `hyperloom.orchestrator.kernel.campaign_baseline`, still imports.

## Breaking changes

No public interface. `PlanCriticOutcome` and `DispatchIntent` are internal; the diagnostics above are audit artifacts no code reads.

## Live check

Claude Code delivers a structured answer through an internal `StructuredOutput` tool call. Every session shape this PR holds to a schema was run against Claude Code 2.1.299 (`claude-agent-sdk` 0.2.178), the KB summary through `run_summary._query_llm` as shipped:

| Session | Tools / turn cap | Result |
|---|---|---|
| KB summary | none / 1 | `success`, valid `RunSummary` |
| Partition | none / 8 | `success`, valid `PartitionAnswer` |
| Plan critic | Read, Grep, Glob / 100 | `success`, valid `PlanCriticAnswer` |
| Dispatch | Read, Grep, Glob / 500 | `success`, valid dispatch answer |

Each session made one `StructuredOutput` call. Disabling every built-in tool does not remove it, and `max_turns=1` does not cut it off: the KB summary ends `success` with `num_turns=2`.

To rerun the KB summary case with the `claude` extra installed and Claude credentials:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python - <<'PY'
import asyncio
from kernelforge.agent_backends import AgentRunSpec, AgentToolPolicy
from kernelforge.agent_backends.claude import ClaudeBackend
from kernelforge.agent_backends.structured_output import structured_answer
from kernelforge.knowledge.kb_store.run_summary import RunSummary

spec = AgentRunSpec(
    system_prompt="Summarize.", user_prompt="A GEMM run whose winning change was a wider tile.", cwd=".",
    writable=False, timeout_sec=120, protected_globs=["*"], output_schema=RunSummary,
    tool_policy=AgentToolPolicy(read=False, search=False, write=False, shell=False, max_turns=1),
)
result = asyncio.run(ClaudeBackend().run(spec))
print(result.subtype, result.num_turns, structured_answer(result, RunSummary))
PY
```

## PR addresses single concern

Yes: agent answers held to a schema. The `AUTHORING_RESULT` removal is the same concern (an answer format nothing reads).

## Root cause is upstream

No.

issue.title: [Fix] [AMD] aiter: Fix garbage decode output with unified attention at page size 1 under CUDA graph

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: CI: run the baseline test suite on this PR

issue.body:
## Motivation

With `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1` on a dense (non-sliding-window) model at the default page size 1, decode produces garbage output when CUDA graph is on. The first token (from prefill) is correct and every decoded token after it is wrong: with greedy sampling, `"The capital of France is"` continues as `" a ( ( ( ( ( ..."` instead of `" a city of romance, art, fashion, and cuisine. Paris is a must"`. GSM8K drops to 0.00. Nothing rejects this configuration, so it fails silently.

In `_apply_cuda_graph_metadata`, the unified-attention page table is copied into the captured `cuda_graph_page_table` only for sliding-window pools or `page_size > 1`. At page size 1 nothing is copied, so `unified_attention` reads an all-zero page table. Sliding-window models and Qwen3-VL (which gets page size 16 from its model override) are not affected. The non-CUDA-graph path builds the page table directly and is not affected either. The SHUFFLE 5D KV layout, the other decode path that reads this page table, requires a page size divisible by 8 (BF16 KV) or 16 (FP8 KV), so it never runs at page size 1. The AMD CI tests and cookbook recipes that enable unified attention all set `--page-size 16` or `64`, so page size 1 had no coverage.

## Modifications

- `aiter_backend.py`: copy the page table for every non-sliding-window configuration. `_transform_table_1_to_real` is the identity at page size 1, so the `page_size > 1` condition only skipped the copy.

issue.title: [Fix] [AMD] aiter: Fix garbage decode output with unified attention at page size 1 under CUDA graph

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: CI: run the baseline test suite on this PR

issue.body:
## Motivation

With `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1` on a dense (non-sliding-window) model at the default page size 1, decode produces garbage output when CUDA graph is on. The first token (from prefill) is correct and every decoded token after it is wrong: with greedy sampling, `"The capital of France is"` continues as `" a ( ( ( ( ( ..."` instead of `" a city of romance, art, fashion, and cuisine. Paris is a must"`. GSM8K drops to 0.00. Nothing rejects this configuration, so it fails silently.

In `_apply_cuda_graph_metadata`, the unified-attention page table is copied into the captured `cuda_graph_page_table` only for sliding-window pools or `page_size > 1`. At page size 1 nothing is copied, so `unified_attention` reads an all-zero page table. Sliding-window models and Qwen3-VL (which gets page size 16 from its model override) are not affected. The non-CUDA-graph path builds the page table directly and is not affected either. The SHUFFLE 5D KV layout, the other decode path that reads this page table, requires a page size divisible by 8 (BF16 KV) or 16 (FP8 KV), so it never runs at page size 1. issue.title: feat(kernelforge): hold planning and KB-summary answers to a JSON Schema

labels.name: repo-214761c4
labels.description: Waives the PR diff budget; added by a maintainer with a reason in the PR description

issue.body:
## Description

KernelForge asked several agent roles to write JSON (or a `VERDICT:` line) somewhere inside a free-form answer, then found, guessed at and repaired it in code. This PR lets a session be held to an answer shape instead and moves the four sessions whose answer code acts on onto it.

**Mechanism**

- `AgentRunSpec.output_schema` names a pydantic model (`AgentAnswer` subclasses: every field required, no extra keys, so the schema is one a provider's strict mode accepts).
- Claude Code is given it as `output_format` and returns the answer as `ResultMessage.structured_output`, now carried on `AgentRunResult.structured_output`. Codex gets it as the turn's `output_schema` (present since `openai-codex` 0.144). DeepSeek Harness cannot constrain its answer, so the schema is appended to the prompt of the turn and of a resume.
- `structured_answer(result, Model)` reads it back: the provider's structured value when there is one, else the text -- whole, then each fenced block, then the first `{` to the last `}` -- and raises `StructuredOutputError` naming the model otherwise. `validated_agent_answer` adds the existing API-failure and incomplete-session checks on top.

**Call sites moved onto it**

| Session | Answer | Removed |
|---|---|---|
| Plan critic | `PlanCriticAnswer`: `verdict` (ACCEPT/REVISE/REPLACE), `review` (Markdown), `lane_narrowing` | `VERDICT:` regex and the "missing means REVISE" inference, the width-block reader (`rfind` + extractor + absent/malformed/answered/repaired/not_asked), the width repair session and its turn/time/effort constants, ~50 lines of format instructions in the prompt |
| Dispatch | built per round: `role_id` and `target_case_ids` are enums of the registered roles and scored cases | the repair call, `_parse_dispatch_intents` (string-or-list, lower-casing, dropping), the unknown-role and unknown-case branches, `DispatchIntent` |
| Partition | `PartitionAnswer`: lanes with a boolean `joint`, and the cross-cutting move as an object | `_as_bool`, the string/list/float tolerance in the move reader and its `unreadable` status, `PARTITION_OUTPUT_SCHEMA` |
| KB experience summary | `RunSummary` with `category` as an enum | `_extract_json` and the LLM-path normalisation; the call now lives in `kb_store/run_summary.py` |

`roles/structured_output.py` (`extract_json_object`, `build_repair_prompt`) has no caller left and is deleted. The forge-fuse author prompt no longer asks for an `AUTHORING_RESULT:` line nothing reads.

**Deliberately not converted**, after reading each:

- *forge-fuse discovery*: sessions explore with tools and are routinely cut short by their turn or time budget; `_salvage_objects` recovers the proposals already written ("three quarters of responses arriving truncated"). A schema-held final answer would lose every one of those rounds.
- *rewrite-opportunity `task.json`*: written with file tools, not a final answer, and validated deliberately leniently with the refusal fed back to the agent.
- *roofline ceiling*: the analyst writes its files mid-session, so a session capped after writing still yields a ceiling today; the published file's `mean_ideal_ms` is documented in `docs/kernelforge/reference/cli.md`.
- *analysis artifacts* (`bottleneck.json`, `normalized_metrics.json`): files the prompt tells the agent not to spend turns repairing.

## Linked issue(s)

None.

## Tests

- New `tests/agent_backends/test_structured_output.py`: native and text answers (whole, fenced, embedded -- the assertions of the deleted `roles/test_structured_output.py`), every unusable shape naming its model, the schema instruction, extra keys refused, Claude's `output_format` and result hand-over, and a contract that every answer model in this PR produces a strict-mode schema (all properties required, no extra keys, no `$ref` siblings).
- Codex: a turn is given the schema only when its spec names one. DeepSeek: the schema rides the first prompt and the resume prompt.
- Plan critic, round review, lane partition, dispatch, planning fallbacks, plan revision and KB writer tests now answer in the structured shape. Tests that pinned the removed tolerance (string booleans, a move given as a string or list, the repair passes) are replaced by tests that such an answer is no answer: the critic fails open to `NOT_REVIEWED`, dispatch falls back to framework coverage without a second call, the partition collapses to one lane, the KB writes nothing.
- CI is green at this head: the full suite on Python 3.10 and 3.11, `pyproject declarations`, `ruff`, `import-linter` and `code-metrics`.
- Commands run locally: `pytest src/kernelforge/tests/agent_backends src/kernelforge/tests/workflows/forge_loop src/kernelforge/tests/knowledge/kb_store src/kernelforge/tests/workflows/forge_fusion` (3132 passed; the 49 failures fail identically on `main` in this environment), `pytest src/hyperloom/inference_optimizer/tests/test_packaging_lint.py` on bare pytest + PyYAML without pydantic (9 passed), `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .`, `lint-imports --no-cache` (14 kept).

## Size/complexity triggers crossed

None new. `orchestration.py` goes from 1604 to 1471 lines.

## If this simplifies or refactors

Removed: four format-recovery mechanisms (critic verdict inference, critic width-block reading plus its repair session, dispatch repair plus normalisation, partition lenient readers) and the two shared JSON extractors. Preserved: the critic's fail-open contract, lane-narrowing rules (single-lane floor, refused-empty-round, challenger refusal, joint-lane accounting), dispatch's framework completion (default roles, missing cases, duplicate merge), the partition's single-lane fallback, the KB rule that a summary the LLM did not give is not filed, and the MCP servers' import boundary (they still start without `kernelforge.agent_backends`).

## Observable effect

- The plan critic answers in one structured object. A review given only in prose, or with a verdict outside the three, is now `NOT_REVIEWED` (fail open to the draft) instead of being read as `REVISE`; `critic_review.md` opens with `VERDICT: <verdict>`.
- No width-repair session and no dispatch repair call are ever spent; an unusable dispatch answer falls back to framework coverage in one call.
- `structured_output.json` diagnostics: `plan_critic` loses `verdict_source`, `narrowing_status` and `narrowing_notes`; `lane_narrowing` loses `block`; `dispatch.raw_responses` becomes `dispatch.answer`; the partition's cross-cutting move no longer has an `unreadable` status.
- A KB experience summary in no usable shape now files nothing, as a failed summary call already did, instead of an empty `others` record.
- `pydantic>=2.0` is a declared dependency of the `forge` extra (it was already installed transitively through the provider SDKs). Importing `kernelforge.agent_backends` does not load it -- the answer types are imported from `kernelforge.agent_backends.structured_output` -- so code that reaches the package without the `forge` extra, such as `hyperloom.orchestrator.kernel.campaign_baseline`, still imports.

## Breaking changes

No public interface. `PlanCriticOutcome` and `DispatchIntent` are internal; the diagnostics above are audit artifacts no code reads.

## Live check

Claude Code delivers a structured answer through an internal `StructuredOutput` tool call. Every session shape this PR holds to a schema was run against Claude Code 2.1.299 (`claude-agent-sdk` 0.2.178), the KB summary through `run_summary._query_llm` as shipped:

| Session | Tools / turn cap | Result |
|---|---|---|
| KB summary | none / 1 | `success`, valid `RunSummary` |
| Partition | none / 8 | `success`, valid `PartitionAnswer` |
| Plan critic | Read, Grep, Glob / 100 | `success`, valid `PlanCriticAnswer` |
| Dispatch | Read, Grep, Glob / 500 | `success`, valid dispatch answer |

Each session made one `StructuredOutput` call. Disabling every built-in tool does not remove it, and `max_turns=1` does not cut it off: the KB summary ends `success` with `num_turns=2`.

To rerun the KB summary case with the `claude` extra installed and Claude credentials:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python - <<'PY'
import asyncio
from kernelforge.agent_backends import AgentRunSpec, AgentToolPolicy
from kernelforge.agent_backends.claude import ClaudeBackend
from kernelforge.agent_backends.structured_output import structured_answer
from kernelforge.knowledge.kb_store.run_summary import RunSummary

spec = AgentRunSpec(
    system_prompt="Summarize.", user_prompt="A GEMM run whose winning change was a wider tile.", cwd=".",
    writable=False, timeout_sec=120, protected_globs=["*"], output_schema=RunSummary,
    tool_policy=AgentToolPolicy(read=False, search=False, write=False, shell=False, max_turns=1),
)
result = asyncio.run(ClaudeBackend().run(spec))
print(result.subtype, result.num_turns, structured_answer(result, RunSummary))
PY
```

## PR addresses single concern

Yes: agent answers held to a schema. The `AUTHORING_RESULT` removal is the same concern (an answer format nothing reads).

## Root cause is upstream

No.

issue.title: fix(gemm_tune): tune in measured chunks on every card, keep finished chunks, and fail on unmeasured timings
issue.body:
gemm-tune ran out of time on the 2026-10-26 image and lost all its work. Shapes were budgeted at a fixed 93 s each, but aiter now tries 5943 candidates per shape instead of 2084, so a shape takes about 110 s. An 18-shape batch needed about 2000 s against a 1799 s cap, was killed, and its tune.log was overwritten, so every finished shape was lost. On the vLLM image every candidate timed 0 us, yet the run still reported `ok` with a speedup: once the tuner's main process has profiled, rocprofiler-sdk exports `ROCPROFILER_REGISTER_LIBRARY`, and the spawned workers inherit it and record no GPU events.

Changes:
- Shapes are tuned in chunks. Each chunk is sized from the measured time per shape of the chunks before it and must end before the deadline. Finished chunks are merged as they land. A cut or failed chunk makes the run `partial_output`, with the shortfall named.
- Without `--mp`, a tuner uses every card it can see (`--gpu-ids`, the device mask, then the torch count).
- A run whose profile or tuned rows are all `us<=0` or `tflops=inf` fails as `unmeasured_timings`.
- On timeout, the captured output is kept and a TIMEOUT note is appended.
- Each tuner starts with a `sitecustomize` first on `PYTHONPATH`. It drops `ROCPROFILER_REGISTER_LIBRARY` in every spawned worker, then runs the image's own `sitecustomize`.

Verified:
- New tests reproduce each failure (chunked deadline, unmeasured timings, worker env) and fail before the change.
- `src/kernelforge/tests/workflows/gemm_tune`: 1176 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `test_demand_bucket_matches_installed_aiter`, which fails on `main` too because of this host's aiter.
- On an MI355X vLLM image with 4 cards and the same demand file: a8w8_blockscale ran in 3 chunks with real timings, 18/18 shapes improved, best 3.78x on aiter's timer. The same run before the fix reported every candidate at 0 us.
- In an MB session, a 4-card lease tuned 32 shapes in chunks, and the result went to a gated test.

## PR #2351 -- fix(gemm_tune): tune in measured chunks on every card, keep finished chunks, and fail on unmeasured timings

What it does: gemm-tune sized each aiter dense / sglang bf16 tuner run from a fixed per-shape cost, so on the newer aiter image a whole-list process was killed at the deadline and lost every finished shape; and spawned tuner workers inherited `ROCPROFILER_REGISTER_LIBRARY` and timed every candidate at 0 us. issue.title: fix(forge-loop): resume the plan revision under its synthesis session's system prompt
issue.body:
## What this is for

When the Plan Critic returns `REVISE` or `REPLACE`, the revision resumes each lane's synthesis session, but under a different system prompt than the one that session ran under. The cached prefix opens with the system prompt, so every resumed revision rewrites the whole synthesis conversation into the cache instead of reading it. On Codex and DeepSeek, which apply a system prompt only when a session starts, the resumed revision also never receives the revision instructions. This change resumes the session under its own system prompt and sends the revision instructions in the resumed message.

## Evidence: paired replay of 29 recorded revisions

Source: every lane revision in the four sessions of the #2281 A/B (`Aiter-task/gemm_a16w16_nt_n1024_k4096`, rewrite-by-flydsl, claude-opus-5.5, Claude Code 2.1.299): 24 lane plans and 5 single plans. Each revision was replayed through Forge's own resume path (`OrchestrationAgent._run_spec` and `ClaudeBackend.resume`), forked from the recorded synthesis session so that every run starts from the same finished synthesis. Each arm ran twice per revision, 116 runs in all. The current arm's first revision request matches production's to the token in all 29 cases. Plans were judged blind by a different model family (`gpt-5.6-sol`): coverage of the critic's concerns, work scheduled on another lane's ground, and pairwise preference asked in both orders.

|                                                   | current      | this change  |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ------------ |
| pass `validated_agent_text`, open with `Summary:` | 58/58        | 58/58        |
| critic-concern coverage (paired)                  | 0.880        | 0.877        |
| plans contradicting a critic concern              | 7/58         | 10/58        |
| plans scheduling another lane's ground            | 12/48        | 10/48        |
| median revision time / turns                      | 78 s / 2     | 58 s / 1     |
| spend on these 29 revisions                       | $21.58       | $10.60       |

- Coverage: the paired difference is -0.003 (Wilcoxon p = 0.93). This change scores higher on 9 revisions and lower on 12; 8 are tied.
- Pairwise, a win counts only when both orders agree: 46 ties, 8 for current, 4 for this change (sign test p = 0.39). Pairs of two runs from the same arm, as a noise control, are decisive 24% of the time; pairs from different arms are decisive 21% of the time.
- The lane prompt's boundary rule does not stop a revision from following the critic onto another lane's ground. Applicable concerns that need another lane's ground: current addressed 15 of 20, this change 16 of 20.
- Spend: "current" is what production paid. "This change" is the replayed runs priced as production would bill them. The first request reads the synthesis's last prompt from the cache when production started the revision within the 5-minute TTL of that request (25 of 29); otherwise it writes the whole prompt. If every revision hit the cache, spend would be $9.01. Across the four sessions this saves about $2.7 per session, or 2.6% of total spend.
- The resumed first request is about 9.9k tokens longer (median). The increase tracks the size of the synthesis's last turn (Spearman 0.58), which is consistent with that turn's thinking staying in context once the system prompt no longer changes. The spend figures include these tokens.
- Limits: plan quality is judged by one model, not by downstream KEEP rate or speedup; the data cover one task and 29 revisions. The TTL margin is thin: 25 of 29 revisions started within 300 s of the synthesis's last request, but only 7 within 240 s, so a slower critic would cut the saving.

## Description

- `roles/contracts.py`: `SynthesizedPlan.system_prompt` records the system prompt the plan's session ran under. A plan that keeps a session id must name it.
- `roles/orchestration.py`: single-plan and lane synthesis record their turn's system prompt on the draft. A resumed revision runs under `draft.system_prompt`. The fresh-session fallback keeps `REVISION_SYSTEM_PROMPT` as its system prompt.
- `roles/plan_requests.py`: `revision_instructions` (the revision prompt's text) moves from the fresh payload into the resumed payload, and the fresh payload inherits it. A fresh revision's request is unchanged.
- `docs/kernelforge/forge_long_horizon_state.md`: the revision step states that a resume keeps the synthesis system prompt and carries the instructions in its message.

- Linked issue(s): none.
- Tests:
  - `test_plan_revision.py`: a resumed revision runs under the synthesis spec's system prompt and its payload carries `revision_instructions`; the summary-line rule ("for the plan as revised") reaches both resumed and fresh revisions through `revision_instructions`; single-plan and lane drafts record the system prompt their spec used (new, parametrized); a draft with a session id but no system prompt does not construct (new).
  - Run: `pytest -n 8 src/kernelforge/tests`: 6349 passed, 8 skipped, 4 failed. Three fail the same way on `main` in this environment (the two `config/test_rocpc_profile_discovery.py` tests and `test_assembly_aiter_moe_gpu.py::test_aiter_w4a16_roundtrip_rejects_wrong_silu_and_rebinds_arguments`). `rewrite_controller/test_opportunity_agent.py::test_hookless_resume_republication_clears_a_corrected_refusal` is flaky on both: in isolation it failed 6 of 6 times on `main` and 1 of 3 times on this branch. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean; `lint-imports` keeps all 12 contracts; the code-metrics gate run locally against `main` passes.
- Size/complexity triggers crossed: none; `roles/orchestration.py` goes from 1608 to 1604 lines.
- If this simplifies or refactors: no mechanism removed.
- Observable effect: resumed revision turns now run under the lane or single-plan synthesis system prompt, and their message carries `revision_instructions`. Revision spend roughly halves when the revision starts within the cache TTL of the synthesis. Revisions on Codex and DeepSeek now receive the revision instructions. The session's role label stays `orchestration revision`, but any transcript analysis that classifies turns by system prompt will now see revision turns as synthesis turns.
- Breaking changes: no. `SynthesizedPlan` is never persisted.
- PR addresses single concern: yes.
- Root cause is upstream (Magpie/TraceLens/GEAK/IntelliKit/AgentKernelArena), ticket filed: no.

issue.title: [Fix] [AMD] aiter: Fix garbage decode output with unified attention at page size 1 under CUDA graph

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: CI: run the baseline test suite on this PR

issue.body:
## Motivation

With `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1` on a dense (non-sliding-window) model at the default page size 1, decode produces garbage output when CUDA graph is on. The first token (from prefill) is correct and every decoded token after it is wrong: with greedy sampling, `"The capital of France is"` continues as `" a ( ( ( ( ( ..."` instead of `" a city of romance, art, fashion, and cuisine. Paris is a must"`. GSM8K drops to 0.00. Nothing rejects this configuration, so it fails silently.

In `_apply_cuda_graph_metadata`, the unified-attention page table is copied into the captured `cuda_graph_page_table` only for sliding-window pools or `page_size > 1`. At page size 1 nothing is copied, so `unified_attention` reads an all-zero page table. Sliding-window models and Qwen3-VL (which gets page size 16 from its model override) are not affected. The non-CUDA-graph path builds the page table directly and is not affected either. The SHUFFLE 5D KV layout, the other decode path that reads this page table, requires a page size divisible by 8 (BF16 KV) or 16 (FP8 KV), so it never runs at page size 1. The AMD CI tests and cookbook recipes that enable unified attention all set `--page-size 16` or `64`, so page size 1 had no coverage.

## Modifications

- `aiter_backend.py`: copy the page table for every non-sliding-window configuration. `_transform_table_1_to_real` is the identity at page size 1, so the `page_size > 1` condition only skipped the copy.
- New AMD CI test `test/registered/attention/test_aiter_unified_attention_page_size_1.py`: GSM8K on `DEFAULT_MODEL_NAME_FOR_TEST` with unified attention at page size 1 (threshold 0.65).

## Accuracy Tests

MI355X (gfx950), single GPU, with and without this patch, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1 --attention-backend aiter`, CUDA graph on. GSM8K uses the same settings as the new CI test (200 questions, 5-shot, completion API, `max_tokens=512`), 3 runs each.

| Configuration | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| unified attention, page size 1 | 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.00 | 0.755 / 0.755 / 0.765 |
| unified attention, page size 16 (reference) | — | 0.765 |

A second dense model gives the same picture: Qwen3-8B scores 0.00 before and 0.95 after, the same as page size 16 (0.95).

The new CI test fails on `main` (`np.float64(0.0) not greater than or equal to 0.65`) and passes with this patch: 0.765 on MI355X, and 0.765 on MI300X (gfx942) in this PR's CI.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No change for configurations other than unified attention at page size 1, which was producing wrong output before. With the patch, page size 1 output throughput is within 2% of page size 16.

MI355X, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, `sglang.bench_serving`, random input 2048 / output 256, CUDA graph on, unified attention, patched build:

| Page size | Concurrency | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 58.79 | 4.24 | 224.5 |
| 16 | 1 | 61.89 | 4.25 | 223.4 |
| 1 | 32 | 572.97 | 7.48 | 3294.8 |
| 16 | 32 | 621.54 | 7.15 | 3342.5 |

## Reproduce

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1 python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct --attention-backend aiter --page-size 1 --port 30000

python -m sglang.test.run_eval --port 30000 --eval-name gsm8k --api completion \
  --num-examples 200 --num-threads 128 --max-tokens 512 --num-shots 5

python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 1 \
  --max-concurrency 32 --num-prompts 128 --seed 1
```

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — bug fix, nothing user-facing to document.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

issue.title: [Fix] mem-cache: Budget the non-DSA EAGLE draft KV pool at its DCP-widened size

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: CI: run the baseline test suite on this PR

issue.body:
## Motivation

Under DCP a non-DSA EAGLE / MTP draft pool is allocated over the allocator's widened ids: `KVCacheConfigurator.loc_space_scale` is `dcp_size` for that draft worker, and `_derive_pool_sizes` allocates `max_total_num_tokens * dcp_size` draft rows per rank. `DefaultPoolConfigurator` prices the DSA draft term and the DFLASH draft term with `dcp_size`, but its non-DSA EAGLE / STANDALONE branch prices one row of the target's per-layer KV. For an MLA draft, whose latent is the size of the target's, that is `dcp_size` times too small: `max_total_num_tokens` comes out too large, and the static pools take `(dcp_size - 1)` draft layers' worth of KV per rank out of the memory that `--mem-fraction-static` leaves for activations and CUDA graphs. A GQA/MHA draft cannot be priced from the target's per-layer KV either way: `ModelConfig.get_num_kv_heads` replicates the target's KV heads over DCP but not the draft's.

This is the MTP + DCP deployment of MLA models such as DeepSeek-V3 / R1. On DeepSeek-R1 at TP8 / DCP8 the draft pool is 20.68 GB per GPU while the budget charges it 2.59 GB, so about 18 GB of the reserve is gone before the first request. The sizing code is shared by all platforms.

An MLA draft writes only its owner rows (`loc // dcp_size`), so most of its widened allocation is never written; #43599 sizes the MLA draft pool in physical rows. This PR does not change the allocation; it makes the budget price the draft rows the pool allocates today.

## Modifications

`DefaultPoolConfigurator`: price the non-DSA EAGLE / STANDALONE draft term as `dcp_size` rows per token, each at the draft's own per-layer KV size from `_compute_cell_size(..., dcp_size=1)`. For MLA that is the target's per-layer size; a GQA/MHA draft keeps its unreplicated KV heads. At `dcp_size == 1` nothing changes.

## Accuracy Tests

The patch changes only how many KV tokens the pools hold; no kernel or model path changes.

`test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_pool_configurator.py`: 71 passed, 36 subtests passed. `test/registered/unit/managers/test_dcp_logical_capacity.py`: 3 passed.

The new `test_eagle_dcp_replicated_draft_does_not_exceed_budget` runs an MLA model and a GQA model (8 KV heads, TP8) at `dcp_size` 1 and 4 and checks that the memory the pools take, with the draft at `dcp_size` rows of its own per-layer KV, stays within the budget and uses more than 99% of it. On `main` the MLA `dcp_size=4` subtest fails with `10907136 not less than or equal to 10000000`; pricing the GQA draft from the target's per-layer KV fails the GQA `dcp_size=4` subtest with `9157632 not greater than 9900000.0`.

## Pool Sizing Measurements

`amd/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4-v2` (61 layers + 1 MTP layer), MI355X, TP8, `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, default `--mem-fraction-static` (0.7718), with and without this patch. Numbers are TP0 startup logs with `--load-format dummy`. With the real weights at DCP 8 the token counts differ by fewer than 60 tokens (4,818,943 before, 4,330,064 after) and the free memory is the same.

| DCP | `max_total_num_tokens` before | after | Draft pool before | after | Free after pools before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5,035,505 | 5,035,505 | 2.70 GB | 2.70 GB | 63.43 GB | 63.43 GB |
| 4 | 4,842,479 | 4,618,980 (−4.6%) | 10.39 GB | 9.91 GB | 53.74 GB | 61.61 GB |
| 8 | 4,819,001 | 4,330,117 (−10.1%) | 20.68 GB | 18.58 GB | 43.69 GB | 61.76 GB |

"Free after pools" is the `Memory pool end. avail mem` line after the draft pool is allocated. Without the fix the unbudgeted draft rows take 7.9 GB (DCP 4) and 18.1 GB (DCP 8) out of that reserve.

The capacity change matches the layer count: the budget now prices `61 + dcp` layer-equivalents instead of `61 + 1`, and `4,842,479 × 62/65 = 4,618,980` and `4,819,001 × 62/69 = 4,330,117` match the measured values. The lower capacity is the cost of pricing the draft rows that are allocated today; the previous capacity was only reachable by spending the activation reserve.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The patch only changes how many KV tokens the pools hold; no kernel or scheduling path changes.

No end-to-end throughput comparison: DeepSeek-R1 with EAGLE and DCP does not serve on ROCm `main`, with or without this patch. The non-DSA NextN draft keeps `dcp_size > 1` (`DeepseekV2AttentionMLA.__init__` only resets it for DSA drafts), so `forward_absorb_rocm_core` sends `draft_extend_v2` into the DCP decode branch with `k_window=None`, and `AiterAttnBackend.forward_extend` fails on `k.shape` while capturing the draft-extend CUDA graph. Both builds stop there, with dummy and with real weights. Pool sizing happens before that point, so the measurements above come from the full startup path.

## Reproduce

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path amd/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4-v2 --trust-remote-code --tp 8 --dcp-size 8 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --load-format dummy
```

Compare the two `KV Cache is allocated` lines (target, then draft) and the `Memory pool end. avail mem` line that follows each, at `--dcp-size 1` and `--dcp-size 8`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — internal sizing correction, nothing user-facing to document.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

The non-CUDA-graph path builds the page table directly and is not affected either. The SHUFFLE 5D KV layout, the other decode path that reads this page table, requires a page size divisible by 8 (BF16 KV) or 16 (FP8 KV), so it never runs at page size 1. The AMD CI tests and cookbook recipes that enable unified attention all set `--page-size 16` or `64`, so page size 1 had no coverage.

## Modifications

- `aiter_backend.py`: copy the page table for every non-sliding-window configuration. `_transform_table_1_to_real` is the identity at page size 1, so the `page_size > 1` condition only skipped the copy.
- New AMD CI test `test/registered/attention/test_aiter_unified_attention_page_size_1.py`: GSM8K on `DEFAULT_MODEL_NAME_FOR_TEST` with unified attention at page size 1 (threshold 0.65).

## Accuracy Tests

MI355X (gfx950), single GPU, with and without this patch, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1 --attention-backend aiter`, CUDA graph on. GSM8K uses the same settings as the new CI test (200 questions, 5-shot, completion API, `max_tokens=512`), 3 runs each.

| Configuration | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| unified attention, page size 1 | 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.00 | 0.755 / 0.755 / 0.765 |
| unified attention, page size 16 (reference) | — | 0.765 |

A second dense model gives the same picture: Qwen3-8B scores 0.00 before and 0.95 after, the same as page size 16 (0.95).

The new CI test fails on `main` (`np.float64(0.0) not greater than or equal to 0.65`) and passes with this patch: 0.765 on MI355X, and 0.765 on MI300X (gfx942) in this PR's CI.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No change for configurations other than unified attention at page size 1, which was producing wrong output before. With the patch, page size 1 output throughput is within 2% of page size 16.

| Page size | Concurrency | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 58.79 | 4.24 | 224.5 |
| 16 | 1 | 61.89 | 4.25 | 223.4 |
| 1 | 32 | 572.97 | 7.48 | 3294.8 |
| 16 | 32 | 621.54 | 7.15 | 3342.5 |

## Reproduce

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1 python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct --attention-backend aiter --page-size 1 --port 30000

python -m sglang.test.run_eval --port 30000 --eval-name gsm8k --api completion \
  --num-examples 200 --num-threads 128 --max-tokens 512 --num-shots 5

python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 1 \
  --max-concurrency 32 --num-prompts 128 --seed 1
```

issue.title: [Fix] mem-cache: Budget the non-DSA EAGLE draft KV pool at its DCP-widened size

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: CI: run the baseline test suite on this PR

issue.body:
## Motivation

Under DCP a non-DSA EAGLE / MTP draft pool is allocated over the allocator's widened ids: `KVCacheConfigurator.loc_space_scale` is `dcp_size` for that draft worker, and `_derive_pool_sizes` allocates `max_total_num_tokens * dcp_size` draft rows per rank. `DefaultPoolConfigurator` prices the DSA draft term and the DFLASH draft term with `dcp_size`, but its non-DSA EAGLE / STANDALONE branch prices one row of the target's per-layer KV. For an MLA draft, whose latent is the size of the target's, that is `dcp_size` times too small: `max_total_num_tokens` comes out too large, and the static pools take `(dcp_size - 1)` draft layers' worth of KV per rank out of the memory that `--mem-fraction-static` leaves for activations and CUDA graphs. A GQA/MHA draft cannot be priced from the target's per-layer KV either way: `ModelConfig.get_num_kv_heads` replicates the target's KV heads over DCP but not the draft's.

This is the MTP + DCP deployment of MLA models such as DeepSeek-V3 / R1. On DeepSeek-R1 at TP8 / DCP8 the draft pool is 20.68 GB per GPU while the budget charges it 2.59 GB, so about 18 GB of the reserve is gone before the first request. The sizing code is shared by all platforms.

An MLA draft writes only its owner rows (`loc // dcp_size`), so most of its widened allocation is never written; #43599 sizes the MLA draft pool in physical rows. This PR does not change the allocation; it makes the budget price the draft rows the pool allocates today.

## Modifications

`DefaultPoolConfigurator`: price the non-DSA EAGLE / STANDALONE draft term as `dcp_size` rows per token, each at the draft's own per-layer KV size from `_compute_cell_size(..., dcp_size=1)`. For MLA that is the target's per-layer size; a GQA/MHA draft keeps its unreplicated KV heads. At `dcp_size == 1` nothing changes.

## Accuracy Tests

The patch changes only how many KV tokens the pools hold; no kernel or model path changes.

`test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_pool_configurator.py`: 71 passed, 36 subtests passed. `test/registered/unit/managers/test_dcp_logical_capacity.py`: 3 passed.

The new `test_eagle_dcp_replicated_draft_does_not_exceed_budget` runs an MLA model and a GQA model (8 KV heads, TP8) at `dcp_size` 1 and 4 and checks that the memory the pools take, with the draft at `dcp_size` rows of its own per-layer KV, stays within the budget and uses more than 99% of it. On `main` the MLA `dcp_size=4` subtest fails with `10907136 not less than or equal to 10000000`; pricing the GQA draft from the target's per-layer KV fails the GQA `dcp_size=4` subtest with `9157632 not greater than 9900000.0`.

## Pool Sizing Measurements

`amd/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4-v2` (61 layers + 1 MTP layer), MI355X, TP8, `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, default `--mem-fraction-static` (0.7718), with and without this patch. Numbers are TP0 startup logs with `--load-format dummy`. With the real weights at DCP 8 the token counts differ by fewer than 60 tokens (4,818,943 before, 4,330,064 after) and the free memory is the same.

| DCP | `max_total_num_tokens` before | after | Draft pool before | after | Free after pools before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5,035,505 | 5,035,505 | 2.70 GB | 2.70 GB | 63.43 GB | 63.43 GB |
| 4 | 4,842,479 | 4,618,980 (−4.6%) | 10.39 GB | 9.91 GB | 53.74 GB | 61.61 GB |
| 8 | 4,819,001 | 4,330,117 (−10.1%) | 20.68 GB | 18.58 GB | 43.69 GB | 61.76 GB |

"Free after pools" is the `Memory pool end. avail mem` line after the draft pool is allocated. Without the fix the unbudgeted draft rows take 7.9 GB (DCP 4) and 18.1 GB (DCP 8) out of that reserve.

The capacity change matches the layer count: the budget now prices `61 + dcp` layer-equivalents instead of `61 + 1`, and `4,842,479 × 62/65 = 4,618,980` and `4,819,001 × 62/69 = 4,330,117` match the measured values. The lower capacity is the cost of pricing the draft rows that are allocated today; the previous capacity was only reachable by spending the activation reserve.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The patch only changes how many KV tokens the pools hold; no kernel or scheduling path changes.

No end-to-end throughput comparison: DeepSeek-R1 with EAGLE and DCP does not serve on ROCm `main`, with or without this patch. The non-DSA NextN draft keeps `dcp_size > 1` (`DeepseekV2AttentionMLA.__init__` only resets it for DSA drafts), so `forward_absorb_rocm_core` sends `draft_extend_v2` into the DCP decode branch with `k_window=None`, and `AiterAttnBackend.forward_extend` fails on `k.shape` while capturing the draft-extend CUDA graph. Both builds stop there, with dummy and with real weights. Pool sizing happens before that point, so the measurements above come from the full startup path.

## Reproduce

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path amd/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4-v2 --trust-remote-code --tp 8 --dcp-size 8 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --load-format dummy
```

Compare the two `KV Cache is allocated` lines (target, then draft) and the `Memory pool end. avail mem` line that follows each, at `--dcp-size 1` and `--dcp-size 8`.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — internal sizing correction, nothing user-facing to document.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

review.body:
@xindubawukong Thank you for contributing Ave to Hyperloom, and for the quick turnaround across the earlier review rounds.

After looking at where this fits, we'd like Ave to land as an extension of KernelForge rather than as a separate kernel backend in Hyperloom.

Hyperloom is built around end-to-end inference optimization, and KernelForge is its built-in kernel agent: within Hyperloom, kernel-level optimization is KernelForge's job. Optimizing AveLang kernels is kernel-level work, so we think it belongs with KernelForge's capabilities, alongside the other kernel languages it already supports, rather than as a parallel route beside it.

Could you rework the PR in that direction? We're happy to discuss the details with you.

issue.title: refactor(common): give Hyperloom and KernelForge one shared package

labels.name: repo-214761c4
labels.description: Waives the PR diff budget; added by a maintainer with a reason in the PR description

labels.name: repo-214761c4
labels.description: Waives new, worse and baseline-growth code-metrics findings; reason required in the PR description

issue.body:
## What this changes

`kernelforge` reached into `hyperloom.common` for the code the two packages share, so the Forge
backend could not be loaded, tested or reused without the optimizer package. That code now lives
in its own top-level package, `hyperloom_common`, and the copies KernelForge kept of four of its
helpers are folded into it.

- `hyperloom_common`: `aiter_jit_cache`, `checkpoint_quant`, `coerce`, `entry_points`, `env`,
  `fs_utils`, `git_safety`, `gpu_identity`, `io`, `jsonio`, `pr_monitor_urls`, `timeutil`,
  `unified_diff`
- `hyperloom_common.llm`: `llm_config`, `llm_headers`, `llm_attribution`, `llm_request_hooks`,
  `llm_stability_env`, `token_usage`, `reasoning_effort`, `claude_oneshot`, `deepseek_session`
- `hyperloom.common` keeps what only the optimizer uses (`perf_metric`, `env_safety`,
  `provenance`, `proctree`, ...).

The wheel installs the package top-level into site-packages, so it carries the project prefix: a
bare `common` can collide with another distribution's, or be shadowed by a `common.py` in the
working directory of `python -m kernelforge.cli`.

## The boundary

| Contract            | Rule                                                                               |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `kf-no-hyperloom`   | `kernelforge` imports nothing from `hyperloom`                                     |
| `common-is-leaf`    | `hyperloom_common` imports nothing from `hyperloom`, `hyperloom_kb`, `kernelforge` |
| `hl-common-is-leaf` | `hyperloom.common` imports nothing from the project but `hyperloom_common`         |

`hyperloom_common` is also an ancestor of the `acyclic` contract, so the
`llm_config -> claude_oneshot` cycle baseline is checked. `test_common_import_lint.py` checks the
two leaf rules per module.

## Duplicates folded into the shared package

| KernelForge copy | Now | Behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| two `rewrite_controller` `_now_iso`, `analysis_session._utc_now`, five inline `strftime`/`isoformat` | `timeutil.now_iso` | same strings |
| `recovery._load_json`, `reporting._load_json`, `forge_fusion/campaign._read_result_json` | `jsonio.read_json` / `read_json_strict` | see below |
| `utils/durable_io.py` (removed) | `io` with `options=DURABLE`; `fsync_directory`, `fsync_tree`, `fsync_tree_directories` | same bytes on disk: JSON writes pass `JsonFormat(trailing_newline=True)` |
| `utils/gpu_arch._ARCH_BY_GPU_TYPE` | built from `gpu_identity.AMD_GPU_BOARDS` | see below |

## Observable effect

- An `io` write that asks for `fsync` or `fsync_dir` now raises when the flush fails instead of
  continuing without it. On the hyperloom side this reaches the call sites that ask for it:
  recipe KB local store, delivery ledger, forge handoff, langfuse emitter, hosted entry.
- KernelForge recognises R9700 (gfx1201) and Radeon 8060S (gfx1151). `canonical_gpu_type` keys
  their records under `r9700` / `radeon8060s`, and the `amd_instinct_mi308x` /
  `amd_instinct_mi325x` spellings under `mi300x`, as it already did for `mi308x` / `mi325x`. The
  boards carry their full "AMD Instinct MI3xxX" names as aliases.
- `forge_loop/campaign/reporting.py` reads its JSON as UTF-8 rather than the locale encoding; a
  forge-fusion result file that holds a non-object is logged and read as `{}`.
- For code importing these modules out of tree: `hyperloom.common.<name>` becomes
  `hyperloom_common.<name>` or `hyperloom_common.llm.<name>`, and `kernelforge.utils.durable_io` is
  gone. No aliases are kept.

## Wiring kept in step

`src/hyperloom_common` is in the coverage `source`, mypy `files`, and the `compileall` and
`bandit` sweeps. The Forge e2e smoke runs on changes under `src/hyperloom_common/`. The release
notes carry an Unreleased entry.

## Code-metrics gate: `baseline-raise`

`forge_loop/roles/analysis.py` (1815 -> 1839 lines) and `forge_loop/memory/knowledge_integration.py`
(1424 -> 1426) grow because each durable write now names its options (`options=DURABLE`, plus
`fmt=` for JSON) instead of getting them implicitly from `durable_io`. The growth is that
explicitness, not new logic; splitting these modules is outside this change.

## Diff budget: `size-exception`

1608 production Python lines, over the 1000-line budget. About 880 of them are the move itself:
import paths rewritten from `hyperloom.common.<name>` to `hyperloom_common[.llm].<name>`, with no
logic change. The other ~730 fold the four KernelForge duplicates into the shared modules; they stay
in this PR so the shared package lands with the copies it replaces rather than beside them. Each
step is its own commit (rename, `timeutil`, `jsonio`, `io`, `gpu`) to review on its own.

## Verification

- `lint-imports --no-cache`: 12 contracts kept, 0 broken
- `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` (0.16.2): clean
- mypy on `src/hyperloom_common`: no error the same modules did not already have on the merge base
- full `pytest -m "not targeted_build_e2e"`, compared with the merge base on the same host: no new
  failure (that host's failures come from missing GPU / optional SDKs;
  `test_hookless_resume_republication_clears_a_corrected_refusal` is flaky on both)

## Not in this PR

These pairs overlap only in part and do different jobs, so they are left as they are:

- `kernelforge/utils/process_reaping.py` vs `hyperloom.common.proctree`: both parse `/proc/<pid>/stat`
- `kernelforge/utils/aiter_cache.py` vs `hyperloom_common.aiter_jit_cache`: both locate AITER through `find_spec`
- `gpu_arch.detect_arch` vs `hyperloom.common.provenance.detect_gfx_arch`: both run `rocminfo`
- KernelForge's own `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES` parsing and `rocm-smi` calls vs `hyperloom.common.visible_devices` / `rocm_smi`
