issue.title: refactor(kernelforge): mirror the source tree in tests, split the loop and orchestration tests by topic
issue.body:
- Description: `src/kernelforge/tests` had 121 test modules at its root, subdirectories named after packages that no longer exist, two test modules far larger than any other, and tests importing helpers from other test modules. Three commits:
  1. **Layout** (`f79a009`, generated by the move script below; running it on `83a898bd8` reproduces every rename, `__init__.py` and import rewrite). `tests/` mirrors `src/kernelforge`: the test of a module in `kernelforge/<package>/` lives in `tests/<package>/`. Subdirectories that already named a package keep it (`fusion/` -> `workflows/forge_fusion/`, `gemm_tune/` -> `workflows/gemm_tune/`, `kernel_rewrite_controller/` -> `workflows/rewrite_controller/`, `tools/` -> `utils/`); `loop/` and 118 root modules move to the package of the module they test; the tests of kernelforge as a whole stay at the root with `conftest.py` (commit 3 moves the two root modules that were not). Every test directory is a package. Hand edits on top: four tests that located files by a fixed number of parent directories use `PACKAGE_ROOT` / `repo_root` from `conftest.py`, and `forge_e2e_gate.py` (and its test), `docs/kernelforge/how-to/assembly.md`, the two assembly example READMEs, `hip_module_validation.md`, `test_rename_completeness.py` and a docstring in `test_dotenv_precedence_recipes.py` name the new paths.
  2. **Topics and helpers** (`35b9d87`). `test_loop_runner.py` (8542 lines, 222 tests) becomes 18 modules in `tests/workflows/forge_loop/iteration/`, one per behaviour of the loop (candidate workspace, pending keep, resume replay, campaign start, outcome pins, lane rounds, round admission, stacking, attempt verdict, device contention, planning context, analysis refresh, search-mode transitions, baseline scoring, supervisor rulings, orchestration failures, lesson recording, failure propagation), with the builders several share in `_iteration_loop.py`. `test_forge_orchestration.py` (3065 lines, 101 tests) becomes 8 modules in `tests/workflows/forge_loop/roles/` with its shared fakes in `_orchestration_fakes.py`. Helpers other tests imported from a test module move to an `_`-prefixed module beside what they build or fake (`_claude_fakes`, `_numerical_contract`, `_assembly_sources`, `_flat_experience`, `_in_memory_store`, `_rewrite_spec`, `_campaign_args`, `_cross_process_campaign`, `_analysis_fakes`, `_sglang_dense_bf16_run`); no test module imports another. Statements move verbatim; besides imports, the only edits remove five pieces of setup the split left repeated across files (the gate counts those as new duplication): the Claude timeout spec reuses the shared one, the KB store reader and writer tests take their fixtures from `tests/knowledge/kb_store/conftest.py`, the two loop builders share `_initialize_workspace`, the stacking tests share `_wide_kernel`, and two orchestration tests share `_single_lane_service`.
  3. **Review fixes** (`7440261`). `fake_aiter` and `_asm_accepts` move from `test_aiter_splitk_validate.py` to `workflows/gemm_tune/_fake_aiter.py`: `test_splitk_cap.py` imported them with a relative import the first commit's rewrite did not reach. `_orchestration_fakes` exports `GROUND_A`, `GROUND_B` and `JOINT_GROUND` without the underscore, which CodeQL reported as unused globals. `test_review_regressions.py` held no kernelforge-wide test: its `_promote_best` call-site guard moves to `workflows/forge_loop/iteration/test_scoring_reachability.py` and its seven tests of the aiter all-reduce example driver to `examples/test_aiter_allreduce_forge_loop.py`; `test_kernel_backend_prompt_modules_are_importable` moves from `test_rename_completeness.py` to `kernel_backends/test_kernel_backend_prompt_contract.py`. The root now holds `conftest.py`, `test_rename_completeness.py` and `test_stdio_tool_schemas.py` (one check over the stdio MCP servers of two packages). The created test modules get back the blank lines between import groups that pruning their copied import blocks dropped.
  - The other test modules over 1500 lines (`test_codex_backend.py`, `test_rewrite_by_flydsl_pipeline.py`, `test_forge_loop_resume.py`, `test_specialist_probe.py`, `test_measurement_guards.py`, `test_knowledge_integration.py`, `test_resolve_and_cli.py`) each test one component and stay whole.
- Linked issue(s): none
- Tests: no test added, removed or changed in what it asserts. Run in a ROCm container without `torch`, on `83a898bd8` and on each commit:
  - `pytest --collect-only src/kernelforge/tests`: 6269 tests every time; every node id maps one-to-one through the renames and splits.
  - `pytest -n 32 src/kernelforge/tests`: identical outcome for every test (6240 passed, 32 skipped, 2 failed). The two failures (`gemm_tune/test_utils.py::TestTunerEnvVars::test_a4w4_env_var_is_read_by_installed_aiter`, which needs `torch`, and `gemm_tune/test_build_parallelism.py::TestTheJobLimit::test_no_ceiling_means_no_opinion`) fail the same way on `83a898bd8` in this container.
  - No test module imports another, by an AST scan of the test tree covering absolute, relative and function-local imports.
  - Commit 2: every top-level statement of the two split modules and the ten helper sources appears exactly once in its destinations, AST-identical apart from the repointed imports and the five deduplications above.
  - `scripts/code_metrics.py --base-ref 83a898bd8` with the pinned tools: passed, 0 new and 0 worse findings, duplicated lines improved in 7 files. `lint-imports` (11 contracts kept, `.importlinter` unchanged), `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` 0.16.2, `reuse lint`, `pytest scripts/tests` and `test_packaging_lint.py` pass.
- Size/complexity triggers crossed: none; no production Python changes.
- If this simplifies or refactors: removed the flat test root, the stale directory names, the two multi-component test modules and every test-to-test import; preserved the test set and every test's outcome, shown by the collection and per-test comparison above.
- Observable effect: none for an operator. A contributor finds a module's tests at the same relative path under `tests/`, and a loop or orchestration test in the module named after its topic. The cached `.test_durations` seed names the old node ids, so the first coverage runs shard the moved tests by pytest-split's average duration until the seed is refreshed.
- Breaking changes: no. Test paths change: an open PR that adds a test at the old root, in an old subdirectory, or in `test_loop_runner.py` / `test_forge_orchestration.py` needs to place it in the mirrored directory or topic module.
- PR addresses single concern: yes
- Root cause is upstream (Magpie/TraceLens/GEAK/IntelliKit/AgentKernelArena), ticket filed: n/a

```python
INIT_HEADER = "# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.\n# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\n"


def plan() -> dict[str, str]:
    moves: dict[str, str] = {}
    for path in sorted(OLD.rglob("*.py")):
        rel = path.relative_to(OLD).as_posix()
        if "__pycache__" in rel:
            continue
        parent = pathlib.PurePosixPath(rel).parent.as_posix()
        if rel in FILES:
            package = FILES[rel]
        elif parent in SUBDIRS:
            package = SUBDIRS[parent]
        else:
            raise SystemExit(f"no destination for {rel}")
        name = pathlib.PurePosixPath(rel).name
        target = OLD / package / name if package != "." else OLD / name
        moves[str(path)] = target.as_posix()
    missing = set(FILES) - {pathlib.Path(p).relative_to(OLD).as_posix() for p in moves}
    if missing:
        raise SystemExit(f"FILES entries with no file: {sorted(missing)}")
    targets = list(moves.values())
    duplicates = {t for t in targets if targets.count(t) > 1}
    if duplicates:
        raise SystemExit(f"two files map to one destination: {sorted(duplicates)}")
    for old, new in moves.items():
        if old != new and pathlib.Path(new).exists():
            raise SystemExit(f"destination exists: {new}")
    return moves


def dotted(path: str) -> str:
    return pathlib.PurePosixPath(path).with_suffix("").as_posix().removeprefix("src/").replace("/", ".")


def main() -> None:
    moves = plan()
    if "--dry-run" in sys.argv:
        for old, new in moves.items():
            print(f"{old} -> {new}")
        return
    for old, new in moves.items():
        if old == new:
            continue
        pathlib.Path(new).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        subprocess.run(["git", "mv", old, new], check=True)
    # Every directory from tests/ down to each destination is a package, so module
    # names never depend on pytest's rootdir-relative basename insertion.
    test_dirs = set()
    for new in moves.values():
        directory = pathlib.Path(new).parent
        while directory != OLD.parent:
            test_dirs.add(directory)
            directory = directory.parent
    for directory in sorted(test_dirs):
        init = directory / "__init__.py"
        if not init.exists():
            init.write_text(INIT_HEADER, encoding="utf-8")
            subprocess.run(["git", "add", str(init)], check=True)
    # Rewrite imports of moved test modules, longest name first so prefixes do not clobber.
    renames = {dotted(o): dotted(n) for o, n in moves.items() if not o.endswith("__init__.py") and o != n}
    pattern = re.compile(r"\b(" + "|".join(re.escape(k) for k in sorted(renames, key=len, reverse=True)) + r")\b")
    changed = []
    for py in sorted(pathlib.Path("src").rglob("*.py")):
        text = py.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        new_text = pattern.sub(lambda m: renames[m.group(1)], text)
        if new_text != text:
            py.write_text(new_text, encoding="utf-8")
            changed.append(str(py))
    json.dump({"moves": moves, "renames": renames, "import_rewrites": changed}, open("/tmp/kf_move_result.json", "w"), indent=1)
    print(f"moved {sum(o != n for o, n in moves.items())} files; rewrote imports in {len(changed)} files")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

- Description: what and why Sixth step of the kernelforge cleanup: the source tree takes the layout of the restructure plan, so a package's place says what it is -- entry points in `cli/`, workflows in `workflows/`, shared capabilities beside them -- and the forge-loop, which was spread over `loop/`, `orchestrator/` and `cli/`, is one package. Generated on `main` at 06b2b6367, which includes #2278. New top level: `agent_backends/ cli/ config/ evaluation/ examples/ kernel_backends/ knowledge/ roofline_ceiling/ tests/ utils/ workflows/`. | Before | After | |---|---| | `loop/`, `orchestrator/` | `workflows/forge_loop/`: `api.py`, `bootstrap/`, `iteration/`, `search/`, `roles/` (all of `orchestrator/`), `gate/`, `memory/`, `preparation/`, `campaign/`, `policy/`, `export/` | | `fusion/`, `rewrite_by_flydsl/`, `kernel_rewrite_controller/`, `gemm_tune/` | `workflows/forge_fusion/`, `workflows/flydsl_rewrite/`, `workflows/rewrite_controller/`, `workflows/gemm_tune/` | | `run_export/` | `workflows/forge_loop/export/` (it reads eight forge-loop modules and only forge-loop runs) | | `assembly/` | merged into `kernel_backends/assembly/` (the backend's prompts and its toolchain) | | `tools/` | `utils/` | | `config.py`, `resources.py` | `config/__init__.py`, `config/resources.py` | | `tracker/` | experiment records -> `forge_loop/campaign/`, token usage -> `agent_backends/` | | `workspace/edit_policy.py` | protection rules (data, used by eight packages) -> `config/edit_policy.py`; `hide_forge_loop_output`, `tracked_editable_paths` -> `forge_loop/campaign/workspace_files.py` | Five commits, and three merges of `main` taken while this was open: 1. **Generated** by the script below, run on `main`. Running the attached script (its current version, with the rule commit 4 added) on the same commit reproduces commits 1 and 4 except their two hand edits, so a conflict with a later `main` is resolved by running it again rather than by hand. It carries commit 5's exclusion too, so a rerun leaves those two literals as `main` has them. Besides `git mv` it rewrites import statements that change shape (submodules of a package that splits, names of a package that dissolves, relative imports that no longer resolve), every dotted module path (imports, patch targets, logger names, `-m` launch paths) and every `kernelforge/` file path in `src/`, `scripts/`, `docs/`, `.github/`, `pyproject.toml` and `.importlinter`, and the quoted kernelforge-relative paths the source-scanning tests use. Release notes and `.claude/` records keep their historical paths. 2. **Follow-ups the script cannot derive**: `.importlinter` contract semantics; flydsl_rewrite and rewrite_controller reach `ExperimentTracker` and `hide_forge_loop_output` through `forge_loop/api.py`; hyperloom takes `resource_path` from `kernelforge.config`; `forge_runner` finds `src/` one level further up; one test's directory join and two messages. 3. **The CodeQL alerts the move re-reported** (they exist on `main` at the old paths; the new paths made them "new"), fixed without changing behaviour: - `gate/insession_gate.py` `py/redos`. The `python [options] -c` prefix was one regex with a repeated option group. Only the interpreter word stays a regex now; the options are walked word by word in linear time. - It was checked differentially against the old regex on 300000 generated commands, with no mismatch. Two new tests pin the cases. - Unchanged here and worth a follow-up: an option with a separate value (`python -W error -c ...`) ends the option run, so that payload is not scanned, exactly as on `main`. - `WorkspaceLock.acquire` `py/file-not-closed`: the lock file is closed when writing the pid fails too. - `harness_authoring` `py/multiple-definition`: a dead initial assignment is gone. - `task_preparer` / `task_preparer_prompts` `py/implicit-string-concatenation-in-list`: the multi-line prompt strings are parenthesized; the text is unchanged. 4. **Names written without the `kernelforge` prefix.** Commit 1 rewrote only names starting with `kernelforge.` or `kernelforge/` and did not scan root configuration, so a few references still named the old layout: - the gemm tuner path in `.gitleaks.toml`'s allowlist (it matches the tuner files again); - the `kf-mcp-servers-light` row of the style guide's contract table (that row and `kf-tools-foundation` also now state the tightened contracts); - comments and docstrings such as `loop.runner`, `rewrite_by_flydsl.optimize` and `tracker/usage.py`. The script now rewrites such a name when it names a module or file that moved, and only inside comments and strings in Python. Outside kernelforge's own files it leaves `loop.*`, `orchestrator.*` and `tools.*` alone, because hyperloom has packages of those names. 5. **Two string literals that are not module paths**, back to the value `main` has. Commit 1 rewrote both because they are spelled like dotted module paths, and neither is used as one: - `_forge_gemm_tuning.py`'s `provenance` label. The snapshot manifest stores it, `project_source_snapshots` copies it into the recipe's `source_snapshots[].provenance`, and the Recipe KB keeps it, so rewriting it would split every stored row from every row written after this change. - the `~/.cache/kernelforge.gemm_tune/script_probe` cache directory, whose rename would cost every host its warm probe cache once and leave the old directory behind. Subpackage boundaries follow the import graph: `relay_runtime` (an `IterationLoop` mixin) is in `iteration/` and `search_policy` in `search/`, because the other placements made `campaign`, `search` and `policy` import each other. `acyclic` now holds with two fewer baseline entries. - Linked issue(s): none - Tests: added/updated? commands run? - No behaviour change, so no new tests; tests only follow the paths (commit 1) and the two path joins in commit 2. - Run locally on `1c7b3b37`, the first version of this branch: `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`; `lint-imports` (11 kept, two acyclic baseline entries fewer); every kernelforge module imports; `pytest --collect-only` over kernelforge, hyperloom and scripts (27016 collected; 9 hyperloom trace-analysis modules need `TraceLens`, absent here); the full `src/kernelforge/tests` suite (6277 passed; the 3 failures -- `test_no_ceiling_means_no_opinion` and two `test_rocpc_profile_discovery` cases -- fail the same way on the base); the 17 hyperloom test files that import kernelforge plus `orchestrator/kernel/tests` (967 passed; the 3 failures fail the same way on the base); every command's `--help` output diffed against main: identical. - The forge-loop E2E (`triton-softmax-forge-loop`) covers what no static check reaches: the `-m` launch paths (specialist probe server, MCP server) and the import lines `kernel_backends/assembly/capture.py` writes into kernel code. It passed at `1f40650cc`, together with every other check. Commit 5 landed after that run, so it has to run once more on the final head. - Size/complexity triggers crossed: - **Diff budget: 1640 production lines, needs `size-exception`.** Pure renames count zero; the 1640 lines are the rewritten import and path lines in the files that reference a moved module. Splitting by package would not shrink it (each reference is rewritten once) and would leave both layouts on main in between. - **Code metrics: needs `baseline-raise`.** Nothing grew or got more complex; the gate cannot pair three moved units: - `_build_prompt` in `flydsl_rewrite/flydsl_rewrite_driver_preparation.py` (65 lines) and in `forge_loop/preparation/task_preparer_prompts.py` (54 lines): unchanged functions, but two moved units share the name, and the gate pairs moves only by a unique qualified name. - `forge_loop/preparation/task_preparer.py` 1450 -> 1459 lines: two import lines became multi-line because the module paths are longer, and commit 3 parenthesizes one prompt string. - `forge_loop/gate/insession_gate.py` (already over 1200 lines) grows by the linear option scan that replaces the flagged regex. - If this simplifies or refactors: no behaviour change. Preserved contracts: command names, options and output; the `kernelforge` entry point and `python -m kernelforge.cli`; every package's public names (only their module paths change); KB, campaign and result formats. - Observable effect: - Module paths change as in the table; `python -m kernelforge.assembly` becomes `python -m kernelforge.kernel_backends.assembly`. - Logger names follow the modules (for example `kernelforge.gemm_tune` -> `kernelforge.workflows.gemm_tune`); a log filter on an old name stops matching. - The import lines `kernel_backends/assembly/capture.py` writes into kernel code name the new path. The Experience KB holds no assembly solution yet, so no persisted data names `kernelforge.assembly`. Nothing is kept for the old path. - Breaking changes: internal module paths, no compatibility modules. hyperloom is updated in this PR; its imports go through the package interfaces (`kf-public-interfaces` now also forbids `kernelforge.config` submodules). The `kernelforge.agent_providers` plugin interface (`kernelforge.agent_backends`) does not move. - PR addresses single concern: yes -- the directory layout of kernelforge. - Root cause is upstream: n/a

"kernelforge." + ".".join(parts[:i]) if old in modules: return ".".join([modules[old][len("kernelforge.") :], *parts[i:]]) return name def _prose_spans(text: str) -> list[tuple[int, int]]: """The comment and string spans of Python source, the only places prose names a module in code.""" import io import tokenize starts = [0] for line in text.splitlines(keepends=True): starts.append(starts[-1] + len(line)) kinds = {tokenize.COMMENT, tokenize.STRING} kinds |= {getattr(tokenize, "FSTRING_MIDDLE")} if hasattr(tokenize, "FSTRING_MIDDLE") else set() spans = [] try: for token in path.endswith(".py"): return substitute(text) pieces, cursor = [], 0 for start, end in _prose_spans(text): pieces.append(text[cursor:start]) pieces.append(substitute(text[start:end])) cursor = end pieces.append(text[cursor:]) return "".join(pieces) def rewrite_text(modules: dict[str, str], paths: dict[str, str], moves: dict[str, str]) -> int: changed = 0 ambiguous = set(OLD_TOP_PACKAGES) & _hyperloom_names() files = _git("ls-files", *TEXT_ROOTS).splitlines() for path in files: if path.startswith(TEXT_EXCLUDE) or Path(path).suffix not in TEXT_SUFFIXES: continue file = ROOT / path try: _QUOTED_REL.sub(lambda m: _rewrite_quoted_rel(m, moves), new) new = _rewrite_bare_text(path, new, modules, moves, ambiguous) for index, literal in enumerate(guarded): new = new.replace(f"<>", literal) the agent relay and its actors, the search mode, and stall detection.", f"{FL}/gate": "The in-session gate an Implementer session must pass before it stops.", f"{FL}/memory": "What the loop remembers across iterations and campaigns: lessons, the outcome ledger, the Experience KB.", f"{FL}/preparation": "Making a task measurable before the loop starts: driver preparation and its preflight.", f"{FL}/campaign": "One campaign's durable records: its configuration, state, recovery, experiments and workspace files.", f"{FL}/policy": "Pure decisions the loop takes from a campaign's state: the round budget and the analysis refresh.", } def move_files(moves: dict[str, str]) -> None: for old, new in sorted(moves.items()): target = KF / new target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) _git("mv", str(KF / old), str(target)) def write_new_files() -> None: for package, doc in NEW_PACKAGES.items(): init = KF / package / "__init__.py" if not init.exists(): ("tracker/__init__.py", "workspace/__init__.py", "assembly/__init__.py"): if (KF / leftover).exists(): _git("rm", "-q", "-f", str(KF / leftover)) _remove_empty_old_dirs() def _remove_empty_old_dirs() -> None: """An empty directory left where a package was would still import as a namespace package.""" for old in ("fusion", "gemm_tune", "kernel_rewrite_controller", "loop", "orchestrator", "rewrite_by_flydsl", "run_export", "tools", "tracker", "workspace", "assembly"): top = KF / old if not top.exists(): continue for directory in sorted((p for p in top.rglob("*") if p.is_dir()), key=lambda p: len(p.parts), reverse=True): if directory.name == "__pycache__" or not any(directory.iterdir()): for cached in directory.glob("*.pyc") if directory.name == "__pycache__" else (): cached.unlink() if not any(directory.iterdir()): directory.rmdir() if not any(top.iterdir()): top.rmdir() else: sys.exit(f"{old}/ still holds files after the move") def _split_edit_policy() -> None: source = KF / "workspace" / "edit_policy.py" text = source.read_text(encoding="utf-8") functions_at = text.index("\ndef hide_forge_loop_output(") rules, functions = text[:functions_at].rstrip() + "\n", text[functions_at:].lstrip("\n") rules = rules.replace( '"""Canonical workspace edit policy Forge\'s sessions and the loop are held to."""', '"""What a Forge workspace protects from a candidate: the measurement surface every agent session is held to."""', ) rules = rules.replace("from kernelforge.utils.git import git_bytes\n", "") rules = rules.replace("from pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Iterable\n\n", "") (KF / "config" / "edit_policy.py").write_text(rules, encoding="utf-8") header = ( f'{SPDX}"""The files a forge-loop campaign keeps in its workspace, and the ones a candidate may edit."""\n\n' "from __future__ import annotations\n\n" "from pathlib import Path\n" "from typing import Iterable\n\n" "from kernelforge.config.edit_policy import FORGE_LOOP_OUTPUT_DIRNAME, str(source)) def _merge_assembly_init() -> None: target = KF / "kernel_backends" / "assembly" / "__init__.py" toolchain = (KF / "assembly" / "__init__.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8") body = toolchain.split('"""', 2)[2] target.write_text( f'{SPDX}"""AMDGPU assembly kernel backend: its optimization expertise, and the compiler-generated assembly\n' 'support Forge kernel candidates run Path(__file__).resolve().parent\n" if old not in text: sys.exit("resources.py: package root line not found") path.write_text(text.replace(old, "_PACKAGE_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\n"), comment.body:
Both literals are back to the values main has, in 3aafe9c14:

- `src/hyperloom/orchestrator/kernel/_forge_gemm_tuning.py:657` -- `provenance="kernelforge.gemm_tune"`
- `src/kernelforge/workflows/gemm_tune/script_probe.py:77` -- `root / "kernelforge.gemm_tune" / "script_probe"`

Both are byte-identical to 06b2b6367, and the commit changes nothing else.

Scope checked before reverting, so that no real module path went back by mistake: at this head there are 19 quoted `kernelforge.<moved package>` literals in production code. Seventeen have to carry the new layout -- the `find_spec` probe, the two compile-import keys in `kernel_backends/assembly/capture.py`, the nine prompt modules in `kernel_backends/constants.py`, the `-m` launch path in `roles/specialists.py`, and four `logging.getLogger` names the description already lists as changing. The two above were the only others.

No test pinned either value: the script-probe tests go through `FORGE_SCRIPT_PROBE_CACHE`, and the tuning tests do not assert the provenance string. So the revert needed no test change.

Your third point is still open: the move script in the description is unchanged, so regenerating the first commit on a later main would reintroduce both. Worth an exclusion list there before anyone reruns it.

issue.body:
- Description: what and why Sixth step of the kernelforge cleanup: the source tree takes the layout of the restructure plan, so a package's place says what it is -- entry points in `cli/`, workflows in `workflows/`, shared capabilities beside them -- and the forge-loop, which was spread over `loop/`, `orchestrator/` and `cli/`, is one package. Generated on `main` at 06b2b6367, which includes #2278. New top level: `agent_backends/ cli/ config/ evaluation/ examples/ kernel_backends/ knowledge/ roofline_ceiling/ tests/ utils/ workflows/`. | Before | After | |---|---| | `loop/`, `orchestrator/` | `workflows/forge_loop/`: `api.py`, `bootstrap/`, `iteration/`, `search/`, `roles/` (all of `orchestrator/`), `gate/`, `memory/`, `preparation/`, `campaign/`, `policy/`, `export/` | | `fusion/`, `rewrite_by_flydsl/`, `kernel_rewrite_controller/`, `gemm_tune/` | `workflows/forge_fusion/`, `workflows/flydsl_rewrite/`, `workflows/rewrite_controller/`, `workflows/gemm_tune/` | | `run_export/` | `workflows/forge_loop/export/` (it reads eight forge-loop modules and only forge-loop runs) | | `assembly/` | merged into `kernel_backends/assembly/` (the backend's prompts and its toolchain) | | `tools/` | `utils/` | | `config.py`, `resources.py` | `config/__init__.py`, `config/resources.py` | | `tracker/` | experiment records -> `forge_loop/campaign/`, token usage -> `agent_backends/` | | `workspace/edit_policy.py` | protection rules (data, used by eight packages) -> `config/edit_policy.py`; `hide_forge_loop_output`, `tracked_editable_paths` -> `forge_loop/campaign/workspace_files.py` | Five commits, and three merges of `main` taken while this was open: 1. **Generated** by the script below, run on `main`. Running the attached script (its current version, with the rule commit 4 added) on the same commit reproduces commits 1 and 4 except their two hand edits, so a conflict with a later `main` is resolved by running it again rather than by hand. It carries commit 5's exclusion too, so a rerun leaves those two literals as `main` has them. Besides `git mv` it rewrites import statements that change shape (submodules of a package that splits, names of a package that dissolves, relative imports that no longer resolve), every dotted module path (imports, patch targets, logger names, `-m` launch paths) and every `kernelforge/` file path in `src/`, `scripts/`, `docs/`, `.github/`, `pyproject.toml` and `.importlinter`, and the quoted kernelforge-relative paths the source-scanning tests use. Release notes and `.claude/` records keep their historical paths. 2. **Follow-ups the script cannot derive**: `.importlinter` contract semantics; flydsl_rewrite and rewrite_controller reach `ExperimentTracker` and `hide_forge_loop_output` through `forge_loop/api.py`; hyperloom takes `resource_path` from `kernelforge.config`; `forge_runner` finds `src/` one level further up; one test's directory join and two messages. 3. **The CodeQL alerts the move re-reported** (they exist on `main` at the old paths; the new paths made them "new"), fixed without changing behaviour: - `gate/insession_gate.py` `py/redos`. The `python [options] -c` prefix was one regex with a repeated option group. Only the interpreter word stays a regex now; the options are walked word by word in linear time. - It was checked differentially against the old regex on 300000 generated commands, with no mismatch. Two new tests pin the cases. - Unchanged here and worth a follow-up: an option with a separate value (`python -W error -c ...`) ends the option run, so that payload is not scanned, exactly as on `main`. - `WorkspaceLock.acquire` `py/file-not-closed`: the lock file is closed when writing the pid fails too. - `harness_authoring` `py/multiple-definition`: a dead initial assignment is gone. - `task_preparer` / `task_preparer_prompts` `py/implicit-string-concatenation-in-list`: the multi-line prompt strings are parenthesized; the text is unchanged. 4. **Names written without the `kernelforge` prefix.** Commit 1 rewrote only names starting with `kernelforge.` or `kernelforge/` and did not scan root configuration, so a few references still named the old layout: - the gemm tuner path in `.gitleaks.toml`'s allowlist (it matches the tuner files again); - the `kf-mcp-servers-light` row of the style guide's contract table (that row and `kf-tools-foundation` also now state the tightened contracts); - comments and docstrings such as `loop.runner`, `rewrite_by_flydsl.optimize` and `tracker/usage.py`. The script now rewrites such a name when it names a module or file that moved, and only inside comments and strings in Python. Outside kernelforge's own files it leaves `loop.*`, `orchestrator.*` and `tools.*` alone, because hyperloom has packages of those names. 5. **Two string literals that are not module paths**, back to the value `main` has. Commit 1 rewrote both because they are spelled like dotted module paths, and neither is used as one: - `_forge_gemm_tuning.py`'s `provenance` label. The snapshot manifest stores it, `project_source_snapshots` copies it into the recipe's `source_snapshots[].provenance`, and the Recipe KB keeps it, so rewriting it would split every stored row from every row written after this change. - the `~/.cache/kernelforge.gemm_tune/script_probe` cache directory, whose rename would cost every host its warm probe cache once and leave the old directory behind. Subpackage boundaries follow the import graph: `relay_runtime` (an `IterationLoop` mixin) is in `iteration/` and `search_policy` in `search/`, because the other placements made `campaign`, `search` and `policy` import each other. `acyclic` now holds with two fewer baseline entries. - Linked issue(s): none - Tests: added/updated? commands run? - No behaviour change, so no new tests; tests only follow the paths (commit 1) and the two path joins in commit 2. - Run locally on `1c7b3b37`, the first version of this branch: `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`; `lint-imports` (11 kept, two acyclic baseline entries fewer); every kernelforge module imports; `pytest --collect-only` over kernelforge, hyperloom and scripts (27016 collected; 9 hyperloom trace-analysis modules need `TraceLens`, absent here); the full `src/kernelforge/tests` suite (6277 passed; the 3 failures -- `test_no_ceiling_means_no_opinion` and two `test_rocpc_profile_discovery` cases -- fail the same way on the base); the 17 hyperloom test files that import kernelforge plus `orchestrator/kernel/tests` (967 passed; the 3 failures fail the same way on the base); every command's `--help` output diffed against main: identical. - The forge-loop E2E (`triton-softmax-forge-loop`) covers what no static check reaches: the `-m` launch paths (specialist probe server, MCP server) and the import lines `kernel_backends/assembly/capture.py` writes into kernel code. It passed at `1f40650cc`, together with every other check. Commit 5 landed after that run, so it has to run once more on the final head. - Size/complexity triggers crossed: - **Diff budget: 1640 production lines, needs `size-exception`.** Pure renames count zero; the 1640 lines are the rewritten import and path lines in the files that reference a moved module. Splitting by package would not shrink it (each reference is rewritten once) and would leave both layouts on main in between. - **Code metrics: needs `baseline-raise`.** Nothing grew or got more complex; the gate cannot pair three moved units: - `_build_prompt` in `flydsl_rewrite/flydsl_rewrite_driver_preparation.py` (65 lines) and in `forge_loop/preparation/task_preparer_prompts.py` (54 lines): unchanged functions, but two moved units share the name, and the gate pairs moves only by a unique qualified name. - `forge_loop/preparation/task_preparer.py` 1450 -> 1459 lines: two import lines became multi-line because the module paths are longer, and commit 3 parenthesizes one prompt string. - `forge_loop/gate/insession_gate.py` (already over 1200 lines) grows by the linear option scan that replaces the flagged regex. - If this simplifies or refactors: no behaviour change. Preserved contracts: command names, options and output; the `kernelforge` entry point and `python -m kernelforge.cli`; every package's public names (only their module paths change); KB, campaign and result formats. - Observable effect: - Module paths change as in the table; `python -m kernelforge.assembly` becomes `python -m kernelforge.kernel_backends.assembly`. - Logger names follow the modules (for example `kernelforge.gemm_tune` -> `kernelforge.workflows.gemm_tune`); a log filter on an old name stops matching. - The import lines `kernel_backends/assembly/capture.py` writes into kernel code name the new path. The Experience KB holds no assembly solution yet, so no persisted data names `kernelforge.assembly`. Nothing is kept for the old path. - Breaking changes: internal module paths, no compatibility modules. hyperloom is updated in this PR; its imports go through the package interfaces (`kf-public-interfaces` now also forbids `kernelforge.config` submodules). The `kernelforge.agent_providers` plugin interface (`kernelforge.agent_backends`) does not move. - PR addresses single concern: yes -- the directory layout of kernelforge. - Root cause is upstream: n/a
Move script (move_layout.py), run from the repository root on a clean tree ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Regenerate the kernelforge directory layout change (PR-6a) on the current checkout. Run from the repository root on a clean tree: python move_layout.py Steps, all derived from the tables below: 1. rewrite import statements that change shape (submodules imported from a package that splits, names imported from a package that is dissolved, relative imports that no longer resolve), on the old tree; 2. rewrite every dotted module path and every ``kernelforge/...`` file path in the repository's text files; 3. ``git mv`` every file to its new place; 4. write the files that are not pure moves (new package ``__init__``s, the edit-policy split, the assembly ``__init__`` merge, the resources package root). """ from __future__ import annotations import ast import re import subprocess import sys from pathlib import Path ROOT = Path.cwd() KF = ROOT / "src" / "kernelforge" FL = "workflows/forge_loop" # --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- # The layout, relative to src/kernelforge/. # --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- DIR_MOVES = { "fusion": "workflows/forge_fusion", "rewrite_by_flydsl": "workflows/flydsl_rewrite", "kernel_rewrite_controller": "workflows/rewrite_controller", "gemm_tune": "workflows/gemm_tune", "tools": "utils", "run_export": f"{FL}/export", "loop/bootstrap": f"{FL}/bootstrap", "loop/iteration": f"{FL}/iteration", } _LOOP_FILES = { "__init__.py": "", "api.py": "", "agent_extras.py": "roles", "agent_relay.py": "search", "analysis_evidence.py": "roles", "analysis_refresh_policy.py": "policy", "analysis_runtime.py": "iteration", "archive.py": "campaign", "campaign_config.py": "campaign", "campaign_setup.py": "campaign", "decision_labels.py": "campaign", "device_hazard.py": "iteration", "dist_harness.py": "preparation", "experience.py": "memory", "experiments_layout.py": "campaign", "external_artifacts.py": "preparation", "fanout.py": "iteration", "gate_settings.py": "gate", "campaign", "runner.py": "iteration", "search_actors.py": "search", "search_policy.py": "search", "supervisor.py": "search", "task_preflight.py": "preparation", "task_preparer.py": "preparation", "task_preparer_audit.py": "preparation", "task_preparer_prompts.py": "preparation", } _ORCHESTRATOR_OVERRIDES = {"gate_tag.py": "gate"} FILE_MOVES: dict[str, str] = {} for name, sub in _LOOP_FILES.items(): FILE_MOVES[f"loop/{name}"] = f"{FL}/{sub + '/' if sub else ''}{name}" for path in sorted((KF / "orchestrator").glob("*.py")): sub = _ORCHESTRATOR_OVERRIDES.get(path.name, "roles") comment.body:
## PR #2282 -- refactor(kernelforge): give the source tree the layout of the restructure plan

What it does: `src/kernelforge/` had no rule that said what a package is -- the forge-loop alone was spread over `loop/`, `orchestrator/` and `run_export/`, and entry points, workflows and shared capabilities sat side by side. This moves 564 paths into a layout where the place says the kind (`cli/`, `config/`, `utils/`, `kernel_backends/`, `workflows/<name>/`, the whole forge-loop under `workflows/forge_loop/`), via a reproducible move script that does the `git mv` and rewrites every import statement, dotted module path and `kernelforge/` file path, plus the follow-ups the script cannot derive.

Blocking issues: none.

Two things were checked and cleared rather than taken on trust. The import line `kernel_backends/assembly/capture.py` writes into candidate kernel source is committed into the operator's workspace and pinned by `launcher_sha256`, so a workspace prepared before this PR cannot be repaired in place (prepare.py:309-310) -- but AMD-AGI/Hyperloom#1768 settled that repo-wide ("a workspace is never resumed across code versions") and deleted every cross-version loader on that basis, naming the assembly preparation record among them, so nothing is owed a migration here. And the `python -c` payload scanner rewritten in e13b6e04b is a fail-closed surface where a missed payload is unseen tampering, so the new walker was compared against the regex it replaces on repeated `-c`, `-cfoo`, `-- -c`, `python foo.py -c`, a trailing `-c`, a separator-terminated option and the `xpython` lookbehind: no divergence, and it carries its own ReDoS case.

Not verified here: the forge-loop GPU `e2e` has not reported at this head, and it is the only thing that exercises the `-m` launch paths and the import lines `capture.py` writes into kernel code. `coverage` and `analyze` are also still running; every other check is green.

Checked: kernel_backends/assembly/{capture,prepare}.py, workflows/forge_loop/bootstrap/{preparation,run,warm_start}.py, workflows/forge_loop/gate/insession_gate.py, workflows/forge_loop/campaign/run_state.py, workflows/forge_fusion/harness_authoring.py, config/{__init__,resources,edit_policy}.py and the deleted workspace/edit_policy.py (both halves diffed), workflows/forge_loop/api.py, workflows/rewrite_controller/{forge_runner,worktree}.py, .importlinter (all 11 contracts), pyproject.toml (package-data, coverage omit, per-file-ignores), .gitleaks.toml, .github/scripts/forge_e2e_gate.py, docs/contributing/style-guide.md | Ran: stale-reference sweeps over the head tree for every old package name as a dotted module, as a path segment and unqualified (both clean); recomputed the two changed `Path(__file__)` depths; confirmed the merge of main resolves `_trace_shape_manifest.py` by deletion with no importer left and no old layout reference surviving | Base: 06b2b636782d66d57b8ca2a12b3ed472b3713ab9 | Head: b691ac0a0d3ae471995e764b14a3bbf777160110

issue.title: refactor(kernelforge): command lines only parse options; each workflow runs without click

labels.name: repo-214761c4
labels.description: Waives the PR diff budget; added by a maintainer with a reason in the PR description

issue.body:
- Description: what and why

  Fifth step of the kernelforge cleanup: separate the command lines from the workflows they start. Every workflow now has a request object and a run function that do not depend on click; `kernelforge/cli/` only parses options, builds the request, calls the run function, and turns its errors into click errors and exit codes. No module outside `cli/` imports click any more (six did on main).

  - **forge-loop runs without a command line.** The run moves out of `cli/forge_loop_command.py` (2000 lines; `forge_loop` alone was 257) into `loop/bootstrap/`: `run.py` holds the stages (`run_forge_loop` → open campaign → agent session → prepare → search → publish), and the pieces it is built from sit beside it -- `request.py` (`ForgeLoopRequest` and its option groups), `errors.py`, `run_context.py`, `reporter.py`, `warm_start.py`, `preparation.py`. `relay`, `lanes`, `publication`, `pr_references` and `session_budget` move from `cli/` unchanged. `loop/api.py` exports `ForgeLoopRequest` and `run_forge_loop(request, publish_result=...)`. The run raises `ForgeLoopError`, `ForgeLoopUsageError`, `InvalidOptionValue` and `TaskPreparationFailed` instead of click exceptions, and releases the workspace lock in a `finally` block instead of a click context callback.
  - **The other five commands move into `cli/`.** forge-fuse, gemm-tune, roofline-ceiling, kernel-rewrite-controller and export-runs each get a `cli/*_command.py`. Business modules that were named after a command are renamed for what they hold:
    - `fusion/command.py` → `fusion/pipeline.py`, with `fuse(request) -> FuseResult`. The request, the discovery stage and the harness-noise diagnostic move to `fusion/request.py`, `fusion/discovery_stage.py` and `fusion/harness_noise.py`, and the repo-root helpers move to `fusion/locate.py`.
    - `gemm_tune/cli.py` → `gemm_tune/pipeline.py`, with `run_tuning` and `plan_tuning`.
    - `roofline_ceiling/command.py` → `roofline_ceiling/standalone.py`, with `estimate_workspace_ceiling`.
  - They raise `FuseError` / `FuseUsageError`, `TuneError` / `TuneFailed` and `CeilingError`, and `cli/` translates them. `run_export` gains `write_document`, so the command no longer writes the files itself.
  - `option_groups.py` moves into `cli/`. The option dataclasses that forge-loop and forge-rewrite share (`GpuOptions`, `CeilingSwitch`, `AgentRuntimeOptions`, `agent_runtime_overrides`) move to `config.py`. `cli/__init__.py` imports and registers every command directly; the per-command `_register_*` helpers are gone.
  - `install.sh`'s gemm-tune readiness probe imports `kernelforge.gemm_tune.pipeline`. The coverage omit list names the two renamed pipeline modules. `loop/bootstrap/` was under the omitted `cli/*` and is now measured.

- Linked issue(s): none

- Tests: added/updated? commands run?
  - `test_cli_optional_registration.py` → `test_cli_registration.py`: every command is on the entry point. The removed cases tested that `_register_gemm_tune()` did not hide an import error; that helper no longer exists, and a failing import now fails `import kernelforge.cli` directly.
  - Tests that patched or inspected the old modules now target the modules the code lives in. Tests that asserted click exceptions from business functions now assert the domain errors. The source-order guards (PR context reaches only the implementer, the result is published before provenance, `commit_new_paths` comes from the campaign, tier 3 runs after the tuners) read the stage functions they now live in.
  - Run locally:
    - `ruff check` and `ruff format --check`.
    - `lint-imports`: 11 kept. The `acyclic` contract ignores no new non-test import.
    - The affected test directories and files: fusion, gemm_tune, roofline_ceiling, kernel_rewrite_controller, the forge-loop, relay, lane, KB, CLI, measurement and install-probe tests, all passing. `test_build_parallelism::test_no_ceiling_means_no_opinion` fails the same way on main.
    - `python scripts/code_metrics.py --base-ref origin/main`: PASSED.
    - Every command's `--help` output diffed against main: identical for all 10 commands and subcommands.
  - The full suite is left to CI.

- Size/complexity triggers crossed:
  - **Diff budget: 6215 production lines (limit 1000), which needs the `size-exception` label.** Almost all of it is code moving between modules, which the budget counts twice. It is one PR because the moves depend on each other: the business modules could not leave the click helpers until `option_groups` moved into `cli/`, and doing that alone created an import cycle through `cli/__init__`, which disappears only once the commands move too. Splitting the PR would land a broken `acyclic` contract in between.
  - Code metrics: nothing is new or worse. Improved: `forge_loop` (257 lines), fusion `run` (65), gemm `run` (58) and `_collect_pr_kb_context` (52) are now within the limit, and `forge_loop_command.py` (2000 lines) and `fusion/command.py` (1708 lines) are gone. The largest modules left are `fusion/pipeline.py` (1124 lines) and `loop/bootstrap/run.py` (837 lines).

- If this simplifies or refactors: no behaviour change for a well-formed run. Preserved contracts: command names, options, defaults and help text; exit codes (task-preparation failure exits 2 silently after publishing its result; a warm-start rollback failure exits 2; usage errors exit 2; other refusals exit 1; gemm-tune and forge-fuse codes are unchanged); error messages; the JSON each command prints.

- Observable effect:
  - An invalid `--agent-options-json` is refused while the options are parsed, before forge-loop takes the workspace lock. The message is the same as on main (`Invalid value for --agent-options-json: ...`, option name unquoted) and so is exit code 2.
  - forge-loop can run in process through `kernelforge.loop.api.run_forge_loop`.

- Breaking changes: internal only. Module paths change:
  - `kernelforge.cli.forge_loop_command` helpers → `kernelforge.loop.bootstrap.*`.
  - `kernelforge.cli.{relay,lanes,publication,pr_references,session_budget}` → `kernelforge.loop.bootstrap.*`.
  - `kernelforge.option_groups` → `kernelforge.cli.option_groups`.
  - `kernelforge.fusion.command` → `kernelforge.fusion.pipeline` / `.request` / `.discovery_stage` / `.harness_noise`.
  - `kernelforge.gemm_tune.cli` → `kernelforge.gemm_tune.pipeline` plus `kernelforge.cli.gemm_tune_command`.
  - `kernelforge.roofline_ceiling.command` → `kernelforge.roofline_ceiling.standalone`.

issue.title: refactor(kernelforge): hyperloom reaches kernelforge only through package interfaces
issue.body:
- Description: what and why

  Third step of the kernelforge cleanup, after #2245: with `gpu_arch` in `tools/`, `fusion → loop` no longer closes a cycle through `roofline_ceiling`, which lets this PR drop that acyclic baseline line.

  hyperloom reached into about twenty kernelforge modules by path, and the kernelforge workflows each carried their own forge-loop subprocess code: three built the argv, and the two that read its stdout result parsed it their own way. Both now go through declared interfaces.

  - **Package interfaces.** `gemm_tune`, `kernel_rewrite_controller`, `knowledge`, `tools` and `resources` declare what they offer in `__all__`; every hyperloom call site (`hosted/mcp_server.py`, `orchestrator/kernel/*`, `orchestrator/measurement/apply_verification.py`) imports those names from the package.
  - **`kernelforge.loop.api` — the one forge-loop entry for sibling workflows.** It owns the subprocess contract the workflows re-implemented: `forge_loop_command()` builds the argv that `fusion/campaign.py`, `rewrite_by_flydsl/optimize.py` and `kernel_rewrite_controller/forge_runner.py` each built (`python -m kernelforge.cli forge-loop …`, falling back to the `kernelforge` script), and `format_forge_loop_result()` / `parse_forge_loop_result()` own the `__FORGE_RESULT__` framing (last payload wins, malformed → `None`) that the two stdout readers, FlyDSL `optimize` and `forge_runner`, each parsed. Fusion shares only the argv builder; it still reads the `--result-json` file. It also re-exports the in-process names those workflows use (`BestResultPublisher`, `GateMeasurement`, path ownership, the implementer-session factory), so `fusion` and `rewrite_by_flydsl` no longer import loop internals. `cli/forge_loop_command.py` emits both of its result lines through `format_forge_loop_result`.
  - **`editable_repo` → `tools/`.** The repo lock and in-place check are used by `kernel_rewrite_controller` and `tools`, not by the loop.
  - **Gate.** New import-linter contract `kf-public-interfaces`: `hyperloom` may not import any kernelforge submodule other than `kernelforge.loop.api` (test code exempt). It lists every top-level kernelforge package, `run_export` (#2037) included. The `acyclic` baseline drops `kernelforge.fusion.shadow_repo -> kernelforge.loop.path_ownership`. Both are documented in `docs/contributing/style-guide.md`.

- Linked issue(s): none

- Tests: added/updated? commands run?
  - New `tests/loop/test_forge_loop_api.py` pins the argv prefix and its fallback, the format/parse round-trip, last-payload-wins, a missing result → `None` with no log, and a malformed one (invalid JSON, or a JSON array) → `None` with a warning.
  - `test_editable_repo*.py` move to `tests/tools/`. Patch targets follow the new lookup site: the `port_loop` tests patch `kernelforge.loop.api.make_agent_fn`, the `apply_verification` stub replaces `kernelforge.gemm_tune`. The two `_forge_loop_argv` tests are dropped with the helper; `forge_loop_command` covers them. The source-order check in `test_pr_kb_cli_wiring` (result emitted before provenance) matches the new emit call.
  - Run: `PYTHONPATH=src pytest -n 16 src/kernelforge src/hyperloom/orchestrator/kernel src/hyperloom/orchestrator/measurement src/hyperloom/hosted` (7171 passed; the 14 failures — `test_rocpc_profile_discovery` x2, `test_build_parallelism`, `test_revert_kernel_patch_containment`'s bytecode case and 10 in `hosted/tests/test_entry.py` — fail the same way without this change in this environment), `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `lint-imports` (11 kept; a probe import of `kernelforge.gemm_tune.router` from hyperloom breaks the new contract as intended), `python scripts/code_metrics.py --base-ref origin/main` (PASSED; three function-length baselines tightened or removed).

- Size/complexity triggers crossed: none.

- If this simplifies or refactors: removes three copies of the forge-loop argv builder (`_forge_loop_argv` in fusion and FlyDSL, the inline one in `forge_runner`), two result-sentinel constants and the FlyDSL result regex. Preserved contracts: the `__FORGE_RESULT__{json}__FORGE_RESULT__` stdout line forge-loop prints, the argv fusion and FlyDSL build, and the behaviour of every name hyperloom imports. The two stdout readers (FlyDSL `optimize` and `forge_runner`) did not agree on how to read that line; they now share one reading, listed below.

- Observable effect:
  - `rewrite_by_flydsl/optimize.py`, when it falls back to the stdout result, reads the **last** result block instead of the first, and rejects a payload that is not a JSON object (it used to accept an array). This is how `kernel_rewrite_controller/forge_runner.py` already read it. forge-loop prints one block per run, so no run reads a different result today; where the sentinel literal appears earlier in the output (the capabilities JSON carries `"result_sentinel"`), the last block is the real one and the first was not.
  - A result block that is not valid JSON, or is JSON but not an object, logs a WARNING from `kernelforge.loop.api` for both stdout readers (FlyDSL `optimize` and `forge_runner`). FlyDSL logged this before under its own message; `forge_runner` logged nothing. Fusion reads the `--result-json` file, not stdout, and is unaffected. A missing result stays silent, and FlyDSL's "no trusted forge-loop result" warning is unchanged.
  - `forge_runner` builds its argv with `forge_loop_command`, so when `sys.executable` is empty it runs the `kernelforge` console script instead of an empty program name. Fusion and FlyDSL already did this.
  - A hyperloom import of a kernelforge internal module now fails `lint-imports`.

- Breaking changes: no for supported interfaces. Internal import path `kernelforge.loop.editable_repo` → `kernelforge.tools.editable_repo`; nothing outside kernelforge imported it. hyperloom call sites switch to package imports in this PR.

- PR addresses single concern: yes — kernelforge's consumers go through declared interfaces.

- Root cause is upstream: n/a

issue.title: [MoE][gfx950] Pick the fp8_w8a8 default tile by routed rows per expert
issue.body:
## Motivation

On MI355X (gfx950) there are no tuned Triton fused-MoE config files, so every fp8_w8a8 per-channel / per-tensor MoE that runs through Triton uses `get_default_config`. That covers `--quantization w8a8_fp8`, Gemma4 FP8, and FP8 MoE with AITER off. The default branches only on `M` vs `E`:

```python
config = {"BLOCK_SIZE_M": 128, "BLOCK_SIZE_N": 256, "BLOCK_SIZE_K": 128, "GROUP_SIZE_M": 32, "num_warps": 8, ...}
if M <= E:
    config = {"BLOCK_SIZE_M": 64, "BLOCK_SIZE_N": 128, "BLOCK_SIZE_K": 128, "GROUP_SIZE_M": 1, "num_warps": 4, ...}
```

`BLOCK_SIZE_M` is also the `moe_align_block_size` alignment: every touched expert is padded to a whole block, and padded blocks still run the full K loop. What matters is therefore the number of rows each expert receives, `M * topk / E`, which this rule never looks at.

## Modifications

On gfx950 only, the fp8_w8a8 (no block quant) default picks the tile by routed rows per expert:

| `M * topk / E` | BLOCK_M | BLOCK_N | BLOCK_K | warps | stages |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| < 8 | 16 | 64 | 128 | 4 | 2 |
| 8 – 24 | 32 | 128 | 128 | 4 | 2 |
| 24 – 48 | 64 | 128 | 128 | 4 | 3 |
| ≥ 48 | 128 | 128 | 128 | 8 | 2 |

`BLOCK_SIZE_K` stays 128, as in both branches it replaces, so the K reduction order is unchanged and the output is bit-identical. Other architectures, block-wise fp8, tuned config files and deterministic inference are untouched. No new environment variable.

The tiers were selected from a sweep of 48 tiles (`BLOCK_M` {16, 32, 64, 128} × `BLOCK_N` {64, 128, 256} × warps {4, 8} × stages {2, 3}, `BLOCK_K` = 128) on three MoE shapes × 14 batch sizes, maximizing the worst-case speedup over the current default and then the geometric mean.

## Accuracy Tests

- Outputs are bit-identical to `main` (`torch.equal`) at all 88 shape × batch points below.
- New `test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_fused_moe_default_config.py` (CPU): tier boundaries, `BLOCK_SIZE_K` = 128 in every tier, and unchanged defaults off gfx950 and for block-wise quant.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.0, torch 2.9.1, Triton 3.7.0. `fused_moe` with `use_fp8_w8a8=True, per_channel_quant=True`, `triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph`, minimum of 3; `main` and this PR run in separate processes. This run is independent of the sweep, uses 22 batch sizes (most of them not in the sweep), and adds a shape that was not used to select the tiers.

| Shape (E, top_k, N, K) | Geomean speedup over 22 batch sizes | Worst point |
|---|---|---|
| Gemma4 (128, 8, 704, 2816) | 1.074x | 0.995x (M=96) |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (256, 8, 512, 2048) | 1.050x | 1.000x |
| Qwen3-Next-80B (512, 10, 512, 2048) | 1.049x | 1.011x |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B (128, 8, 768, 2048), not used for selection | 1.056x | 0.993x (M=96) |

Selected points (µs, `main` → this PR):

| M | Gemma4 | Qwen3-30B-A3B (held out) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 35.2 → 32.6 (1.08x) | 31.4 → 29.1 (1.08x) |
| 8 | 65.2 → 61.0 (1.07x) | 57.5 → 53.4 (1.08x) |
| 32 | 132.3 → 127.6 (1.04x) | 107.2 → 104.6 (1.03x) |
| 128 | 153.5 → 153.1 (1.00x) | 123.0 → 122.3 (1.01x) |
| 256 | 194.3 → 163.6 (1.19x) | 145.7 → 128.5 (1.13x) |
| 512 | 212.3 → 184.1 (1.15x) | 160.3 → 144.3 (1.11x) |
| 1024 | 243.2 → 225.6 (1.08x) | 190.0 → 182.6 (1.04x) |
| 4096 | 595.6 → 553.6 (1.08x) | 453.2 → 411.6 (1.10x) |

Only gfx950 was measured, so the change is gated to it. Tuned MI355X config files, if added later, still take precedence over this default.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not needed.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

comment.body: Closing. The change only reaches non-block-wise fp8_w8a8 MoE on gfx950 that runs through the Triton default config, which in the default ROCm setup (SGLANG_USE_AITER=1) means per-tensor ModelOpt / Quark / compressed-tensors checkpoints; the common block-wise FP8 checkpoints are unaffected. Measured end to end on MI355X with amd/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507-FP8, the gain is about 2-3% decode throughput at low concurrency and under 2% elsewhere, which does not justify a gfx950-specific hand-tuned tile table in the shared default config.

- Description: what and why

  Fourth step of the kernelforge cleanup: two foundation layers depended upward on the packages built on them. Independent of #2247.

  - **`Config` is plain data.** It resolved its own agent runtime: `__post_init__` checked provider names against the `agent_backends` registry, and `agent_runtime()`, `agent_runtime_for()` and `agent_runtime_settings()` lived on the dataclass. They move to `kernelforge.agent_backends.runtime` as functions of a `Config`; the 16 call sites switch, and the provider names are checked where the runtime is resolved. `KnowledgeConfig` and `KnowledgeStoreMode` -- pure data the `Config` embeds -- move from `knowledge.kb_store.config` into `kernelforge.config`; `knowledge_config_from_runtime` stays in knowledge. `import kernelforge.config` now loads only `kernelforge.resources`.
  - **The workspace guard enforces its caller's rules.** `agent_backends.workspace_guard` imported Forge's protected-path rules (`workspace.edit_policy`) and the loop's new-file allowlist, so every provider session -- fusion, FlyDSL, the rewrite controller, roofline, gemm-tune tier 3 -- was held to forge-loop's list without saying so. The matching mechanism moves to `tools.protected_paths.ProtectedPathRules`, with the rules as data; Forge's rules are `edit_policy.FORGE_PROTECTED_PATHS` (same globs, directories and skipped bookkeeping), and `is_protected_path` / `protected_path_inventory` callers use it. The allowlist matcher moves from `loop/new_path_allowlist.py` to `tools/`. `AgentRunSpec` gains `protected_path_rules`; the ten places that build a session reaching the guard (nine writable sessions and the orchestration read-only resume) pass `FORGE_PROTECTED_PATHS` explicitly, and a writable session without rules is refused in `prepare()` before anything is snapshotted, as a `WorkspaceSafetyError` that is non-retryable and not counted as the agent's safety rejection.
  - The `acyclic` baseline loses `agent_backends.workspace_guard -> loop.new_path_allowlist` and `knowledge.kb_store.recipe -> config`, both gone with the imports above.
  - **Units the wiring grew give up a self-contained piece.** Passing the rules grew seven functions and modules that were already over the code-metrics limits by 1–3 lines each. Rather than raise their baseline, each moves out a piece that stands on its own (moved classes, prompts and hooks verbatim; the extracted functions behave as the code they replace): `AnalysisProtection` (the hooks and snapshot restore that keep an Analysis session in its staging root) to `orchestrator/analysis_protection.py`, and the session spec to `AnalysisAgentService._session_spec`; the round-partition prompts to `orchestrator/plan_prompts.py` beside the other planning prompts; `PrepareAudit` to `loop/task_preparer_audit.py`; the fusion author's edit-tool hook to `fusion/author_hooks.py`; `_session_cwd` out of the implementer's `agent_fn`; `_outcome` out of `generate_tuner`. `WorkspaceGuard.prepare` drops its explicit rules check, since the protected inventory it builds refuses a spec without rules before anything changes. Every one of those baselines goes down (for example `analysis.py` 1955 → 1815 lines, `_run_analysis_session` 81 → 59).

- Linked issue(s): none

- Tests: added/updated? commands run?
  - New `tests/test_workspace_guard_rules.py`: a writable session without rules is refused before it starts (not retryable, not an agent rejection); a read-only session needs none; the guard protects what the caller's rules name and nothing of Forge's beyond them.
  - New `test_provider_registry` case: an unregistered provider or fallback is refused when the runtime is resolved. Spec-capture tests for task preparation, the implementer session and the rewrite-controller analysis now assert they carry `FORGE_PROTECTED_PATHS`.
  - Tests that stubbed `config.agent_runtime` now patch `agent_runtime` where it is looked up; tests that build a guarded session pass the rules; `test_workspace_policy` exercises `FORGE_PROTECTED_PATHS`.
  - Run locally: `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `lint-imports` (10 kept), and the 26 affected test files and directories (agent backends, guard, provider registry, config and knowledge, tools, loop, roofline, rewrite controller, fusion author -- 1952 passed), then for the extraction commit the analysis, orchestration, task-preparer, fusion and gemm-tune tests (2145 passed; `test_build_parallelism::test_no_ceiling_means_no_opinion` fails the same way without this change), and `python scripts/code_metrics.py` against the merge base (PASSED). The full suite is left to CI.

- Size/complexity triggers crossed: none; every touched unit is at or below its baseline.

- If this simplifies or refactors: no behaviour change for a well-formed run. Preserved contracts: every session protects the same paths (`FORGE_PROTECTED_PATHS` is the former default list), the runtime each call site resolves, and the KB configuration parsing.

- Observable effect:
  - An unknown `FORGE_AGENT_BACKEND` or fallback provider is reported when a session's runtime is resolved, with the same "unknown agent provider" message, instead of when `Config` is built. forge-loop resolves it during setup, before the first session.
  - A third-party caller that builds a writable `AgentRunSpec` and runs it through a built-in provider must now pass `protected_path_rules`; without it the session is refused with a message naming the field.

- Breaking changes: internal only. `Config.agent_runtime*()` → `kernelforge.agent_backends.runtime`; `kernelforge.knowledge.kb_store.config.KnowledgeConfig` / `KnowledgeStoreMode` → `kernelforge.config` (dropped from `kernelforge.knowledge`'s exports; nothing imported them from there); `workspace.edit_policy.is_protected_path` / `protected_path_inventory` → `FORGE_PROTECTED_PATHS.is_protected` / `.inventory`; `kernelforge.loop.new_path_allowlist` → `kernelforge.tools.new_path_allowlist`. hyperloom imports none of them. The `kernelforge.agent_providers` plugin interface is unchanged.

- PR addresses single concern: yes -- foundation layers stop depending on the layers above them.

- Root cause is upstream: n/a

issue.title: [MiniMax] Key sparse-decode autotune on real kernel args; skip the one-chunk merge
issue.body:
## Motivation

Two small issues in the MiniMax-M3 sparse decode launcher (`minimax_sparse/decode/topk_sparse.py`):

1. The autotune key of `_gqa_share_sparse_decode_kernel` lists `"block_size"`, which is not a kernel argument (the kernel takes `BLOCK_SIZE_N`). Triton's `Autotuner.run` keeps only key names that are kernel arguments (`[_args[key] for key in self.keys if key in _args]`), so the entry is silently dropped. `PAGED_CONTIG` is not in the key either. Both select different compiled kernels, so a config tuned for one block size or KV layout is reused for another. Within one serving process both are fixed today, so this does not change current results; it does when they vary in one process (tests, multiple models).
2. When `NUM_TOPK_CHUNKS == 1` the merge kernel still launches, although merging one chunk is an identity: `weights = exp(lse - lse) / 1 = 1`. With one KV head per rank (MiniMax-M3 at TP4 and TP8) this is every decode step at batch size > 128.

## Modifications

- Key on `BLOCK_SIZE_N` and `PAGED_CONTIG` instead of the nonexistent `block_size`. Tensor dtypes (bf16 vs fp8 KV) were already part of the key through Triton's automatic dtype entries.
- Return the single chunk directly when `NUM_TOPK_CHUNKS == 1`.

## Accuracy Tests

New `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_minimax_sparse_decode_chunks.py` compares the kernel with a torch fp32 reference at the per-rank MiniMax-M3 shape (16 q heads, 1 KV head, head_dim 128, block 128, top-16), at batch 4 (several chunks, merge runs) and batch 256 (one chunk, merge skipped). Registered for CUDA (`base-b-kernel-unit`, next to the sibling tests) and AMD (`stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd`). 2 passed on MI355X.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.0, torch 2.9.1, Triton 3.7.0. One `flash_decode_with_gqa_share_sparse` call at the TP4 per-rank shape, 8k context, page size 128; `triton.testing.do_bench` median, minimum of 5 repetitions:

| Batch | Chunks | `main` (µs) | This PR (µs) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | 8 | 53.3 | 53.0 |
| 64 | 4 | 49.6 | 49.0 |
| 128 | 2 | 62.1 | 62.0 |
| 256 | 1 | 98.5 | 95.6 |
| 512 | 1 | 154.6 | 149.4 |

About 3% per sparse layer once the batch has a single chunk (57 sparse layers in MiniMax-M3); no change below that, as expected.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not needed.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

issue.title: [Fix] [AMD] aiter: Fix garbage decode output with unified attention at page size 1 under CUDA graph
issue.body:
## Motivation

With `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1` on a dense (non-sliding-window) model at the default page size 1, decode produces garbage output when CUDA graph is on (GSM8K 0.00 on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; 0.76 with `--disable-cuda-graph`).

In the CUDA-graph decode metadata, the unified-attention page table is copied into the captured `cuda_graph_page_table` only for sliding-window pools or `page_size > 1`. At page size 1 nothing is copied, so `unified_attention` reads an all-zero page table. Sliding-window models and Qwen3-VL (which gets page size 16 from its model override) are not affected.

## Modifications

- `aiter_backend.py`: copy the page table for every non-sliding-window configuration. `_transform_table_1_to_real` is the identity at page size 1, so the `page_size > 1` condition only skipped the copy.
- New AMD CI test `test/registered/amd/test_aiter_unified_attention_page_size_1.py`: GSM8K on the default test model with unified attention at page size 1.

## Accuracy Tests

MI325X (gfx942), single GPU, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, `--attention-backend aiter`, GSM8K 200 questions, CUDA graph on, 3 runs each.

Main does not start in the current ROCm image (sgl-kernel mismatch), so these runs use the image's sglang (`dc6b5d1f5a`) with the identical one-line patch; the page-table code is the same on main.

| Configuration | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| unified attention, page size 1 | 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.00 | 0.76 / 0.76 / 0.77 |
| default decode (reference) | 0.765 / 0.76 / 0.76 | — |

The new CI test: 0.76 on the patched build (threshold 0.65), 0.00 on the unpatched build.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No change for other configurations. For reference, unified attention at page size 1 is now correct but much slower than at page size 16, because the kernel gathers KV one token per block; page size 16 remains the recommended setting.

MI325X, `sglang.bench_serving`, random input 2048 / output 256, CUDA graph on, unified attention, patched build:

| 16 | 32 | 885.03 | 10.72 | 2260.3 |

issue.title: [DSV4] Split-K fallback when the decode grid cannot fill the CU array
issue.body:
## Problem

The non-split-K dual-scope DSV4 decode kernel launches a grid of
`(cdiv(h_q, BLOCK_H), total_tokens)`. `_prune_dual_scope_configs` pins
`BLOCK_H = 16` whenever `h_q <= 64`, so on a TP-sharded decode the H dimension
collapses to a single block:

* DSV4 at TP4: `h_q = 64 / 4 = 16` → `cdiv(16, 16) == 1`
* grid degenerates to `(1, total_tokens)`

At batch 64 on a 256-CU MI355X that is **64 workgroups — 25% CU occupancy**, idle
by construction no matter how well the kernel body is tuned.

`_decide_splitk_dual_scope` does not rescue it: it enables split-K only for small
batches (`<= 8`), very large topk (`>= 2048`), or `h_q > 64`. A mid-batch,
moderate-topk decode (`total_tokens=64, h_q=16, total_topk=512`) falls through
every branch — note `use_splitk_for_large_topk` tests `total_tokens > 64`, so batch
**exactly** 64 misses it — and returns 0.

## Change

Add an occupancy-driven fallback: when the base grid cannot fill the CU array,
split the topk dimension until it can.

* Only converts a `return 0` into split-K. Every shape the existing heuristics
  already handle is untouched.
* Restricted to the supported factors (2, 4, 8) — the combine stage implements
  exactly those and raises `ValueError` otherwise.
* Each split keeps at least one full `BLOCK_N=64` tile of KV work, so the combine
  kernel and partial-buffer traffic stay amortised.

`SGLANG_DSV4_DECODE_SPLITK` = `auto` (default) / `off` / `2` / `4` / `8`, scoped to
this fallback only — the original heuristics and the `force_no_splitk` prefill path
are not affected.

## Verification

**Not benchmarked.** The occupancy arithmetic is checkable from the launch shape
and the `total_tokens > 64` off-by-one is visible in the source, so I am confident
the *gap* is real. That splitting actually wins there is not established: split-K
buys parallelism at the cost of fp32 partial buffers plus a reduce pass, and where
that pays off is hardware-specific.

`auto` is the default, so if it loses this is a regression rather than a no-op.
Sweep `SGLANG_DSV4_DECODE_SPLITK` over {off, 2, 4, 8} at batch 16/32/64/128 before
merging, and consider defaulting to `off` until that exists.

## House-rule note

`SGLANG_DSV4_DECODE_SPLITK` is registered as an `EnvStr` in `environ.py` per
`.claude/skills/env-var-conventions` rather than read through `os.environ`, which is
how the original patch had it.

## Related

A sibling agent session produced a near-identical fallback in the same file
(`001_dsv4_decode_splitk_occupancy.diff`, kept in `scratch/`) with a slightly
different occupancy formula and an extra `total_tokens <= 256` prefill guard. Same
diagnosis, so only this one is submitted.

---

(hyperloom session `20260813T091422Z`, model `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`).*

The Triton DSV4 decode kernel is only used on ROCm when SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=triton is set; the default backend is aiter_sparse on gfx950 and tilelang elsewhere, so this fallback is effectively unreachable in default deployments. If Triton becomes a default DSV4 decode path on ROCm, the occupancy gap should be addressed in the existing split-K heuristic on current main, backed by a batch 16/32/64/128 sweep.

issue.title: [MoE] Route w8a8_fp8 MoE through the AITER runner on ROCm
issue.body:
## Summary

Route `w8a8_fp8` MoE through the AITER runner on ROCm, instead of always building a
`TritonMoeQuantInfo`.

## Why

`W8A8Fp8MoEMethod` constructs its runner unconditionally for Triton, so on ROCm with
AITER enabled the fused-MoE path is unavailable to `--quantization w8a8_fp8` even
where the AITER kernels exist and the rest of the stack is using them. The backend
selection this adds mirrors the auto-selection rule the MXFP4 method already uses.

## Verification

**Not tested.** No GPU or Python interpreter here.

The structural gap — one method resolving a runner backend, the other hardcoding it —
is checkable and I checked it. What is not established is that the AITER w8a8_fp8
MoE kernels produce equivalent output for these weights: this changes which kernel
family executes the MoE, so it is an output-affecting change and wants an accuracy
run, not just a smoke test.

## Related

Three other agent sessions produced variants of this (one targeting a
`/sgl-workspace/`-prefixed path that does not exist, one adding a separate
`_moe_runner_backend_bridge` helper). Only this one is submitted.

`gemma-4-26B-A4B-it`).*

On ROCm with SGLANG_USE_AITER=1, per-channel FP8 MoE checkpoints already reach the AITER runner through the compressed-tensors path when --quantization w8a8_fp8 is not passed, so this change only affects users who add that flag explicitly. If w8a8_fp8 MoE on AITER is needed later, it should reuse SGLANG_USE_AITER and the compressed-tensors routing rule instead.

issue.title: feat(forge): cut Claude session token spend: cached lesson resumes, no title calls, streamed thinking, shared lane prefix
issue.body:
## What this saves

Measured on one 12 h `forge-loop` campaign (AgentKernelArena `Aiter-task/gemm_a16w16_nt_n1024_k4096`, MI325X, claude-opus-5, 3 lanes). Every figure is priced from the campaign's Claude Code transcripts (per-request `usage`, Opus 5 list prices) and attributed per request; the campaign cost **$187.76** for 4 KEEPs.

| Change | Tokens / spend saved per campaign | Time saved |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No Claude Code session-title call | **$15.11 (8.0%)**: one uncached resend of every session's first prompt (73 sessions, 70–180k tokens each for planning roles) | — |
| Summarized thinking display | **up to $8.30 (4.4%)** of prompt-cache rewrites after retried requests ($6.31) and cut-off streams ($1.99) | **221 min of critical-path waiting** (305 min across sessions) in 55 failed request attempts; R4 and R5 synthesis each ran into the 60 min session limit; **3 lane plans** were lost |
| Lane syntheses share one cached prefix | **≈ $4.0 (2.1%)**: sibling lanes read ~98% of their first prompt (≈70k tokens) instead of writing it | siblings start ~20 s after the first lane (at most 120 s) |
| Lesson summary keeps the cached prefix | **≈ $1.8 (1.0%)**: two summaries rewrote 168k / 188k-token prefixes | — |

Together about **$29 (≈16%) of the campaign's priced spend**, and most of the planning time that was lost to the gateway.

Not counted above: the 55 failed attempts have no `usage` in the transcripts, so they are not in the $187.76. If the gateway bills tokens of aborted requests (each thought for ~6 minutes before it was cut), the real saving from the thinking fix is larger; the gateway's own billing would have to confirm that.

At a fixed wall-clock budget the recovered time and lane plans buy more search rather than a smaller bill, so the effect shows as more candidates per campaign and a lower cost per KEEP.

## Description

Four changes to how Forge runs Claude-backed sessions, plus the review fixes.

**1. Lesson summary resumes on the Implementer's cached prefix** (`b993bd613`, `2abefb115`)
The summarizer resumed the Implementer session with its own system prompt and a read-only tool set. Both sit in the cached prefix (tools, then system), so every summary rewrote the whole session context. The Claude backend refuses every built-in tool a spec describes but its `tool_policy` does not allow with a **PreToolUse deny hook**. The hook runs before any permission mode (including an operator's `--agent-options-json` `permission_mode`) and before any settings `permissions.allow` rule, and it leaves the tool definitions, and so the cached prefix, untouched. `disallowed_tools` was tried and rejected: it removes the tools from the definitions, which changes the request shape and loses the cache.
