issue.body:
The repository has many stale remote branches. `delete_branch_on_merge` is on and works, but it only fires when a PR merges. A closed PR, or a branch that never had a PR, keeps its branch.

**Already cleaned up (2026-10-23).** 40 branches are deleted. Every deleted SHA is recorded, so any of them can be restored; for a closed PR, use the PR page's "Restore branch" button.
- 34 branches whose PR was closed without merging more than 30 days ago, with no commits after the close.
- 6 merged branches that came back after their PR merged: #1163, #1402, #1840, #1404 and #1405 were re-pushed, and #1495 was restored. All of their extra commits are already on main.

**Please confirm by 2026-10-30.** These branches never had a PR and have had no commit for over 30 days. Release and docs branches are excluded. If you still need one, comment here or open a PR from it. Anything unclaimed by 2026-10-30 will be deleted, and its SHA is listed so it can be recreated.

issue.title: refactor(kernelforge): dissolve kernelforge.llm into the packages that own its modules
issue.body:
- Description: what and why

  `kernelforge.llm` held four modules, and only one of them is about an LLM. The package name sent readers to the wrong place (`from kernelforge.llm.git import git` is a git wrapper). Each module now lives with the package that owns its concern:

  | Module | New home | Why there |
  |:--|:--|:--|
  | `llm/gateway.py` | `agent_backends/gateway.py` | Resolves the endpoint, credential and headers the Claude and Codex backends call |
  | `llm/git.py` | `tools/git.py` | Technical helper with no kernelforge dependency |
  | `llm/process_reaping.py` | `tools/process_reaping.py` | Technical helper with no kernelforge dependency, beside `tools/process_group.py` |
  | `llm/workspace_policy.py` | `workspace/edit_policy.py` | Which paths a candidate may not touch is a policy, and `tools/` excludes policy by its own charter ("no product or evaluation policy"), so this starts a `workspace` package |

  `workspace` depends only on `tools`. The other workspace rules that are scattered today (`loop/new_path_allowlist.py`, `loop/path_ownership.py`, `loop/editable_repo.py`) can join it in a follow-up.

  Every import moves to the new path, and nothing re-exports the old one.

- Linked issue(s): none

- Tests: added/updated? commands run?

  - Updated: test imports and `monkeypatch` targets follow the moved modules. No assertion changed.
  - Added: `test_rename_completeness::test_no_stray_llm_package_references`. Following the guard this file already keeps for earlier package moves, it fails on any `kernelforge.llm` / `kernelforge/llm` reference. The one exemption is the historical record in `.claude/skills/review-pr/rules.md`, which cites the path a past PR added.

Apart from the added test, no case is failing here that does not fail on `main`:

issue.body:
## Description

Adds `speculative_decoding_specialist`, a specialist domain Orchestration may delegate to when decode is memory-bound with idle compute — small batch, or long context where decode attention streams the whole KV cache every step — judged from the session's profiling and roofline evidence.

Until now speculative decoding only reached a run through the operator's base launch args, ATOM's `atom_mtp_{1,3}` seed variants, or a freeform dispatch that happened to think of it; no specialist knew when it fits, which method fits where, or where drafter weights come from.

The focus prompt (`orchestrator/prompts/speculative_decoding_focus.py`) covers:

- **When it fits:** memory-bound decode (small batch / long context); not when decode is already compute-bound, the run is prefill-dominated, or drafter memory costs more batch than acceptance gives back. The specialist judges this from the profiling and roofline evidence it already receives.
- **Where each method fits:** MTP, EAGLE / EAGLE-3, block drafters (DFlash / DSpark), a separate draft model, Medusa, and context copying (n-gram / suffix — never on the synthetic benchmark, where the existing refusal already blocks it).
- **Method order and drafter weights:** MTP first. The focus states the MTP layer count read from the target's `config.json` (or that there is none, or that the session's summary does not record one); the specialist still confirms the weight index carries those tensors, since some quantized or converted checkpoints keep the config field but drop the weights, and tensor naming differs per model family. Drafter-based methods look for weights trained for this exact target locally — next to the target and in the Hugging Face cache — before downloading one from Hugging Face (safetensors only, no `trust_remote_code`, revision pinned, repo id + sha recorded). Downloads go to the Hugging Face cache by default; any other location must outlive the dispatch (not the worktree or workspace, since every later benchmark launch of the proposal loads the drafter from that path), be passed as an absolute path, and sit on the shared filesystem on multi-node runs.
- **No framework flags in the prompt:** flag names, config keys and environment variables change between framework versions, so the focus describes methods and constraints generically and has the specialist take every flag from the installed framework's source. (A probe on SGLang 0.5.18 showed why: the vLLM memory flag an earlier draft named would have aborted the launch.)
- **Constraints:** the focus tells the specialist to follow four rules — keep a pinned draft when the base simulates acceptance, never switch to simulated acceptance, enable speculative decoding in one atomic proposal together with the paired memory change, and pass drafter weights as an absolute path (on the shared filesystem on multi-node runs). The runner enforces only the first two (`refuse_unpinned_speculative_change`), plus the existing n-gram / suffix refusal on the synthetic benchmark; nothing checks the memory pairing or the drafter path.

Supporting changes:

- The target model reaches the focus from the state that owns it. `warm_specialist_params` exports `SharedState.model_name` / `model_path` through `_STATE_PARAMS` into `SpecialistPromptInputs.model_name` / `model_path`; only the speculative-decoding focus renders them, so every other domain's prompt is unchanged. When neither is recorded, the focus tells the specialist to identify the target from the serving configuration.
- `summarize_model_config` always reports `mtp_layers` (from `num_nextn_predict_layers`, `mtp_num_hidden_layers` or `num_mtp_modules`; 0 when none), and `warm_specialist_params` passes `model_info` to the speculative decoding domain as it already did for static recon. A `model_info` without the key — an unreadable `config.json`, or a summary written before this change and kept on resume — makes the focus ask the specialist to read the count from `config.json` instead of reporting no MTP.
- `warm_specialist_params` resolves the domain with `dispatch_domain`, as the runner does, so a tags-only dispatch (the delegate shape `orchestration.md` teaches) or one whose domain is backfilled from a gap's KB-anchor `domain_hint` is warmed for the domain it runs as.
- Specialist subprocesses inherit `HF_HOME`, `HF_HUB_CACHE`, `HF_HUB_OFFLINE`, `HF_ENDPOINT` (non-secret). `HF_TOKEN` is not forwarded, but `huggingface_hub` still uses a login stored under `HF_HOME`, so where the operator has logged in, a specialist download authenticates as the operator.
- New knowledge anchor `speculative_decoding`; `orchestration.md` routes memory-bound decode to the domain; `specialist.md` lists the tag.

No deterministic trigger is added, by design: whether decode is memory-bound is a judgment over profiling and roofline evidence, which Orchestration already makes when it picks a domain. The existing stalled-domain forcing applies to the domain once an open gap is tagged for it. In an end-to-end `optimize` run (Llama-3.1-8B, 1 × MI325X, SGLang), Orchestration delegated to the domain 5 times on its own, and research scout opened a gap tagged `speculative_decoding`. Several of those 5 delegations were duplicates of a still-queued task, a pre-existing scheduling issue tracked in [#2027](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom/issues/2027) and fixed in [#2041](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom/pull/2041).

## Linked issue(s)

None.

## Tests

- New `test_speculative_decoding_specialist.py` (assertions on whitespace-normalised text, so reflowing the prompt does not break them):
  - the gate admits a delegate to the domain under its own anchor;
  - the focus names the target model, or sends the specialist to the serving configuration when none is recorded;
  - the MTP step for each case: N layers declared (with the tensor check), none declared, count not recorded (config unreadable, or a summary that predates `mtp_layers`);
  - local before download; the download rules (Hugging Face cache by default, a location that outlives the dispatch, safetensors only, no `trust_remote_code`, revision pinned);
  - the focus names no framework flag, config key or environment variable, and a patch-mode dispatch gets no altitude coda about flags it never listed (the domain is not in `_THROUGHPUT_AUTHORING_DOMAINS`);
  - end to end, the session's model name, path and `model_info` flow through `warm_specialist_params` and `SpecialistRunner._prepare` into the system prompt for every dispatch shape: `domain` key, tag key, KB-anchor tag, and a domain backfilled from a gap's `domain_hint`.
- `test_model_config_summary.py`: `mtp_layers` under each of the three field names (top level and nested `text_config`), and 0 when the config declares none or omits the field.
- `test_specialist_subprocess.py`: HF Hub settings are forwarded, `HF_TOKEN` is not.
- Updated the catalogue pins in `test_custom_specialist.py` (emit-hint domain list, knowledge-domain tags).
- On the branch merged with current main: 1198 tests across every suite touching `model_info`, `warm_specialist_params`, `summarize_model_config`, static recon, `SpecialistPromptInputs` or speculative decoding — all pass. With `warm_specialist_params` reverted to the raw `domain` check, the end-to-end test fails for the tag-key, KB-anchor-tag and gap-backfill shapes.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `lint-imports` clean.

## Size/complexity triggers crossed

The new focus text lives in its own module (180 lines, every function under the limits) so the large modules only get wiring. Units already above their limits still grow by the wiring a new domain needs; this needs the `baseline-raise` label:

| Unit | main | this PR | Why it grows |
|---|---|---|---|
| `orchestrator/prompts/specialist_prompt_builder.py` (module) | 2557 | 2568 | import, adapter and focus-registry entry, the `model_name` / `model_path` inputs, one line in the throughput-set comment |
| `orchestrator/specialists/subprocess_.py` (module) | 1737 | 1742 | four HF names in the specialist env allowlist |
| `orchestrator/specialists/runner.py` (module) / `SpecialistRunner._prepare` | 1455 / 193 | 1457 / 195 | `model_name` / `model_path` copied into the prompt inputs |
| `SpecialistDispatchCollaborator.warm_specialist_params` | 170 | 172 | the domain resolved with `dispatch_domain` instead of read raw |

`dispatch.py` (1012 → 1019) and `model_config_utils.py` (610 → 614) stay under the module failure limit; `cli/__init__.py` and `cli/bootstrap.py` are unchanged.

The alternative is extracting unrelated code out of these modules in this PR, which would mix a refactor into a feature; I would rather do that split as its own change. Line counts were measured by hand against main at 43712699b; complexity and duplication (jscpd, no Node locally) were not run locally and are left to the CI gate.

## Refactor / simplification

Not a refactor.

## Observable effect

- Orchestration's specialist emit list offers `speculative_decoding_specialist`, and its domain-selection rules route memory-bound decode to it. A dispatched specialist proposes enabling or tuning speculative decoding as benchable variants, and may download a matching drafter from Hugging Face when none is available locally.
- `SharedState.model_info` now also holds `mtp_layers` (0 for a model without MTP). Prompt and predictor consumers read named keys and are unchanged; the breakdown export's verbatim `model_info` section gains the key.
- Every specialist's params now carry `model_name` / `model_path` from `SharedState`; only the speculative-decoding focus renders them.
- A tags-only or gap-backfilled dispatch to `static_recon_specialist` now also receives `model_info`; the coordinator's own static-recon dispatch names `domain` and already did.
- Specialist subprocesses now see `HF_HOME`, `HF_HUB_CACHE`, `HF_HUB_OFFLINE` and `HF_ENDPOINT`: previously they could not find a Hugging Face cache outside `~/.cache/huggingface`, ignored an operator's offline setting, and could not download through a configured mirror. `HF_TOKEN` is still not forwarded; a login stored under `HF_HOME` is still used, and forwarding `HF_HOME` makes one stored under a non-default `HF_HOME` reachable.
- Previously no specialist owned speculative decoding, so outside ATOM's MTP seeds it was explored only if the operator configured it or a freeform dispatch happened to propose it.

## Breaking changes

No.

## PR addresses single concern

Yes — the speculative decoding specialist and the inputs it needs (target model identity, HF Hub settings).

## Root cause is upstream

No.

issue.title: [AITER] Quantize q with its own dynamic scale, not the KV cache k_scale
issue.body:
## Problem

On the AITER unified-attention path, when the KV cache is fp8 the query is quantized
to fp8 using the **KV cache's** `k_scale`:

```python
q_descale = layer.k_scale if layer.k_scale is not None else self.k_scale
q, _ = scaled_fp8_quant(q, q_descale)
```

`k_scale` is calibrated for the K cache's dynamic range. Query activations have a
different range. Using one as the other clips and distorts `q`.

This is the root cause of the accuracy drop observed with
`SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` enabled.

## Fix

Use a dynamic per-tensor scale computed from `q` itself:

```python
q, q_scale = scaled_fp8_quant(q)  # dynamic per-tensor scale
q_descale = q_scale
```

The kernel folds `q_descale * k_descale` into `qk_scale`, so the dequantized product
is correct either way — the only thing that changes is whether `q` was quantized with
a scale appropriate to its own range.

With a proper scale the fp8-q × fp8-KV path stays numerically sane, which makes the
~+15% decode throughput from that path actually usable instead of being a
correctness/speed trade.

## Verification

**Not independently verified.** The diagnosis is a strong one on inspection — reusing
a tensor's calibration scale for a different tensor is straightforwardly wrong — and
`scaled_fp8_quant(q)` with no scale argument is the documented dynamic path.

Not measured here: the +15% decode figure, and the actual accuracy recovery. Before
merging, run an accuracy benchmark with `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1` and an fp8
KV cache, against the same config with the flag off.

## Note

A sibling agent session produced an alternative fix for the same symptom: keep `q` in
bf16 and let the kernel dequantize the fp8 KV in-kernel. That avoids the quantization
error rather than fixing the scale, and gives up the fp8-q × fp8-KV path. I am
submitting this one instead because it addresses the actual bug; the bf16-q variant
is a reasonable fallback if the fp8-q path turns out to have further issues.

issue.title: [AgentX] Specialist prompts omit the resolved serving recipe, so specialists are not told speculative decoding is running
issue.body:
## Summary

On a native AgentX session (Magpie resolves the InferenceX recipe), the specialist
prompt never states what the server is actually running. In particular it never
says that speculative decoding is active, which draft is driving it, or that the
acceptance length is simulated.

`manifest.json` records `server_args: []` on that path, because Magpie owns the
launch, so nothing in `SharedState` carries the resolved recipe either.

The specialists in the session I looked at did end up knowing — the research scout
went and read the InferenceX recipe script directly and put the findings into the
KB context block. That is a discovery, not a guarantee.

## What the specialist is told

`## 2. HARDWARE CONTEXT` of a specialist `prompt.md` from a native AgentX session
(`GLM-5.2-MXFP4_20261019T120212Z_cdc589c2`):

```
## 2. HARDWARE CONTEXT

- gpu_type: mi355x
- TP: 8

Workload:
- precision: fp4
- concurrency: 4
**Graded on E2E normalised interactivity P50** — ...
- max_model_len: 1048576
```

`## 5. WARM-START RECIPE SUMMARY` is `(none)`.

Two things are missing:

1. **The resolved serving recipe**, including speculative decoding.
2. **The corpus shape.** On the native AgentX path the manifest's `workload`
   block carries no `isl` / `osl` / `corpus_*` fields, so `corpus_lines()` renders
   nothing. The specialist is told `concurrency: 4` for a workload whose measured
   ISL is median ~119K / p90 ~518K.

An earlier campaign that passed `--server-args` explicitly *does* render the corpus
distribution, but still never renders the server args: grepping every specialist
`prompt.md` in that session for a distinctive substring of its recipe
(`tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41`) returns zero hits. So (1) is not specific to the
native path — it is missing everywhere.

## What is actually running

From `agentx_server_launch.json` (`"owner": "magpie"`) in the same session:

```
--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5
--speculative-eagle-topk 1  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6
```

with

```
SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.61
SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected
SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token
```

and `server.log` showing the draft weights loaded on every rank:

```
Load weight end. elapsed=2.77 s, type=GlmMoeDsaForCausalLMNextN, quant=quark, mem usage=2.73 GB
```

`recipe_source_files` names the origin:
`InferenceX/.../srt-slurm-recipes/glm5.2/sglang/mi355x-fp4-mtp/agentic.yaml`.

## Where the gap is

`src/hyperloom/orchestrator/prompts/specialist_prompt_builder.py` L1406-1431 builds
§2 from `gpu_type`, `allocated_gpu_ids`, `tp`, `hbm_gb`, `peak_tflops`, `precision`,
`conc`, `corpus_lines(...)` and `grading_lines(...)`. There is no serving-recipe row.

Nothing under `src/hyperloom/orchestrator/prompts/` or
`src/hyperloom/orchestrator/state/` reads `base_argv`, `effective_argv`,
`observed_server_config` or `recipe_source_files`. The only consumers are
execution-time guards and plumbing:

- `actions/executors/_launch_restatement.py`
- `actions/executors/_spec_decode_context_copy.py`
- `actions/executors/explore.py`
- `inference_optimizer/agentx/geak_proxy.py`
- `inference_optimizer/agentx/report.py`

## Why it matters

- A specialist that does not know a draft model is running cannot reason about the
  cost it is looking at. In this session the draft and verify phases together are a
  large share of decode GPU time, and several of the hottest kernels only exist
  because speculative decoding is on.
- With `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN` set, acceptance is pinned to the InferenceX golden
  value, so **any proposal that would change draft quality cannot show a gain at
  all** — only proposals that change how fast the draft runs can. A specialist that
  is not told this can spend its whole budget on a lever the benchmark cannot score.
- #1885 added `_spec_decode_pin.py` to refuse candidates that change the draft or the
  simulated acceptance. That guard compensates at execution time for context the
  specialist never had at proposal time. Giving the specialist the context would let
  it avoid the dead end rather than be stopped at it.

## The data is already on disk

Nothing new has to be measured:

- `runs/<action>/<task>/<variant>/agentx_server_launch.json` —
  `base_argv`, `effective_argv`, `base_env`, `effective_env`, `recipe_source_files`
- `.../launch_evidence.json` — `observed_server_config`, `observed_server_env`

It only needs to reach the prompt.

## Suggested direction

Render a short resolved-recipe block in §2 for AgentX sessions, sourced from the
launch evidence rather than from `state.server_args` (which is empty on the native
path). Worth stating explicitly, because each changes what a specialist should
even consider:

- the speculative algorithm, step count and draft-token count, and whether the draft
  is an external checkpoint or the model's own nextn/MTP head;
- whether acceptance is simulated, and at what value — together with the fact that
  draft-quality levers cannot score while it is;
- the few serving flags that shape the decode path (KV cache dtype, the DSA backends,
  chunked-prefill size).

Separately, the native AgentX path should populate the manifest's `workload` corpus
fields so `corpus_lines()` has something to render, as the non-native path already does.

I am happy to pick this up.

issue.title: [Bug] gpt-oss: Quark checkpoint KV scales are silently dropped, so fp8 KV runs with unit scales
issue.body:
## Summary

gpt-oss silently drops the attention KV scales of Quark checkpoints (`self_attn.k_proj.output_scale` / `self_attn.v_proj.output_scale`). With `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` the KV cache then runs with `k_scale = v_scale = 1.0` instead of the calibrated per-layer scales.

Affected checkpoints, for example:
- `amd/gpt-oss-20b-MoE-Quant-W-MXFP4-A-FP8-KV-FP8` (per-layer scales 0.16–0.27; 0.32–0.55 after the e4m3fnuz adjustment)
- `amd/gpt-oss-20b-WFP8-AFP8-KVFP8`
- `amd/gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8-kv-fp8-fp8attn-no_lmhead_router`

Found by code reading at upstream `8e3e2980db`; not verified end to end (see below).

## Cause

Two gaps in `python/sglang/srt/models/gpt_oss.py`:

1. `GptOssAttention` builds `RadixAttention` without `quant_config`, so no quant method is attached and the layer has no `k_scale` / `v_scale` parameters to load into.
2. `_load_normal_weights` (also used for the non-expert weights of Quark checkpoints via `load_gptoss_weight_quark`) never calls `maybe_remap_kv_scale_name`. `k_proj.output_scale` is renamed by the stacked mapping to `qkv_proj.output_scale`, which is not a parameter, and is skipped without a warning. `maybe_remap_kv_scale_name` already maps the Quark names to `.attn.k_scale` / `.attn.v_scale`, and Llama and other models call it.

## Proposed fix

- Pass `quant_config=quant_config` to `RadixAttention` in `GptOssAttention`.
- In `_load_normal_weights`, remap scale names before the stacked mapping, as Llama does:

```python
if "scale" in name:
    name = maybe_remap_kv_scale_name(name, params_dict)
    if name is None:
        continue
```

Effect of passing `quant_config` per quant method, for `RadixAttention`: MXFP4, W4AFP8 and Petit return no method (no change); FP8, ModelOpt and Quark attach a KV-cache method whose scales default to 1.0 when the checkpoint has none (same behaviour as Llama).

## Risks to resolve before submitting

- **Depends on jiaqiang-dot-liu/sglang#27 on ROCm.** gpt-oss uses sliding-window attention, which forces AITER unified attention. Once real (non-1) KV scales are loaded, the AITER q-descale / k-v-scale bugs fixed in #27 become active, so landing this fix alone could make fp8-KV gpt-oss on AITER worse than today (where the scales are ignored).
- **CUDA fused KV write.** `create_fused_set_kv_buffer_arg` asserts `layer.k_scale is None and layer.v_scale is None` on CUDA. With `quant_config` passed, FP8 / ModelOpt / Quark gpt-oss gets non-None scale parameters, so this assertion would fire whenever the fused path is enabled on CUDA (bf16 KV pool, non-hybrid SWA pool, e.g. `--disable-hybrid-swa-memory`). That path only runs with a bf16 KV cache, where the scales are unused, so the assertion should be relaxed (or the fused path gated) rather than worked around in gpt-oss. No other model currently combines the fused write with `quant_config` (gemma4 has the fused path disabled).

## Why this is not verified

On MI325X (gfx942) neither Quark gpt-oss checkpoint with KV scales can be served:
- `amd/gpt-oss-20b-WFP8-AFP8-KVFP8` (FP8 experts): the Quark gpt-oss expert loader assumes the MXFP4 W4A8 MoE scheme with expert biases; `QuarkW8A8FP8MoE` creates no `w13/w2_weight_bias`, so loading fails with `KeyError: 'model.layers.0.mlp.experts.w2_weight_bias'`. This is a separate gap; the checkpoint targets vLLM.
- `amd/gpt-oss-20b-MoE-Quant-W-MXFP4-A-FP8-KV-FP8` (MXFP4 experts): the AITER MXFP4 MoE kernel is not available on gfx942 (`module_moe_cktile2stages.so: undefined symbol ...pk_float4_e2m1...`).

Suggested verification on MI355X (gfx950) with `amd/gpt-oss-20b-MoE-Quant-W-MXFP4-A-FP8-KV-FP8`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, together with #27: check the loaded `layer.k_scale_float` values, then GSM8K / GPQA for bf16 KV, fp8 KV before, and fp8 KV after.

issue.title: [Bug] [AMD] aiter: gfx950 head_dim-256 fp8 prefill passes descales that do not match how q/k/v were quantized
issue.body:
## Summary

On gfx950, the two head_dim-256 fp8 prefill paths in `AiterAttnBackend.forward_extend` that call `flash_attn_varlen_fp8_pertensor_func` pass descales that do not match how their inputs were quantized. With an fp8 KV cache and a checkpoint that ships calibrated KV scales (`layer.k_scale` / `layer.v_scale` far from 1), the attention output is wrong. With `k_scale == v_scale == 1` (no KV scales) the mismatch is invisible.

This is the gfx950 counterpart of the q-descale bug fixed for the NHD prefill and the unified-attention decode in #27. It is not fixed there because it cannot be verified on MI325X (gfx942).

## Affected code

`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py` at upstream `8e3e2980db`:

1. **Context-chunk prefill (extend with a prefix)**, around L4501–L4512: q is cast with `.to(fp8_dtype)` (no scaling), but `layer.k_scale` is passed as `q_descale`. K/V are gathered from the cache, so `k_descale` / `v_descale` are correct here. Effect: every logit is scaled by `k_scale`.

2. **First-chunk prefill (extend without a prefix)**, around L4542–L4551: q, k and v are all cast with `.to(fp8_dtype)` from bf16, but `layer.k_scale`, `k_descale` and `v_descale` are passed as their descales. Effect: logits are scaled by `k_scale²`, and the output by `v_scale`.

In addition, `.to(fp8)` does not saturate: out-of-range values become NaN (on e4m3fn above ~464, on e4m3fnuz above ~248), whereas `scaled_fp8_quant` clamps.

Trigger conditions: gfx950, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, `qk_head_dim == v_head_dim == 256`, no sliding window / sinks / logit cap, GQA ratio supported by the ASM kernel, and a checkpoint with KV scales.

## Suggested fix

Follow the gfx950 HD128 ASM prefill in the same function, which already handles both points correctly:

- q: use `_quantize_q_fp8` from #27 (static unit q scale, saturating, contiguous input) and pass the returned scale as `q_descale`. The HD128 path casts q at unit scale and passes the unit `self.k_scale`.
- First-chunk path: read K/V from the already quantized KV cache (as the HD128 path does for first and later chunks alike) instead of casting the raw bf16 `k` / `v`, so `k_descale` / `v_descale` match the data. This also gives the first chunk the same quantization as later chunks.

## Verification needed

Requires an MI355X (gfx950). Suggested check: a head_dim-256 model with an fp8 KV-scale checkpoint (or a head_dim-256 model with KV scales injected), `--attention-backend aiter --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, GSM8K before/after, plus a long-prompt run that exercises chunked prefill so both paths are hit.

issue.title: [AgentX] Specialist prompts omit the resolved serving recipe, so specialists are not told speculative decoding is running
issue.body:
## Summary

On a native AgentX session (Magpie resolves the InferenceX recipe), the specialist
prompt never states what the server is actually running. In particular it never
says that speculative decoding is active, which draft is driving it, or that the
acceptance length is simulated.

`manifest.json` records `server_args: []` on that path, because Magpie owns the
launch, so nothing in `SharedState` carries the resolved recipe either.

The specialists in the session I looked at did end up knowing — the research scout
went and read the InferenceX recipe script directly and put the findings into the
KB context block. That is a discovery, not a guarantee.

## What the specialist is told

`## 2. HARDWARE CONTEXT` of a specialist `prompt.md` from a native AgentX session
(`GLM-5.2-MXFP4_20261019T120212Z_cdc589c2`):

```
## 2. HARDWARE CONTEXT

- gpu_type: mi355x
- TP: 8

Workload:
- precision: fp4
- concurrency: 4
**Graded on E2E normalised interactivity P50** — ...
- max_model_len: 1048576
```

`## 5. WARM-START RECIPE SUMMARY` is `(none)`.

Two things are missing:

1. **The resolved serving recipe**, including speculative decoding.
2. **The corpus shape.** On the native AgentX path the manifest's `workload`
   block carries no `isl` / `osl` / `corpus_*` fields, so `corpus_lines()` renders
   nothing. The specialist is told `concurrency: 4` for a workload whose measured
   ISL is median ~119K / p90 ~518K.

An earlier campaign that passed `--server-args` explicitly *does* render the corpus
distribution, but still never renders the server args: grepping every specialist
`prompt.md` in that session for a distinctive substring of its recipe
(`tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41`) returns zero hits. So (1) is not specific to the
native path — it is missing everywhere.

## What is actually running

From `agentx_server_launch.json` (`"owner": "magpie"`) in the same session:

```
--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5
--speculative-eagle-topk 1  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6
```

with

```
SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.61
SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected
SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token
```

and `server.log` showing the draft weights loaded on every rank:

```
Load weight end. elapsed=2.77 s, type=GlmMoeDsaForCausalLMNextN, quant=quark, mem usage=2.73 GB
```

`recipe_source_files` names the origin:
`InferenceX/.../srt-slurm-recipes/glm5.2/sglang/mi355x-fp4-mtp/agentic.yaml`.

## Where the gap is

`src/hyperloom/orchestrator/prompts/specialist_prompt_builder.py` L1406-1431 builds
§2 from `gpu_type`, `allocated_gpu_ids`, `tp`, `hbm_gb`, `peak_tflops`, `precision`,
`conc`, `corpus_lines(...)` and `grading_lines(...)`. There is no serving-recipe row.

Nothing under `src/hyperloom/orchestrator/prompts/` or
`src/hyperloom/orchestrator/state/` reads `base_argv`, `effective_argv`,
`observed_server_config` or `recipe_source_files`. The only consumers are
execution-time guards and plumbing:

- `actions/executors/_launch_restatement.py`
- `actions/executors/_spec_decode_context_copy.py`
- `actions/executors/explore.py`
- `inference_optimizer/agentx/geak_proxy.py`
- `inference_optimizer/agentx/report.py`

## Why it matters

- A specialist that does not know a draft model is running cannot reason about the
  cost it is looking at. In this session the draft and verify phases together are a
  large share of decode GPU time, and several of the hottest kernels only exist
  because speculative decoding is on.
- With `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN` set, acceptance is pinned to the InferenceX golden
  value, so **any proposal that would change draft quality cannot show a gain at
  all** — only proposals that change how fast the draft runs can. A specialist that
  is not told this can spend its whole budget on a lever the benchmark cannot score.
- #1885 added `_spec_decode_pin.py` to refuse candidates that change the draft or the
  simulated acceptance. That guard compensates at execution time for context the
  specialist never had at proposal time. Giving the specialist the context would let
  it avoid the dead end rather than be stopped at it.

## The data is already on disk

Nothing new has to be measured:

- `runs/<action>/<task>/<variant>/agentx_server_launch.json` —
  `base_argv`, `effective_argv`, `base_env`, `effective_env`, `recipe_source_files`
- `.../launch_evidence.json` — `observed_server_config`, `observed_server_env`

It only needs to reach the prompt.

## Suggested direction

Render a short resolved-recipe block in §2 for AgentX sessions, sourced from the
launch evidence rather than from `state.server_args` (which is empty on the native
path). Worth stating explicitly, because each changes what a specialist should
even consider:

- the speculative algorithm, step count and draft-token count, and whether the draft
  is an external checkpoint or the model's own nextn/MTP head;
- whether acceptance is simulated, and at what value — together with the fact that
  draft-quality levers cannot score while it is;
- the few serving flags that shape the decode path (KV cache dtype, the DSA backends,
  chunked-prefill size).

Separately, the native AgentX path should populate the manifest's `workload` corpus
fields so `corpus_lines()` has something to render, as the non-native path already does.

I am happy to pick this up.

issue.title: refactor(kernelforge): split loop/runner.py into per-concern IterationLoop mixins

labels.name: repo-214761c4
labels.description: Waives the PR diff budget; added by a maintainer with a reason in the PR description

issue.body:
- Description: what and why

  `src/kernelforge/loop/runner.py` held the whole `IterationLoop` in 6,545 lines (module-length limit: 1,200). This PR moves ten groups of methods, verbatim, into modules of their own. Each module is a mixin that `IterationLoop` now inherits, which is the pattern `RelayRuntimeMixin` and `AnalysisRuntimeMixin` already follow. `runner.py` drops to 2,520 lines; the largest new module is 650.

  | Module | What it owns | Lines |
  |:--|:--|--:|
  | `workspace_runtime.py` | git, diffs, new-path ownership, source reads | 512 |
  | `budget_runtime.py` | campaign clock, round admission, stop conditions | 261 |
  | `ceiling_runtime.py` | roofline ceiling and attainment | 279 |
  | `scoring_runtime.py` | baseline and incumbent case times, case coverage | 372 |
  | `lane_runtime.py` | lane fan-out, the lane queue, merge stacking | 566 |
  | `planning_runtime.py` | search policy, orchestration, critic, supervisor | 450 |
  | `outcome_runtime.py` | iteration events, handoffs, ledger, archive | 412 |
  | `resume_runtime.py` | the pending KEEP, resume validation, recovery replay | 650 |
  | `publication_runtime.py` | best-result publication and the final report | 363 |
  | `warm_start_runtime.py` | run-state hydration, warm starts, the anchor | 229 |
  | `iteration_types.py` | `IterationConfig`, `IterationResult`, `LoopAgents`, per-iteration records | 314 |

  This is the first of three steps. `runner.py` still holds the iteration control flow, measurement, candidate sourcing, and six methods over the function-length or cognitive-complexity limit. The code-metrics gate judges a method moved to another class as new code, so those six get split before they move (step 2). Step 3 splits the control-flow methods themselves and takes `runner.py` under 800 lines.

- Linked issue(s): none

- Tests: added/updated? commands run?

  Updated, with no assertion changed:
  - `test_loop_runner.py`: patches `git`, `is_protected_path`, `run_lanes`, `admit_round` and `admit_dispatch` in the module that now looks them up, and imports `pin_iteration` from `run_state`, which defines it.
  - `test_measurement_guards.py`: the fake clock now also replaces `time` in `budget_runtime`, because `_observe_measurement` moved there while `run_one_iteration` stayed in `runner`.
  - `roofline_ceiling/test_integration.py`: "one ceiling reader for the whole loop" counts across every `kernelforge.loop` module in `IterationLoop.__mro__`, not just `runner.py`.

  Added: two tests for `_line_buffer_stdout` (see "Observable effect").

  Commands run:
  - `pytest src/kernelforge/tests -n 32`, on this branch and, as a baseline, on an untouched worktree of `main` at the same commit. Both runs have the same 6,001 cases. Apart from the two added tests, not one case changed status. The four failures are identical on both and come from this host's environment: `test_rocpc_profile_discovery` (x2, a ROCm install under `/opt/rocm`), `test_build_parallelism::test_no_ceiling_means_no_opinion` (host CPU count) and `test_opportunity_agent::test_hookless_resume_republication_clears_a_corrected_refusal`.
  - The `hyperloom` tests that touch kernelforge (`orchestrator/kernel/tests/test_controller_submit.py`, `test_forge_fusion.py`, `test_forge_gemm_tuning.py`, `test_campaign_baseline.py`, `inference_optimizer/tests/test_install_kernelforge_ready.py`): 116 passed.
  - `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .`, `lint-imports --no-cache` (10 contracts kept), `scripts/check_broad_suppress.py`, `compileall`.
  - `scripts/code_metrics.py --base-ref main`: PASSED. No new or worse units, and every design check (A1, A8 to A12) found nothing.

- Size/complexity triggers crossed: split, or why the shape is right:

  The split is the point of the PR. All eleven new modules are under the 800-line review trigger.

  **Diff budget.** `scripts/pr_hygiene.py size` counts 8,703 changed lines. A move counts every line twice, once as deleted from `runner.py` and once as added to its new module. The PR does not shrink by splitting it further: moving `resume_runtime` on its own would still cross 1,000. Reason for `size-exception`: the change is a verbatim move, and that is checked mechanically (see next item), so review is about where code went, not what it does.

- If this simplifies or refactors: which mechanism was removed, which contract was preserved, and the tests that show it:

  No mechanism is removed. Preserved, and checked directly:
  - Every moved function, class and constant is AST-identical to its original (`ast.dump` compared unit by unit: 205 units, none missing, none duplicated). The only unit that differs is `_run_locked`, for the stdout change below.
  - `dir(IterationLoop)` is identical before and after, and no name in its MRO is defined by more than one class, so no mixin shadows another.
  - Every public name `runner.py` defined is still importable from it, through `__all__`.
  - Callers are untouched: `cli/forge_loop_command.py` and `assembly/prepare.py`.

  The tests above are the behavioural evidence. The private methods tests call on a loop instance still resolve on `IterationLoop`.

- Observable effect: what an operator will now see, and what the old behaviour cost them (if none, why the change is unobservable):

  One change is re-expressed rather than moved. `_run_locked` used `global print` to rebind the `print` of `runner.py` so that it flushed on every call. That only covered code in `runner.py`, and it would have stopped covering the methods this PR moves out. It is replaced by `_line_buffer_stdout()`, which puts `sys.stdout` in line-buffered mode when the stream supports it. No `print` in the loop passes `end=`, so the same lines are flushed. One difference an operator can see: progress lines from `relay_runtime` and `analysis_runtime`, which were never flushed before, now reach a piped reader as soon as they are printed.

  Logger names change from `kernelforge.loop.runner` to the module that now logs, for example `kernelforge.loop.workspace_runtime`. These are still under `kernelforge.loop`, and no code or test configures logging by the old name.

- Breaking changes: no. Imports from `kernelforge.loop.runner` and the `IterationLoop` surface are unchanged.

- PR addresses single concern: yes (moving code out of `runner.py`).

- Root cause is upstream (Magpie/TraceLens/GEAK/IntelliKit/AgentKernelArena), ticket filed: n/a

comment.body: Closing: this overlaps with another in-progress refactor of loop/runner.py.

issue.title: [Kimi-K3][ROCm] Enable the KDA/MLA side stream on HIP
issue.body:
## Summary

Enable one of Kimi-K3's three alt streams on ROCm (slot `[2]`), and raise the
side-stream token bound to 128 on HIP.

Today the whole pool is switched off with `None if _is_hip else [...]`, so the
decode path of all 69 KDA layers and all 24 full-attention layers runs fully
serialized on HIP.

## What slot [2] carries

* the KDA `[f_a|b]` + `f_b` tiny GEMVs, which read only `hidden_states` and can run
  concurrently with the wide fused `[q,k,v,g]` GEMM on the main stream;
* the MLA output-gate GEMM, which overlaps the attention core.

Both are plain GEMM work with an existing HIP path — `kimi_k3_tiny_gemm` falls back
to `F.linear`, the MLA gate to `x * sigmoid(gate)` — and both users are gated on
`get_is_capture_mode()` plus a token-count bound, so the fork/join is recorded
inside the decode graph exactly as it is on CUDA.

## Why slots [0] and [1] stay off

Slot `[0]` is the MoE dual-stream shared-expert tail, which reaches
`k3_ar_fusion`'s symmetric-memory all-reduce — that has no HIP path. Both remain
behind the established `SGLANG_ROCM_USE_MULTI_STREAM` switch, the same opt-in
deepseek_v2 / deepseek_v4 use on ROCm.

## Token bound

`_bfa_bs_limit` goes from 64 to 128 on HIP, matching Blackwell. The quoted
measurement (gfx950, 69-layer graph replay of this projection block, TP8, bf16) is
that the overlap wins from M=1 through M=128 — 1.10× at 64, 1.11× at 96, 1.04× at
128 — and turns negative from M=160 up, where the wide GEMM already fills the CUs.

## Kill switch

`SGLANG_K3_ROCM_ALT_STREAM=0` restores the fully serialized HIP path. Registered as
an `EnvBool(True)` in `environ.py` per `.claude/skills/env-var-conventions`.

## Verification

**Not verified — and this turns something on by default.** The 1.10× / 1.11× /
1.04× figures come from the originating agent run on MI355X; I have no such
hardware and have reproduced none of them. Nor have I confirmed the more important
claim: that the fork/join is actually capture-safe on HIP in practice, not just by
the argument above. A stream fork that misbehaves under HIP graph capture is a hang
or a wrong-numbers bug, not a slowdown.

Before merging: capture and replay a K3 decode graph on gfx950 with the switch on,
confirm output matches the serialized path, and re-measure the M sweep to confirm
128 is the right bound rather than 64.

Given it defaults on, a reviewer may reasonably prefer `EnvBool(False)` until that
sweep exists. I kept the author's default; flipping it is a one-character change.

## Rebase note

The original patch did not apply. Rebased onto current `main`:
`is_blackwell_supported()` became `get_platform().is_blackwell`, the env var moved
from a module-level `get_bool_env_var` to an `environ.py` `EnvBool` per the repo's
env-var conventions, and the stream-pool construction was restructured into a plain
if/elif chain.

---

*Provenance: originally authored by an automated kernel-optimization agent
(hyperloom session `20260813T103007Z`, model `Kimi-K3`).*

<!-- pr-states:start -->
---
### CI States

Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #34923977970](https://github.com/jiaqiang-dot-liu/sglang/actions/runs/34923977970)<!-- slot:pr-test:end -->
Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #34923977847](https://github.com/jiaqiang-dot-liu/sglang/actions/runs/34923977847)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end -->
Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #34923977948](https://github.com/jiaqiang-dot-liu/sglang/actions/runs/34923977948)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end -->

comment.body: Closing. The HIP side-stream disable came in with the initial Kimi-K3 support (sgl-project/sglang#32541) without a stated reason; two of the three alt-stream users reach CUDA-only kernels, and on ROCm sglang keeps multi-stream opt-in (SGLANG_ROCM_USE_MULTI_STREAM), where the gain depends on settings such as GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES. Making it default-on would need confirmation of why it was disabled plus end-to-end Kimi-K3 data at default settings, and the extra env var here overlaps the existing one. Not worth pursuing in this form.

issue.title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3] Widen the workgroup for decode-shaped attn_res launches
issue.body:
## Summary

Widen the workgroup for decode-shaped `attn_res` launches on ROCm so the kernel
covers more of the machine and carries fewer accumulators per lane. Prefill is
untouched.

## Why

`attn_res` launches with `grid=(num_tokens,)` — one workgroup per sequence. On a
CDNA3/CDNA4 part (256 CUs × 4 SIMDs ≈ 1024 SIMDs) a concurrency-64 decode step
therefore resides only `num_tokens * num_warps = 64 * 8 = 512` wavefronts and
leaves roughly half the machine idle. At the same time each lane carries
`BLOCK_D / (64 * num_warps) = 16` fp32 accumulators of the hidden-dim reduction —
high VGPR pressure, 1–2 waves/SIMD.

Widening the workgroup raises wave residency and lowers per-lane register pressure
without changing the tiling or the math.

This matters because `attn_res` is the most-launched kernel in the model: two per
decoder layer plus a final one.

## Change

For `num_tokens < 128` only, raise `num_warps` toward the AMD workgroup maximum
(16 wavefronts = 1024 work-items), bounded so each lane keeps at least 4 fp32
accumulators — otherwise a small hidden size would be widened into mostly-masked
lanes.

Prefill (`num_tokens >= 128`) already saturates the grid and takes the existing
path unchanged.

## Numerics

Only the reduction's lane partitioning changes. Results differ at most by
floating-point reassociation — this is **not** bit-identical, which is worth
knowing if anything downstream is being compared exactly.

## Verification

**Not benchmarked.** The occupancy arithmetic is checkable from the launch shape
and I believe it is right, but I have no MI355X and have not confirmed the wider
workgroup actually wins. Note the change is unconditional for decode-shaped
launches — there is no env switch — so if it does not win it is a regression, not
a no-op. That is the main thing to check before merging.

---

*Provenance: originally authored by an automated kernel-optimization agent
(hyperloom session `20260903T234719Z`, model `Kimi-K3`); applies cleanly to current
`main`.*

---

issue.title: [ROCm][KDA] Align the merged in_proj row count to 256 so tuned GEMMs are reachable
issue.body:
## Problem

`KimiGDNLinearAttention` pads the merged `in_proj` row count to a multiple of 16:

```python
self.in_proj_padding = -local_output_size % 16
```

For Kimi-K3 at TP8 that gives `N = 4*1536 + 128 + 12 = 6284 -> 6288 = 16 * 393`.
**393 is odd**, so `N` is not a multiple of 64, 128 or 256 — and every tuned BF16
GEMM path this projection could take rejects the shape:

* `aiter/ops/flydsl/kernels/small_m_hgemm.py` asserts `n % BLOCK_N == 0`, and
  `BLOCK_N` is 64/128/256 across the tuned small-M catalog, so every FlyDSL
  candidate in `aiter.tuned_gemm` is unusable;
* `aiter/tuned_gemm.py`'s bpreshuffle default requires `N % 64 == 0` before it will
  select the `asm` library;
* hipBLASLt reaches its widest N tiles only on an aligned N, and otherwise runs a
  ragged final tile column.

The net effect is that **all 69 KDA layers fall back to a generic GEMM**.

## Change

Widen the alignment to 256, giving `N = 6400 = 256 * 25` (also a multiple of 64 and
128), overridable via `VLLM_KDA_IN_PROJ_ALIGN`. Setting it to 16 restores today's
behaviour exactly.

## Cost

116 extra zeroed output rows out of 6284 — +1.85% of this one projection's FLOPs,
roughly 114 MiB of weights per rank across 69 layers. The extra columns are split
off and discarded in `forward()` and the rows are zeroed at load, so every consumed
output is bit-identical.

## Verification

**Not benchmarked.** I confirmed the alignment arithmetic (6284 → 6288 = 16 × 393,
odd) and read the two aiter constraints the description cites, but I have no MI355X
and have not measured that the wider GEMM path is actually faster than the generic
fallback it replaces. The +1.85% FLOP cost is certain; the win is not.

Worth checking before merging that the tuned path is genuinely selected at
`N = 6400` and beats the current fallback by more than 1.85%.

## Style note

The patch as authored does `import os as _os` inside the constructor. Happy to
hoist it to module scope if preferred; I left it as-authored to keep the diff
minimal.

issue.title: [ROCm][KDA] Offer BV=128 / num_warps=8 in the chunk_delta_h autotune space
issue.body:
## Summary

On ROCm, widen the autotune space of
`chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64` to include `BV = 128` and
`num_warps = 8`. CUDA is untouched.

```python
if torch.version.hip:
    _CHUNK_DELTA_H_NUM_WARPS = [2, 4, 8]
    _CHUNK_DELTA_H_BV = [32, 64, 128]
else:
    _CHUNK_DELTA_H_NUM_WARPS = [2, 4]   # as today
    _CHUNK_DELTA_H_BV = [32, 64]        # as today
```

## Why `BV = 128` is worth offering

The h-stage grid is `(triton.cdiv(V, meta["BV"]), N * H)` (line 360), so **every
V-block independently re-streams the whole `k` / `w` / `g` / `gk` sequence** for its
`(sequence, head)` and re-runs the chunk recurrence. At `V = 128` the shipped
`BV` list forces 2–4 redundant passes over those operands.

For gated linear attention with a *per-channel* gate — KDA, where `gk` is fp32
`[T, H, 128]` — that operand is the largest tensor in the stage, so the redundant
passes dominate the kernel's HBM traffic.

`BV` tiles only the V axis: the kernel body is hardcoded around 64-wide K
sub-blocks (`b_h1 = tl.zeros([BV, 64])` … `b_h4`, lines 88–94; the kernel is
literally named `..._blockdim64`). So `BV == V` is structurally valid and removes
the redundancy entirely.

## Why it must be paired with `num_warps = 8`

At `K = V = 128` a `BV = 128` config holds 2 × `[128, 64]` fp32 accumulators:

* `num_warps = 8` (512 lanes) → 32 VGPRs/lane — comfortable on CDNA3/CDNA4
* `num_warps = 4` (256 lanes) → 64 VGPRs/lane — only spills

Offering `BV = 128` without `num_warps = 8` would be pointless. Note
`NUM_WARPS = [2, 4, 8, 16]` is already defined at the top of this file (line 19)
but unused by this particular autotune block.

## Safety

These are tiling/scheduling knobs only. Every config computes the same result, and
Triton's autotuner prunes any that fail to compile or exceed the register/LDS
budget (`OutOfResources` → `+inf`). Widening the space is numerics-neutral and
cannot select something slower than the previous best — worst case the new configs
lose and nothing changes.

The existing `_CHUNK_DELTA_H_NUM_STAGES` guard (`num_stages=4` fails to lower on
the AMD backend) is untouched.

## Cost

The HIP autotune space goes from 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 configs to 3 × 2 × 3 = 18, so
first-call autotune warmup for this kernel gets roughly 2× longer. Cached
afterwards.

## Verification

**Not benchmarked.** I verified the three structural claims above against the
source — the grid expression, the hardcoded 64-wide K sub-blocks, and the
accumulator shapes — and the register arithmetic follows from those. What I have
not done is run it: I have no MI355X, so I cannot confirm `BV = 128` actually wins
on any real KDA shape, only that it is legal to offer and cannot lose.

If it never wins, this change is dead weight in the autotune space and should be
dropped rather than merged.

---

comment.body: Closing: the h-stage recurrence is sequential over chunks, so its parallelism comes only from sequences x heads x V-blocks. BV=128 cuts that by 4x, which likely loses in the common serving case of few long sequences per prefill chunk. The autotune key (H, K, V, BT) has no sequence count, so the first call's choice is reused for every shape. Doing this safely would mean a parallelism-aware key in vendored FLA code, ideally upstreamed to flash-linear-attention first. The value is also shrinking as ROCm prefill moves to AITER FlyDSL (GDN) and Gluon chunk_kda (Kimi-K3).

issue.title: [ROCm][KDA] Make the packed decode launch tile tunable and default BV to 64
issue.body:
## Summary

Resolve `(BV, num_warps)` for the packed KDA decode launch through a helper with
env overrides, and move the AMD default `BV` from 32 to 64.

## Why

`fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode` hard-codes `BV = min(next_pow2(V), 32)` and
`num_warps = 4`, with no `triton.autotune` config — unlike every prefill kernel in
this directory, which carries `is_amd` num_warps/num_stages branches. This launch
is replayed once per decode step for **all 69 KDA layers**, so it was the one
kernel here still running an NVIDIA-shaped tile on gfx950.

## Why `BV` is safe to change

`BV` partitions only the V axis:

* every reduction in the kernel runs along `axis=1` (the K axis), which is always
  whole within a workgroup — no partial sums cross blocks;
* each V block owns a disjoint slice of state rows.

So results stay elementwise equivalent; this changes work decomposition, not
numerics.

Raising `BV` shrinks the V grid and therefore the number of times the
`i_v`-independent q/k/g/dt_bias vectors (`BK` elements each) are re-read and the two
L2-norm reductions re-run, at the cost of more registers per workgroup.

For the Kimi-K3 shape (V = K = 128), `BV = 64` takes the V grid from 4 to 2 —
halving those redundant reads — while the state tile stays at 64 × 128 fp32 = 32
VGPRs/thread at `num_warps = 4`, well clear of spilling, and still leaves
`2 * B * H` workgroups to fill the GPU.

## Overrides

`VLLM_KDA_DECODE_BV` / `VLLM_KDA_DECODE_NUM_WARPS`, both validated as powers of two
in range (bad values warn once and fall back). `VLLM_KDA_DECODE_BV=32` restores the
NVIDIA-identical tile exactly.

The AMD-vs-NVIDIA divergence is documented in the `__init__.py` header, which
already tracks deltas against the NVIDIA copy.

## Verification

**Not benchmarked.** The elementwise-equivalence argument is structural and I am
reasonably confident in it. The register arithmetic (32 VGPRs/thread at BV=64,
num_warps=4) follows from the state tile shape. What I have not done is measure
that `BV = 64` beats `BV = 32` on real decode shapes — this changes a default, so
if it loses it is a regression.

Given the kernel has no autotune config at all, an alternative worth considering is
adding one rather than moving the hard-coded default.

issue.title: [ROCm] Set waves_per_eu for the prefix_prefill Triton launch
issue.body:
## Summary

Pass a ROCm `waves_per_eu` hint to the `prefix_prefill` Triton kernel launch, which
currently passes an empty `extra_kargs` dict on ROCm.

## Why

`_fwd_kernel` is latency-bound on the paged K/V gather, not on the MFMA pipe —
TraceLens on MI355X measures the long-sequence chunked-prefill signatures at only
**17-28% of the HBM roofline**. With no `waves_per_eu` hint the AMD backend spends
the whole VGPR file on a single wave per EU, so there is no second wave to hide the
global-load latency behind.

The sibling decode kernels in `v1/attention/ops/triton_decode_attention.py` already
pass a ROCm `waves_per_eu`; this launch site was left as an empty dict.

## Verification

**Not benchmarked.** The roofline percentages come from the originating agent run on
MI355X and I have not reproduced them. The structural observation — that the sibling
decode kernels set this and prefix_prefill does not — is checkable and I checked it.

`waves_per_eu` caps the VGPR budget, so a kernel that genuinely needs the registers
will spill instead of gaining occupancy. That is the risk, and it is workload- and
head-dim-dependent. Worth measuring across head dims before merging.

issue.title: [ROCm][AR] Size the custom all-reduce staging buffers for full prefill chunks
issue.body:
## Summary

Two related changes to the ROCm all-reduce staging buffers:

1. **`aiter_custom_all_reduce.py`** — raise the IPC buffer default from 128 MiB to
   256 MiB, overridable via `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_CUSTOM_AR_MAX_SIZE_MB`.
2. **`custom_all_reduce.py`** — add `VLLM_CUSTOM_AR_MAX_SIZE_MB` so the otherwise
   hard-coded 8 MiB cap can be raised at all on ROCm.

## Why (1)

`effective_max_size()` is `max_size / 2`, so 128 MiB gives 64 MiB. At bf16
`hidden_size=6144` that caps the fused AR+RMSNorm path at
`64 MiB / (6144 * 2) == 5461` tokens — so a full `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`
prefill chunk (96 MiB) falls outside both the compiled fusion range
(`VllmConfig._set_compile_ranges`) and the runtime `should_custom_ar` guard. The
allreduce and the RMSNorm stay **unfused on exactly the chunks that dominate
prefill time**.

AITER's own `CustomAllreduce` default is 1 GiB, so 128 MiB was a conservative
vLLM-side choice, not a hardware limit. 256 MiB gives an effective 128 MiB == 10922
tokens at bf16 x 6144, covering an 8192-token chunk.

## Why (2)

On ROCm the `CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_MAX_SIZES` clamp is gated on `is_cuda()`, so it is
unreachable and there is no way at all to keep a large TP prefill all-reduce off
RCCL. This adds the knob; the default is unchanged.

## Memory cost — the reason to scrutinise (1)

The AITER pool allocates `max_size` (input) + `2 * max_size` (meta) per rank, i.e.
roughly **768 MiB/GPU at 256 MiB versus ~384 MiB today**. That is real KV-cache
budget given up on every deployment, whether or not it runs 8192-token chunks.

A defensible alternative is to merge only the env override and leave the default at
128 MiB. I would not argue against that; the default bump is the aggressive half.

## Verification

**Not measured.** The token-count arithmetic is straightforward and I am confident
the fusion window really does end at 5461 tokens for that shape. Unverified: that
fusing the 8192-token chunk is worth ~384 MiB/GPU of KV capacity, which is the
actual trade.

---

## AI-assistance disclosure (per `AGENTS.md`)

**AI assistance was used.** From automated kernel-optimization agent runs (hyperloom
session `20260813T174047Z`, model `MiniMax-M3-MXFP4`). No human review of every
line, no tests run — per `AGENTS.md` §1 **not ready for `vllm-project/vllm`**;
targets a personal fork.

**Tests run: none.** Outstanding: human review, an all-reduce benchmark, a memory
headroom check, `pre-commit`, and a `Signed-off-by:` trailer.

**Duplicate check.** `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search
"custom all reduce max size"` surfaced #50505 ("Size custom all-reduce buffers at
init so batch-invariant mode can use them"), which is adjacent — it also touches
custom-AR buffer sizing, though for a different reason (batch invariance rather than
fusion range). Worth coordinating; they will likely conflict.

comment.body: Closing: the premise is unverified. Fusing 4096-8192-token prefill chunks needs AITER custom all-reduce to beat RCCL at 32-128 MiB, which has not been measured, while the cost is certain: about 384 MiB more IPC memory per GPU on every TP deployment, plus two new env vars. The right path is to measure fused vs. unfused AR + RMSNorm on a multi-GPU host first and only then change the default, without env vars.

issue.title: [EP] Skip .qweight expert payloads in the EP weight filter
issue.body:
## Problem

`should_skip_weight` in the EP weight filter gates on the tensor name suffix:

```python
if not weight_name.endswith((".weight", ".weight_packed")):
    return False
```

AWQ- and GPTQ-style checkpoints store the per-expert payload under **`.qweight`**,
which is not in the tuple. `parse_expert_id` matches those names fine, but the
`endswith` guard then rejects them, `should_skip_weight` returns `False`, and the
tensor is read from disk on every rank.

So the EP I/O filter silently degrades to a no-op on int4/int8 MoE checkpoints —
exactly the checkpoints where the per-expert payload is largest relative to
everything else.

`.qweight` is the real name for these paths, not a hypothetical: see
`quantization/auto_awq.py`, `quantization/auto_gptq.py`,
`quantization/moe_wna16.py`, `compressed_tensors_moe_wna16.py`, and the
`w13_qweight` / `w2_qweight` parameters in
`fused_moe/oracle/int_wna16.py`.

## Change

Pull the suffixes into a named constant and add `.qweight`:

```python
_HEAVY_WEIGHT_SUFFIXES = (".weight", ".weight_packed", ".qweight")
```

with a comment recording what is deliberately **excluded** and why:
`.weight_scale`, `.weight_scale_inv`, `.weight_shape`, `.weight_zero_point` stay
out, because they are tiny and some backends need them from all experts (the
existing comment about FlashInfer NVFP4 computing a global max of activation
scales).

## Scope note

The originating patch also added `.weight_packed`; that has since landed upstream,
so this PR is only the `.qweight` half plus the named constant.

## On the "no low-value busywork" rule

`AGENTS.md` §1 rules out one-off tiny edits. I think this clears that bar — it is a
one-token functional fix that turns a silently-inert I/O optimization back on for a
whole checkpoint family, not a typo or style change. But it is a one-token fix, so
if a maintainer disagrees it should be bundled with other EP-loader work rather
than merged alone.

## Verification

**Not tested.** No GPU and no Python interpreter in the preparation environment, so
no pytest run and no load-time measurement of the skipped bytes on an AWQ/GPTQ MoE
checkpoint. The reasoning is a straightforward string-suffix argument and the
`.qweight` naming is confirmed by the files listed above, but the actual I/O saving
is unmeasured.

issue.title: [Core] Apply NUMA binding in-process when numactl is not installed
issue.body:
## Summary

Apply NUMA binding in-process when the `numactl` **binary** is not installed,
instead of failing the engine.

## Why

`numactl` is absent from many slim ROCm / vLLM images, but `libnuma` and
`sched_setaffinity` are still there. Today the missing binary takes down the whole
engine even though the binding is perfectly achievable.

## Change

When `shutil.which("numactl")` is `None`, hand the requested binding to the child
process through `_VLLM_INTERNAL_NUMA_INPROC` and let it apply the binding itself via
`apply_inproc_numa_binding()`. When the binary is present nothing changes — the
existing `numactl` exec path is untouched.

## Verification

**Not tested.** No Python interpreter in the preparation environment, so the CPU-list
parsing and the in-process binding were not exercised at all. This is
process-startup code that runs before any model work, so a mistake here is a
startup failure rather than a silent one — but the parsing of `numactl --physcpubind`
style CPU lists is exactly the sort of thing that wants a unit test, and I did not
write one.

Before merging: exercise it both with and without `numactl` on the PATH, and confirm
the resulting affinity matches what the `numactl` path would have produced.

**Duplicate check.** No overlapping open PR found for numactl-free NUMA binding.

comment.body: Closing: upstream intentionally fails fast when numa_bind is requested without numactl. A best-effort in-process fallback that only warns on failure changes that behavior and reimplements numactl semantics; installing numactl or improving the error message is the simpler path.

issue.title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Fix wrong output of the QK-norm + RoPE + KV-cache fusion on ROCM_ATTN
issue.body:
## Purpose

On `ROCM_ATTN`, the QK-norm + RoPE + KV-cache fusion (`fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache`) stores V in an interleaved layout, and the layer's attention kernels must read it that way. Two places break that contract, so the fusion produces wrong output on `main`:

1. **Qwen3 models decode garbage** (Qwen3-8B GSM8K 0.87 → 0.005). `QkNormRopeKvCacheFusionPass` calls `set_interleaved_v_cache()` on each eligible layer, but with `layer_name` hoisted (`_USE_LAYERNAME`, torch >= 2.11) one layer's patterns cover the model, so the loop `break`s after the first eligible layer and skips the call for every other one. Those layers keep `_use_interleaved_v_cache=False`: the fused kernel then writes the NHD layout into a cache their kernels read as the paged layout. Prefill looks right because it attends over the fused kernel's `k_out`; every decode step after it reads the cache. The existing fusion tests use a single attention layer, so they never reached the second layer.
2. **With `fuse_rope_kvcache` also on, models without QK-norm get a corrupted V cache** (Llama-3.1-8B GSM8K 0.766 → 0.71). The pass switches layers to the interleaved V cache before any pattern matches. On a layer the QK-norm pattern does not match, the RoPE + KV-cache fusion writes the KV cache instead, through `RocmAttentionImpl.do_rope_and_kv_cache_update`, whose Triton writer (`rocm_aiter_ops.triton_rope_and_cache`) only stores the regular V layout. A per-layer check at pattern registration cannot keep such layers out, because with `layer_name` hoisted one pattern serves every layer and graphs loaded from the compile cache skip the passes.

Fixing the first alone makes the second hit every layer instead of one (Llama-3.1-8B GSM8K 0.012), so both are fixed here, one commit each:

1. `QkNormRopeKvCacheFusionPass` switches every eligible layer and only skips the duplicate pattern registration.
2. `do_rope_and_kv_cache_update` applies RoPE in place (`ops.rotary_embedding`) and takes the unfused `do_kv_cache_update`, which already writes the interleaved layout, on layers that use the interleaved V cache. Layers with the regular V cache keep the fused Triton writer.

Only `ROCM_ATTN` is affected; `fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache` is off by default.

## Test Plan

Single MI300-series GPU (gfx942), ROCm 7.2.3, torch 2.11, AITER v0.1.25, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, `ROCM_ATTN`, TP1. The change is on `main` @ `83db1ab496`; it was exercised on a source build of `main` @ `5be4266f5c` with the touched files replaced (they and the pass manager are unchanged between the two).

- `pytest tests/compile/passes/test_rocm_aiter_qk_norm_rope_kvcache_fusion.py tests/compile/passes/test_rope_kvcache_fusion.py`
- `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 --temperature 0` against `vllm serve <model> -cc.pass_config.fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache=true [-cc.pass_config.fuse_rope_kvcache=true] -cc.use_inductor_graph_partition=true`
- Speed: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 --random-range-ratio 0.0 --ignore-eos --max-concurrency C --num-prompts max(16, 4*C)`, median TPOT, two rounds per arm in the order PR, base, PR, base.

## Test Result

**Unit tests:** 1497 and 50 passed (24 skipped). Two new cases fail on `main` and pass here:

- `test_qk_norm_rope_kvcache_fusion_interleaves_every_layer` builds three `ROCM_ATTN` layers and checks that all of them switch.
- `test_rope_kvcache_fusion` gains an `interleaved_v` case that compares the fused and unfused caches of an interleaved-V `ROCM_ATTN` layer; its bf16 variants fail on `main`. (With an fp8 cache and `block_size=16` the two V layouts coincide, so those pass either way.)

**Root cause of the first bug, confirmed at runtime** on Qwen3-0.6B (28 layers): on `main`, `set_interleaved_v_cache()` ran for one layer; that layer's fused writes used `use_shuffle_layout=True` and the other 27 layers' used `False`. The fused writer and the unfused interleaved writer produce byte-identical caches, and the decode and prefill kernels read the interleaved layout correctly, so only the flag was missing.

**GSM8K** (1319 questions unless noted):

| Model | Fusions on | `main` | This PR | Fusions off |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B | QK-norm | 0.005 (200 questions) | 0.871 | 0.879 / 0.873 |
| Qwen3-8B | QK-norm + RoPE | — | 0.876 | 0.879 / 0.873 |
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | QK-norm + RoPE | 0.718 / 0.706 | 0.757 | 0.766 / 0.763 |

The QK-norm pass replaces all 36 patterns of Qwen3-8B in both arms. With only the first commit, the Llama row drops to 0.012.

**Speed, Qwen3-8B.** QK-norm fusion on with this PR, versus `main` without the fusion. The opt-in goes through the ROCm default-config change in jiaqiang-dot-liu/vllm#20 rather than graph partition, so the comparison is against the stock `main` server. Mean of two rounds:

| Concurrency | `main` (ms) | With fusion (ms) | TPOT | Output throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4.886 | 4.650 | **−4.8%** | +5.2% |
| 8 | 6.552 | 6.275 | **−4.2%** | +4.4% |
| 32 | 8.983 | 8.715 | −3.0% | +2.6% |
| 64 | 11.576 | 11.368 | −1.8% | +2.5% |
| 128 | 17.554 | 17.206 | −2.0% | +4.2% |

GSM8K in that setup: 0.876 / 0.876.

On interleaved-V layers the RoPE + KV-cache fusion now runs as two kernels instead of one. A fused write of the interleaved layout needs the Triton RoPE + cache kernel to support it, which is an AITER change.

---

**AI assistance was used** (per `AGENTS.md`). The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and benchmarks above.

comment.body: Closing: merged upstream as https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62403.

issue.title: [ROCm][Perf] Build the sparse-attn prefill mask once, not per gqa head
issue.body:
_gqa_sparse_fwd_kernel builds its additive attention mask into a
[BLOCK_SIZE_Q, BLOCK_SIZE_H, SUB_K] tensor, but neither term depends on
the gqa head: the causal comparison is over query and key positions, and
the in-range comparison is over key positions alone. The head dimension
therefore holds BLOCK_SIZE_H copies of the same values, and every KV
sub-tile of every selected block pays for them.

Build the sum once in [BLOCK_SIZE_Q, SUB_K] and broadcast it into the
score tensor instead. The terms are only 0 or -inf, so the reassociation
introduces no rounding: adding 0 leaves a float untouched, and adding
-inf yields -inf in either order.

Bit-identical to the current kernel, verified with torch.equal over ten
configurations on gfx950 -- query lengths 512 to 8192, per-rank head
counts 8 / 16 / 64, and prefix_lens of 0, 7, 100, 128 and 4096 to cover
chunked prefill and a query block that does not start on a sparse-block
boundary.

Measured on one MI355X (gfx950, 256 CU), MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 shapes
(head_dim 128, sparse_topk_blocks 16, sparse_block_size 128, bf16), TP=8
per-rank heads, interleaved A/B with alternating order, 300 pairs per
shape, median of per-pair ratios:

  q_len   avg real_topk   base ms   patched ms   speedup
    512             2.5    0.0548       0.0531      3.2%
   1024             4.5    0.0774       0.0730      3.8%
   2048             8.5    0.1268       0.1218      4.6%
   4096            12.2    0.2287       0.2197      3.4%
   8192            14.1    0.4303       0.4168      3.0%
  16384            15.1    0.8711       0.8483      3.1%

The gain peaks near 2048 rather than growing with sequence length: the
inner loop runs min(sparse_topk_blocks, visible blocks) times, so it
saturates at 16 once a query can see that many blocks, while the KV
traffic keeps growing and the kernel becomes bandwidth-bound.

Only the ROCm copy is touched. common/ops/sparse_attn.py carries the same
pattern in both its prefill and decode kernels, but that path was not
measured here.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

comment.body: Closing: the change is correct (bit-identical) but the gain is small. The mask is cheap next to the MFMA QK dot (128 MACs per element at head_dim 128), so removing the per-head copies only speeds the kernel up by 3-5% on MI355X, and end-to-end TTFT is estimated below 1% since MiniMax-M3 prefill is dominated by MoE and projection GEMMs. It only affects one model and cannot be validated end to end on a single GPU.

issue.title: [ROCm][GEMM] Add the TP=2/TP=4 gpt-oss shard shapes to the aiter Triton allowlist
issue.body:
## Summary

Add the TP=2 and TP=4 shard shapes of the gpt-oss qkv / o_proj pair to
`use_aiter_triton_gemm`'s allowlist.

## Why

The list already carries the TP=1 shapes for `hidden_size=2880` models —
`(5120, 2880)` and `(2880, 4096)` — plus some small aux projections and the TP=8
shards. The TP=2 and TP=4 shards of the *same two projections* were simply missing,
so those deployments fall off the aiter Triton GEMM path for their two largest
GEMMs.

| TP | qkv | o_proj |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | (5120, 2880) — present | (2880, 4096) — present |
| 2 | (2560, 2880) — **added** | (2880, 2048) — **added** |
| 4 | (1280, 2880) — **added** | (2880, 1024) — **added** |
| 8 | (640, 2880) — present | (2880, 512) — present |

The shapes are exactly `TP=1 / tp_size`, so this is filling a gap in an existing
series rather than introducing a new claim.

## Verification

**Not benchmarked.** The arithmetic is trivially checkable and the pattern is
self-evident from the surrounding entries. What is *not* established is that the
aiter Triton kernel actually wins at these narrower N — the allowlist exists
because it does not win everywhere, and nobody measured the intermediate TP degrees.
That is the whole risk: adding a shape that loses makes those deployments slower.

Worth benchmarking the four added shapes against the default path before merging.

---

## AI-assistance disclosure (per `AGENTS.md`)

**AI assistance was used.** From an automated kernel-optimization agent run
(hyperloom session `20260803T022733Z`, model `gpt-oss-120b`); applies cleanly to
current `main`. No human review of every line, no tests run — per `AGENTS.md` §1
**not ready for `vllm-project/vllm`**; targets a personal fork.

**Tests run: none.** Outstanding: human review, a GEMM benchmark for the four added
shapes, `pre-commit`, and a `Signed-off-by:` trailer.

**Duplicate check.** No overlapping open PR found for the aiter Triton GEMM shape
list.

comment.body: Closing: the gain is unmeasured and may be negative. The path only runs on gfx950 (it returns early on fp8-fnuz MI300/MI325), and adding these shapes makes AITER Triton take precedence over wvSplitK at 1-5 tokens, the lowest-concurrency decode case. Only gpt-oss (mainly 120b) at TP2/TP4 is affected. A better approach is to benchmark AITER Triton vs. wvSplitK / wvSplitKrc / hipBLASLt on MI355X and derive a size-based rule instead of enumerating shapes.

issue.title: [Core] Make --enable-dbo work at data_parallel_size == 1
issue.body:
## Problem

`--enable-dbo` is a **silent no-op** whenever `data_parallel_size == 1`.

`_determine_batch_execution_and_padding()` initialises `should_ubatch = False` and
only ever assigns it inside `if data_parallel_size > 1`, where the value is
negotiated across DP ranks by an all-reduce. At DP=1 — i.e. pure TP —
`parallel_config.use_ubatching` is True and the `UBatchWrapper` is installed, so
everything *looks* enabled, but `should_ubatch` never becomes True,
`maybe_create_ubatch_slices()` always returns `(None, None)`, and every step runs
as a single batch.

## Why no negotiation is needed at DP=1

Every TP rank runs the identical batch shape and therefore derives the identical
decision from the same inputs. The cross-rank all-reduce exists to reconcile
*different* DP ranks; with one DP rank there is nothing to reconcile.

## Change

Add a local decision path reusing the exact predicates the DP path uses —
`check_ubatch_thresholds()` (already imported) plus the `is_last_ubatch_empty()`
guard, inlined to keep the change import-free.

## Motivation

On MI355X TP=2 with gpt-oss-120b, the four `_C_custom_ar::all_reduce` kernels are
~17.7% of GPU time and TraceLens reports **34.2% exposed** (non-overlapped)
communication. DBO exists to overlap the per-layer TP all-reduce with the sibling
microbatch's compute, and it was unreachable.

## Verification

**Not tested.** The reachability argument is source-level and I am confident in it —
`should_ubatch` really is only assigned under `data_parallel_size > 1`. The
TraceLens percentages come from the originating agent run on MI355X; I have not
reproduced them.

Untested and important: that the two ranks genuinely always agree at DP=1. The DP
path's all-reduce also serves as a *safety* mechanism against ranks diverging; the
argument that TP ranks cannot diverge is reasoning, not a proof, and a divergence
would deadlock rather than degrade. Worth a maintainer's eye specifically on that.

---

## AI-assistance disclosure (per `AGENTS.md`)

**AI assistance was used.** From an automated kernel-optimization agent run
(hyperloom session `20260804T224054Z`, model `gpt-oss-120b`); applies cleanly to
current `main`. No human has reviewed every line or run tests — per `AGENTS.md` §1
**not ready for `vllm-project/vllm`**; targets a personal fork.

**Tests run: none** (no GPU / Python interpreter here). Outstanding: human review,
the DBO test suite, a TP=2 DP=1 run, `pre-commit`, and a `Signed-off-by:` trailer.

**Duplicate check.** No overlapping open PR found for enabling DBO at DP=1.

comment.body: Closing: the premise does not hold. DBO only switches microbatches at the MoE EP all-to-all points (modular_kernel and the deepep_ht / deepep_ll / naive_dp_ep / nixl_ep prepare/finalize paths); there are no yield points around the TP all-reduce. At DP=1 the two microbatches would just run back to back with no overlap, making smaller GEMMs plus switching overhead. Overlapping the TP all-reduce needs DBO yield points on the TP collectives, which is separate and much larger work.
